name: phospholipase C-activating G protein-coupled acetylcholine receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: activation of phospholipase C activity by G-protein coupled acetylcholine receptor signaling pathway|activation of phospholipase C activity by muscarinic acetylcholine receptor signaling pathway|activation of phospholipase C activity by muscarinic acetylcholine receptor signalling pathway|muscarinic acetylcholine receptor|phospholipase C activating pathway|muscarinic receptor signaling pathway via activation of PLC|phospholipase C-activating G-protein coupled acetylcholine receptor signaling pathway
description: A phospholipase C-activating G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by acetylcholine binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phospholipase C-activating serotonin receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: activation of phospholipase C activity by serotonin receptor signaling pathway|activation of phospholipase C activity by serotonin receptor signalling pathway|serotonin receptor|phospholipase C activating pathway
description: A phospholipase C-activating receptor G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by serotonin binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phospholipase C-activating tachykinin receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: activation of phospholipase C activity by tachykinin receptor signaling pathway|activation of phospholipase C activity by tachykinin receptor signalling pathway|tachykinin receptor|phospholipase C activating pathway
description: A phospholipase C-activating receptor G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by tachykinin binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: serotonin receptor signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of a serotonin receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: G protein-coupled dopamine receptor signaling pathway
description: A G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by a dopamine binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: G protein-coupled acetylcholine receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: G-protein coupled acetylcholine receptor signaling pathway|acetylcholine receptor signalling|muscarinic pathway|muscarinic acetylcholine receptor signaling pathway
description: A G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by a ligand binding to an acetylcholine receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ends with regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: gamma-aminobutyric acid signaling pathway
synonyms: 4-aminobutanoate signaling pathway|4-aminobutanoate signalling pathway|4-aminobutyrate signaling pathway|4-aminobutyrate signalling pathway|GABA signaling pathway|GABA signalling pathway|gamma-aminobutyric acid signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals generated by the binding of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA, 4-aminobutyrate), an amino acid which acts as a neurotransmitter in some organisms, to its receptor on the surface of a target cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glutamate receptor signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by the binding of glutamate to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: G protein-coupled glutamate receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: G-protein coupled glutamate receptor signaling pathway|metabotropic glutamate receptor signaling pathway|metabotropic glutamate receptor signalling pathway
description: A G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by glutamate binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tachykinin receptor signaling pathway
description: A G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by tachykinin binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process. Tachykinin is a short peptide with the terminal sequence (Phe-X-Gly-Leu-Met-NH2).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuropeptide signaling pathway
description: A G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by a neuropeptide binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Notch signaling pathway
synonyms: N signaling pathway|N signalling pathway|Notch receptor signaling pathway|Notch receptor signalling pathway|Notch signalling pathway|Notch-receptor signaling pathway|Notch-receptor signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by an extracellular ligand binding to the receptor Notch on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Notch receptor processing
description: The series of successive proteolytic cleavages of the Notch protein, which result in an active form of the receptor.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of transcription of Notch receptor target
synonyms: N receptor target transcription factor activation|Notch receptor target transcription factor activation
description: The activation of transcription of specific genes as a result of Notch signaling, mediated by the Notch intracellular domain.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Wnt signaling pathway, calcium modulating pathway
synonyms: Wnt receptor signaling pathway|calcium modulating pathway|Wnt-activated signaling pathway|calcium modulating pathway|frizzled-2 signaling pathway|frizzled-2 signalling pathway|non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway
description: A type of non-canonical Wnt signaling in which Wnt binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell leads to an increase in intracellular calcium and activation of protein kinase C (PKC).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: smoothened signaling pathway
synonyms: Shh signaling pathway|Sonic hedgehog signaling pathway|hedgehog signaling pathway|hh signaling pathway|hh signalling pathway|smoothened signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of activation of the transmembrane protein Smoothened.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: integrin-mediated signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by an extracellular ligand binding to an integrin on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: osmosensory signaling pathway
synonyms: osmolarity sensing|osmolarity sensing signaling pathway|osmolarity sensing signalling pathway|osmosensory signal transduction|osmosensory signalling pathway|signal transduction during osmotic stress
description: The series of molecular signals initiated in response to osmotic change.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction
synonyms: I-kappaB kinase/NF-kappaB cascade|I-kappaB kinase/NF-kappaB signal transduction|I-kappaB kinase/NF-kappaB signaling|NF-kappaB cascade|canonical NF-kappaB signaling cascade|p50-dependent NF-kappaB signaling
description: An intracellular signaling cassette characterized by the I-kappaB-kinase (IKK)-dependent activation of NF-kappaB, also known as the canonical NF-kappaB signaling cascade. The cascade begins with activation of a trimeric IKK complex (consisting of catalytic kinase subunits IKKalpha and/or IKKbeta, and the regulatory scaffold protein NEMO) and ends with the regulation of transcription of target genes by NF-kappaB. In a resting state, NF-kappaB dimers are bound to I-kappaB proteins, sequestering NF-kappaB in the cytoplasm. Phosphorylation of I-kappaB targets I-kappaB for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, thus releasing the NF-kappaB dimers, which can translocate to the nucleus to bind DNA and regulate transcription. The canonical NF-kappaB pathway is mainly stimulated by proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-1beta, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha, antigen ligands, and toll-like receptors (TLRs).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: activation of NF-kappaB-inducing kinase activity
synonyms: activation of NIK activity|positive regulation of NF-kappaB-inducing kinase activity
description: The stimulation of the activity of NF-kappaB-inducing kinase through phosphorylation at specific residues.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: I-kappaB phosphorylation
synonyms: IKB phosphorylation|IkappaB phosphorylation|inhibitor of NF-kappaB phosphorylation|inhibitor of kappaB phosphorylation
description: The process of introducing a phosphate group into an inhibitor of kappa B (I-kappaB) protein. Phosphorylation of I-kappaB targets I-kappaB for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, thus releasing bound NF-kappaB dimers, which can translocate to the nucleus to bind DNA and regulate transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: JNK cascade
synonyms: JNK1 cascade|JNK2 cascade|JNK3 cascade|MAPK10 cascade|MAPK8 cascade|MAPK9 cascade|SAPK cascade|c-Jun N-terminal kinase cascade|stress-activated protein kinase cascade
description: A MAPK cascade containing at least the JNK (MAPK8) MAP kinase. It starts with the activation of JUN3K (a MAPK3K), which activates JNKK a MAP2K), which in turn activates JNK. The cascade can also contain an additional tier: the upstream MAP4K. The kinases in each tier phosphorylate and activate the kinases in the downstream tier. The JNK cascade is activated by stress signals, as well as by G protein-coupled receptors, growth factors, and cytokines, and results in cellular responses such as cell proliferation, cell differentiation, apoptosis and inflammation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: JUN phosphorylation
description: The process of introducing a phosphate group into a JUN protein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell surface receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT
synonyms: JAK-STAT cascade|JAK-STAT signal transduction|receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT
description: A cell surface receptor signaling pathway in which ligand binding causes the receptor to dimerize, bringing the receptor-associated JAKs into close proximity. The JAKs then phosphorylate and activate each other on tyrosine residues.This leads to the activation of associated STAT protein, causing the STATs to dissociate from the receptor, translocate to the nucleus. The pathway ends with regulation of target gene expression by STAT proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tyrosine phosphorylation of STAT protein
synonyms: tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat1 protein|tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat2 protein|tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat3 protein|tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat4 protein|tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat5 protein|tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat6 protein|tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat7 protein
description: The process of introducing a phosphate group to a tyrosine residue of a STAT (Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription) protein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: small GTPase-mediated signal transduction
synonyms: Ras family protein signal transduction|small GTPase mediated signal transduction
description: An intracellular signaling cassette in which a small monomeric GTPase relays a signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Ras protein signal transduction
description: An intracellular signaling cassette in which a small monomeric GTPase of the Ras subfamily relays a signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Rho protein signal transduction
description: An intracellular signaling cassette in which a small monomeric GTPase of the Rho subfamily relays a signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell-cell signaling
description: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from one cell to another. This process includes signal transduction in the receiving cell and, where applicable, release of a ligand and any processes that actively facilitate its transport and presentation to the receiving cell. Examples include signaling via soluble ligands, via cell adhesion molecules and via gap junctions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: chemical synaptic transmission
synonyms: neurotransmission|signal transmission across a synapse|synaptic transmission
description: The vesicular release of classical neurotransmitter molecules from a presynapse, across a chemical synapse, the subsequent activation of neurotransmitter receptors at the postsynapse of a target cell (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) and the effects of this activation on the postsynaptic membrane potential and ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol. This process encompasses both spontaneous and evoked release of neurotransmitter and all parts of synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Evoked transmission starts with the arrival of an action potential at the presynapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neurotransmitter secretion
description: The regulated release of neurotransmitter from the presynapse into the synaptic cleft via calcium-regulated exocytosis during synaptic transmission.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuron-neuron synaptic transmission
description: The process of synaptic transmission from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic transmission, cholinergic
description: The vesicular release of acetylcholine from a presynapse, across a chemical synapse, the subsequent activation of dopamine receptors at the postsynapse of a target cell (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) and the effects of this activation on the postsynaptic membrane potential and ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol. This process encompasses both spontaneous and evoked release of neurotransmitter and all parts of synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Evoked transmission starts with the arrival of an action potential at the presynapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuromuscular synaptic transmission
description: The process of synaptic transmission from a neuron to a muscle, across a synapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: multicellular organism development
description: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a multicellular organism over time from an initial condition (e.g. a zygote or a young adult) to a later condition (e.g. a multicellular animal or an aged adult).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: gamete generation
description: The generation and maintenance of gametes in a multicellular organism. A gamete is a haploid reproductive cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: germ cell development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an immature germ cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure (gamete). A germ cell is any reproductive cell in a multicellular organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: spermatogenesis
description: The developmental process by which male germ line stem cells self renew or give rise to successive cell types resulting in the development of a spermatozoa.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: spermatogonial cell division
description: The mitotic divisions of the primary spermatogonial cell (a primordial male germ cell) to form secondary spermatogonia (primary spermatocytes).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: spermatid development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a spermatid over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sperm axoneme assembly
description: The assembly and organization of the sperm flagellar axoneme, the bundle of microtubules and associated proteins that forms the core of the eukaryotic sperm flagellum, and is responsible for movement.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: spermatid nucleus differentiation
description: The specialization of the spermatid nucleus during the development of a spermatid into a mature male gamete competent for fertilization.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: female gamete generation
description: Generation of the female gamete; specialised haploid cells produced by meiosis and along with a male gamete takes part in sexual reproduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: insemination
description: The introduction of semen or sperm into the genital tract of a female.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sperm displacement
description: The physical displacement of sperm stored from previous mating encounters.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: peptide pheromone maturation
description: The generation of a mature, active peptide pheromone via processes unique to its processing and modification. An example of this process is found in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: single fertilization
description: The union of male and female gametes to form a zygote.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: binding of sperm to zona pellucida
description: The process in which the sperm binds to the zona pellucida glycoprotein layer of the egg. The process begins with the attachment of the sperm plasma membrane to the zona pellucida and includes attachment of the acrosome inner membrane to the zona pellucida after the acrosomal reaction takes place.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: acrosome reaction
description: The discharge, by sperm, of a single, anterior secretory granule following the sperm's attachment to the zona pellucida of the oocyte. The process begins with the fusion of the outer acrosomal membrane with the sperm plasma membrane and ends with the exocytosis of the acrosomal contents into the zona pellucida.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: penetration of zona pellucida
description: The infiltration by sperm of the zona pellucida to reach the oocyte. The process involves digestive enzymes from a modified lysosome called the acrosome, situated at the head of the sperm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fusion of sperm to egg plasma membrane involved in single fertilization
description: The binding and fusion of a sperm, with the plasma membrane of the oocyte as part of the process of single fertilization. In sperm with flagella, binding occurs at the posterior (post-acrosomal) region of the sperm head.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pronuclear fusion
description: The merging of two pronuclei in a fertilized egg to fuse and produce a single zygotic genome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of mitotic cell cycle
synonyms: mitotic cell cycle modulation|mitotic cell cycle regulation|mitotic cell cycle regulator|modulation of mitotic cell cycle progression|regulation of mitotic cell cycle progression|regulation of progression through mitotic cell cycle
description: Any process that modulates the rate or extent of progress through the mitotic cell cycle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: zygotic specification of dorsal/ventral axis
synonyms: zygotic determination of dorsal-ventral axis|zygotic determination of dorsal/ventral axis|zygotic determination of dorsoventral axis
description: The specification of the dorsal/ventral axis of the embryo, through the products of genes expressed in the zygote.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: thorax and anterior abdomen determination
description: Specification of the central (trunk) regions of the embryo by the gap genes; exemplified in insects by the actions of the Kruppel gene product.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: determination of left/right symmetry
description: The establishment of an organism's body plan or part of an organism with respect to the left and right halves. The pattern can either be symmetric, such that the halves are mirror images, or asymmetric where the pattern deviates from this symmetry.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: gastrulation
description: A complex and coordinated series of cellular movements that occurs at the end of cleavage during embryonic development of most animals. The details of gastrulation vary from species to species, but usually result in the formation of the three primary germ layers, ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ventral midline determination
synonyms: determination of anterior border of ventral midline|determination of posterior border of ventral midline
description: The regionalization process in which the area where the ventral midline will form is specified.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: segment specification
description: The process in which segments assume individual identities; exemplified in insects by the actions of the products of the homeotic genes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anterior compartment pattern formation
description: The process giving rise to specification of cell identity in the anterior compartments of the segmented embryo.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: posterior compartment specification
description: The process involved in the specification of cell identity in the posterior compartments of the segmented embryo.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pattern specification process
description: Any developmental process that results in the creation of defined areas or spaces within an organism to which cells respond and eventually are instructed to differentiate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ectoderm development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the ectoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure. In animal embryos, the ectoderm is the outer germ layer of the embryo, formed during gastrulation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nervous system development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of nervous tissue over time, from its formation to its mature state.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuroblast proliferation
description: The expansion of a neuroblast population by cell division. A neuroblast is any cell that will divide and give rise to a neuron.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of neuroblast proliferation
synonyms: down regulation of neuroblast proliferation|down-regulation of neuroblast proliferation|downregulation of neuroblast proliferation|inhibition of neuroblast proliferation|suppression of neuroblast proliferation
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the proliferation of neuroblasts.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: axonogenesis
synonyms: axon growth|axon morphogenesis|neuron long process generation
description: De novo generation of a long process of a neuron, including the terminal branched region. Refers to the morphogenesis or creation of shape or form of the developing axon, which carries efferent (outgoing) action potentials from the cell body towards target cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: axon guidance
synonyms: axon chemotaxis|axon growth cone guidance|axon pathfinding
description: The chemotaxis process that directs the migration of an axon growth cone to a specific target site in response to a combination of attractive and repulsive cues.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: axon target recognition
description: The process in which an axon recognizes and binds to a set of cells with which it may form stable connections.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: axonal fasciculation
description: The collection of axons into a bundle of rods, known as a fascicle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synapse assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a synapse. This process ends when the synapse is mature (functional).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: central nervous system development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the central nervous system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The central nervous system is the core nervous system that serves an integrating and coordinating function. In vertebrates it consists of the brain and spinal cord. In those invertebrates with a central nervous system it typically consists of a brain, cerebral ganglia and a nerve cord.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ventral midline development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the ventral midline over time, from its formation to the mature structure. In protostomes (such as insects, snails and worms) as well as deuterostomes (vertebrates), the midline is an embryonic region that functions in patterning of the adjacent nervous tissue. The ventral midline in insects is a cell population extending along the ventral surface of the embryo and is the region from which cells detach to form the ventrally located nerve cords. In vertebrates, the midline is originally located dorsally. During development, it folds inwards and becomes the ventral part of the dorsally located neural tube and is then called the ventral midline, or floor plate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: brain development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the brain over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Brain development begins with patterning events in the neural tube and ends with the mature structure that is the center of thought and emotion. The brain is responsible for the coordination and control of bodily activities and the interpretation of information from the senses (sight, hearing, smell, etc.).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: peripheral nervous system development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the peripheral nervous system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The peripheral nervous system is one of the two major divisions of the nervous system. Nerves in the PNS connect the central nervous system (CNS) with sensory organs, other organs, muscles, blood vessels and glands.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sensory organ development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of sensory organs over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: salivary gland development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the salivary gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Salivary glands include any of the saliva-secreting exocrine glands of the oral cavity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: salivary gland morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of the salivary gland are generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hindgut morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of the hindgut are generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endoderm development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the endoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The endoderm is the innermost germ layer that develops into the gastrointestinal tract, the lungs and associated tissues.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: midgut development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the midgut over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The midgut is the middle part of the alimentary canal from the stomach, or entrance of the bile duct, to, or including, the large intestine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: visceral mesoderm-endoderm interaction involved in midgut development
description: The process of cell-cell signaling between visceral mesoderm cells and endoderm cells that is involved in the differentiation of cells in the midgut.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: posterior midgut development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the posterior midgut over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mesoderm development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesoderm is the middle germ layer that develops into muscle, bone, cartilage, blood and connective tissue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mesodermal cell fate determination
description: The cell fate determination process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a mesoderm cell regardless of its environment; upon determination, the cell fate cannot be reversed.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mesodermal cell fate specification
description: The cell fate determination process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a mesoderm cell in an environment that is neutral with respect to the developmental pathway; upon specification, the cell fate can be reversed.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: heart development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the heart over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The heart is a hollow, muscular organ, which, by contracting rhythmically, keeps up the circulation of the blood.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mesoderm migration involved in gastrulation
description: The migration of mesodermal cells during gastrulation to help establish the multilayered body plan of the organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: adult heart development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the adult heart over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: muscle organ development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The muscle is an organ consisting of a tissue made up of various elongated cells that are specialized to contract and thus to produce movement and mechanical work.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myoblast fate determination
description: The cell fate determination process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a myoblast regardless of its environment; upon determination, the cell fate cannot be reversed. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skeletal muscle tissue development
description: The developmental sequence of events leading to the formation of adult skeletal muscle tissue. The main events are: the fusion of myoblasts to form myotubes that increase in size by further fusion to them of myoblasts, the formation of myofibrils within their cytoplasm and the establishment of functional neuromuscular junctions with motor neurons. At this stage they can be regarded as mature muscle fibers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myoblast fusion
description: A process in which non-proliferating myoblasts fuse to existing fibers or to myotubes to form new fibers. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: muscle cell fate determination
description: The cell fate determination process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a muscle cell regardless of its environment; upon determination, the cell fate cannot be reversed.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: visceral muscle development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the visceral muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: somatic muscle development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the somatic muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Somatic muscles are striated muscle structures that connect to the exoskeleton or cuticle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuromuscular junction development
synonyms: NMJ stability|neuromuscular junction organization|neuromuscular junction stability
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a neuromuscular junction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment of synaptic specificity at neuromuscular junction
description: The biological process in which a synapse between a motor neuron and a muscle is initially formed.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sex determination
description: Any process that establishes and transmits the specification of sexual status of an individual organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: primary sex determination
description: The sex determination process that results in the initial specification of sexual status of an individual organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sex differentiation
description: The establishment of the sex of an organism by physical differentiation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: female pregnancy
description: The set of physiological processes that allow an embryo or foetus to develop within the body of a female animal. It covers the time from fertilization of a female ovum by a male spermatozoon until birth.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryo implantation
description: Attachment of the blastocyst to the uterine lining.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: parturition
description: The reproductive process in which the parent is separated from its offspring either by giving birth to live young or by laying eggs.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to nutrient
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nutrient stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: respiratory gaseous exchange by respiratory system
description: The process of gaseous exchange between an organism and its environment. In plants, microorganisms, and many small animals, air or water makes direct contact with the organism's cells or tissue fluids, and the processes of diffusion supply the organism with dioxygen (O2) and remove carbon dioxide (CO2). In larger animals the efficiency of gaseous exchange is improved by specialized respiratory organs, such as lungs and gills, which are ventilated by breathing mechanisms.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: digestion
description: The whole of the physical, chemical, and biochemical processes carried out by multicellular organisms to break down ingested nutrients into components that may be easily absorbed and directed into metabolism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: body fluid secretion
description: The controlled release of a fluid by a cell or tissue in an animal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lactation
description: The regulated release of milk from the mammary glands and the period of time that a mother lactates to feed her young.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: blood coagulation
description: The sequential process in which the multiple coagulation factors of the blood interact, ultimately resulting in the formation of an insoluble fibrin clot; it may be divided into three stages: stage 1, the formation of intrinsic and extrinsic prothrombin converting principle; stage 2, the formation of thrombin; stage 3, the formation of stable fibrin polymers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: blood coagulation, intrinsic pathway
synonyms: initiation of blood coagulation cascade|contact activation system|initiation of blood coagulation cascade|contact pathway
description: A protein activation cascade that initiates blood coagulation, triggered when Factor XII, prekallikrein (PK) and high-molecular-weight kininogen  (HK) assemble on a suitable surface or polymer. This results in the reciprocal activation of factor XII to Factor XIIa by kallikrein, and PK to kallikrein by Factor XIIa. The resulting generation of Factor XIIa activates Factor XI to Factor XIa, which then converts Factor IX to Factor IXa. Factor IXa converts Factor X to Xa. Factor Xa then initiates the common pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: blood coagulation, extrinsic pathway
synonyms: initiation of blood coagulation cascade|tissue factor pathway
description: A protein activation cascade that initiates blood coagulation, starting with a signal from tissue factor (TF), a cell-surface, integral-membrane protein, which converts Factor IX to IXa, and Factor IXa converts Factor X to Xa. Factor Xa then initiates the common pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hemostasis
description: The stopping of bleeding (loss of body fluid) or the arrest of the circulation to an organ or part.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sensory perception
description: The series of events required for an organism to receive a sensory stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: visual perception
description: The series of events required for an organism to receive a visual stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Visual stimuli are detected in the form of photons and are processed to form an image.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phototransduction
description: The sequence of reactions within a cell required to convert absorbed photons into a molecular signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phototransduction, visible light
description: The sequence of reactions within a cell required to convert absorbed photons from visible light into a molecular signal. A visible light stimulus is electromagnetic radiation that can be perceived visually by an organism; for organisms lacking a visual system, this can be defined as light with a wavelength within the range 380 to 780 nm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phototransduction, UV
synonyms: UV-sensitive opsin|phototransduction|UV light|phototransduction|UV radiation|phototransduction|ultraviolet light|phototransduction|ultraviolet radiation
description: The sequence of reactions within a cell required to convert absorbed photons from UV light into a molecular signal; ultraviolet radiation is electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength in the range of 10 to 400 nanometers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sensory perception of sound
description: The series of events required for an organism to receive an auditory stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Sonic stimuli are detected in the form of vibrations and are processed to form a sound.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sensory perception of chemical stimulus
description: The series of events required for an organism to receive a sensory chemical stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sensory perception of smell
description: The series of events required for an organism to receive an olfactory stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Olfaction involves the detection of chemical composition of an organism's ambient medium by chemoreceptors. This is a neurological process.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: learning or memory
description: The acquisition and processing of information and/or the storage and retrieval of this information over time.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: learning
description: Any process in an organism in which a relatively long-lasting adaptive behavioral change occurs as the result of experience.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: memory
description: The activities involved in the mental information processing system that receives (registers), modifies, stores, and retrieves informational stimuli. The main stages involved in the formation and retrieval of memory are encoding (processing of received information by acquisition), storage (building a permanent record of received information as a result of consolidation) and retrieval (calling back the stored information and use it in a suitable way to execute a given task).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: short-term memory
description: The memory process that deals with the storage, retrieval and modification of information received a short time (up to about 30 minutes) ago. This type of memory is typically dependent on direct, transient effects of second messenger activation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: long-term memory
description: The memory process that deals with the storage, retrieval and modification of information a long time (typically weeks, months or years) after receiving that information. This type of memory is typically dependent on gene transcription regulated by second messenger activation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mating behavior
description: The behavioral interactions between organisms for the purpose of mating, or sexual reproduction resulting in the formation of zygotes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: copulation
description: The act of sexual union between male and female, involving the transfer of sperm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of female receptivity
synonyms: down regulation of female receptivity|down-regulation of female receptivity|downregulation of female receptivity|inhibition of female receptivity
description: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the receptiveness of a female to male advances.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: rhythmic behavior
synonyms: rhythmic behavioral response to stimulus|rhythmic behaviour|rhythmic behavioural response to stimulus
description: The specific behavior of an organism that recur with measured regularity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: circadian rhythm
synonyms: circadian process|circadian response|response to circadian rhythm
description: Any biological process in an organism that recurs with a regularity of approximately 24 hours.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ultradian rhythm
description: The specific actions or reactions of an organism that recur with a regularity more frequent than every 24 hours.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: grooming behavior
description: The specific behavior of an organism relating to grooming, cleaning and brushing to remove dirt and parasites.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: locomotory behavior
synonyms: behavior via locomotion|locomotion in response to stimulus|locomotory behavioral response to stimulus|locomotory behaviour|locomotory behavioural response to stimulus
description: The specific movement from place to place of an organism in response to external or internal stimuli. Locomotion of a whole organism in a manner dependent upon some combination of that organism's internal state and external conditions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: adult walking behavior
description: The behavior of an adult relating to the progression of that organism along the ground by the process of lifting and setting down each leg.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: feeding behavior
synonyms: behavioral response to food|behavioural response to food|eating|feeding behaviour|feeding from phloem of other organism|feeding from plant phloem|feeding from tissue of other organism|feeding from vascular tissue of another organism|feeding from xylem of other organism|feeding on or from other organism|feeding on plant sap
description: Behavior associated with the intake of food.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: visual behavior
synonyms: behavioral response to visual stimulus|behavioural response to visual stimulus|visual behaviour
description: The behavior of an organism in response to a visual stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: optokinetic behavior
description: The behavior of an organism pertaining to movement of the eyes and of objects in the visual field, as in nystagmus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: chemosensory behavior
synonyms: behavioral response to chemical stimulus|behavioural response to chemical stimulus|chemosensory behaviour
description: Behavior that is dependent upon the sensation of chemicals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: blood circulation
description: The flow of blood through the body of an animal, enabling the transport of nutrients to the tissues and the removal of waste products.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of heart contraction
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of heart contraction. Heart contraction is the process in which the heart decreases in volume in a characteristic way to propel blood through the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tRNA processing
description: The process in which a pre-tRNA molecule is converted to a mature tRNA, ready for addition of an aminoacyl group.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell recognition
description: The process in which a cell in an organism interprets its surroundings.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuron recognition
description: The process in which a neuronal cell in a multicellular organism interprets its surroundings.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic target recognition
description: The process in which a neuronal cell in a multicellular organism interprets signals produced by potential target cells, with which it may form synapses.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: motor neuron axon guidance
synonyms: motoneuron axon guidance|motor axon guidance|motor axon pathfinding
description: The process in which the migration of an axon growth cone of a motor neuron is directed to a specific target site in response to a combination of attractive and repulsive cues.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial fusion
description: Merging of two or more mitochondria within a cell to form a single compartment.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: eye pigment granule organization
synonyms: eye pigment granule organisation|eye pigment granule organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of intracellular pigment storage granules in the eye.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Toll signaling pathway
synonyms: Tl signaling pathway|Tl signalling pathway|Toll signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by an extracellular ligand binding to the receptor Toll on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of actin polymerization or depolymerization
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the assembly or disassembly of actin filaments by the addition or removal of actin monomers from a filament.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment of blood-nerve barrier
description: The establishment of the barrier between the perineurium of peripheral nerves and the vascular endothelium of endoneurial capillaries. The perineurium acts as a diffusion barrier, but ion permeability at the blood-nerve barrier is still higher than at the blood-brain barrier.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: axo-dendritic transport
description: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules in neuron projections.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anterograde axonal transport
description: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules from the cell body toward the cell periphery in nerve cell axons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retrograde axonal transport
description: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules from the cell periphery toward the cell body in nerve cell axons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intracellular protein localization
synonyms: asymmetric protein localisation|asymmetric protein localization|cellular protein localisation|cellular protein localization|channel localizer activity|establishment and maintenance of asymmetric protein localization|establishment and maintenance of protein localization|protein localisation|protein localization
description: Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: actin polymerization or depolymerization
description: Assembly or disassembly of actin filaments by the addition or removal of actin monomers from a filament.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of DNA replication
synonyms: DNA replication inhibitor|down regulation of DNA replication|down-regulation of DNA replication|downregulation of DNA replication|inhibition of DNA replication
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of DNA replication.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: steroid metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving steroids, compounds with a 1,2,cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cholesterol metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving cholesterol, cholest-5-en-3 beta-ol, the principal sterol of vertebrates and the precursor of many steroids, including bile acids and steroid hormones. It is a component of the plasma membrane lipid bilayer and of plasma lipoproteins and can be found in all animal tissues.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bile acid metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving bile acids, a group of steroid carboxylic acids occurring in bile, where they are present as the sodium salts of their amides with glycine or taurine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: C21-steroid hormone metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving C21-steroid hormones, steroid compounds containing 21 carbons which function as hormones.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: androgen metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving androgens, C19 steroid hormones that can stimulate the development of male sexual characteristics.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: estrogen metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving estrogens, C18 steroid hormones that can stimulate the development of female sexual characteristics. Also found in plants.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glucocorticoid metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving glucocorticoids, hormonal C21 corticosteroids synthesized from cholesterol. Glucocorticoids act primarily on carbohydrate and protein metabolism, and have anti-inflammatory effects.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: spermine metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving spermine, a polybasic amine found in human sperm, in ribosomes and in some viruses, which is involved in nucleic acid packaging. Synthesis is regulated by ornithine decarboxylase which plays a key role in control of DNA replication.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of blood pressure
synonyms: blood pressure homeostasis|blood pressure regulation|control of blood pressure
description: Any process that modulates the force with which blood travels through the circulatory system. The process is controlled by a balance of processes that increase pressure and decrease pressure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell death
description: Any biological process that results in permanent cessation of all vital functions of a cell. A cell should be considered dead when any one of the following molecular or morphological criteria is met: (1) the cell has lost the integrity of its plasma membrane; (2) the cell, including its nucleus, has undergone complete fragmentation into discrete bodies (frequently referred to as apoptotic bodies). The cell corpse (or its fragments) may be engulfed by an adjacent cell in vivo, but engulfment of whole cells should not be considered a strict criteria to define cell death as, under some circumstances, live engulfed cells can be released from phagosomes (see PMID:18045538).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: opsonization
description: The process in which a microorganism (or other particulate material) is rendered more susceptible to phagocytosis by coating with an opsonin, a blood serum protein such as a complement component or antibody.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of G protein coupled receptor protein signaling pathway|regulation of G protein coupled receptor protein signalling pathway|regulation of G-protein coupled receptor protein signaling pathway|regulation of G-protein coupled receptor protein signalling pathway|regulation of G-protein-coupled receptor protein signalling pathway|regulation of GPCR protein signaling pathway|regulation of GPCR protein signalling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell population proliferation
description: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of cell population proliferation
synonyms: activation of cell proliferation|positive regulation of cell proliferation|stimulation of cell proliferation|up regulation of cell proliferation|up-regulation of cell proliferation|upregulation of cell proliferation
description: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cell population proliferation
synonyms: down regulation of cell proliferation|down-regulation of cell proliferation|downregulation of cell proliferation|inhibition of cell proliferation|negative regulation of cell proliferation
description: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the rate or extent of cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: insulin receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: daf-2 receptor signaling pathway|insulin receptor signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of the insulin receptor binding to insulin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: acetylcholine biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of acetylcholine, the acetic acid ester of the organic base choline.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: spermidine biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of spermidine, N-(3-aminopropyl)-1,4-diaminobutane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intracellular mRNA localization
synonyms: establishment and maintenance of intracellular RNA localization|intracellular mRNA localisation|intracellular mRNA positioning|mRNA localization|intracellular|mRNA positioning|intracellular
description: Any process in which mRNA is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location within the cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: isoprenoid biosynthetic process
synonyms: isoprenoid anabolism|isoprenoid biosynthesis|isoprenoid formation|isoprenoid synthesis|polyisoprenoid anabolism|polyisoprenoid biosynthesis|polyisoprenoid biosynthetic process|polyisoprenoid formation|polyisoprenoid synthesis|polyterpene biosynthesis|polyterpene biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of an isoprenoid compound, isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene) or compounds containing or derived from linked isoprene (3-methyl-2-butenylene) residues.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: associative learning
description: Learning by associating a stimulus (the cause) with a particular outcome (the effect).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: G2/MI transition of meiotic cell cycle
synonyms: meiotic G2/MI phase transition|meiotic G2/MI transition|meiotic cell cycle G2/MI phase transition
description: The cell cycle process in which a cell progresses from meiotic G2 phase to M phase of meiosis I.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endosome to lysosome transport
description: The directed movement of substances from endosomes to lysosomes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: histone mRNA metabolic process
synonyms: histone mRNA metabolism|stem-loop-containing histone mRNA 3\'-end processing
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving an mRNA encoding a histone.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: determination of adult lifespan
description: The pathways that regulate the duration of the adult phase of the life-cycle of an animal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: adult feeding behavior
description: Feeding behavior in a fully developed and mature organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: adult locomotory behavior
description: Locomotory behavior in a fully developed and mature organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glial cell migration
description: The orderly movement of a glial cell, non-neuronal cells that provide support and nutrition, maintain homeostasis, form myelin, and participate in signal transmission in the nervous system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: primordial germ cell migration
synonyms: embryonic germ cell migration|germ cell migration|germ-cell migration|pole cell migration
description: The orderly movement of a cell specialized to produce haploid gametes through the embryo from its site of production to the place where the gonads will form.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: olfactory learning
description: Any process in an organism in which a relatively long-lasting adaptive behavioral change occurs in response to (repeated) exposure to an olfactory cue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: asymmetric cell division
description: The asymmetric division of cells to produce two daughter cells with different developmental potentials. It is of fundamental significance for the generation of cell diversity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cell shape
description: Any process that modulates the surface configuration of a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cell size
description: Any process that modulates the size of a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: axon ensheathment
synonyms: cellular axon ensheathment|cellular nerve ensheathment|nerve ensheathment
description: Any process in which the axon of a neuron is insulated, and that insulation maintained, thereby preventing dispersion of the electrical signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: RNA splicing
description: The process of removing sections of the primary RNA transcript to remove sequences not present in the mature form of the RNA and joining the remaining sections to form the mature form of the RNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: gonad development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the gonad over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The gonad is an animal organ that produces gametes; in some species it also produces hormones.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: respiratory chain complex IV assembly
synonyms: cytochrome c oxidase biogenesis|cytochrome c oxidase complex assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form respiratory chain complex IV (also known as cytochrome c oxidase), the terminal member of the respiratory chain of the mitochondrion and some aerobic bacteria. Cytochrome c oxidases are multi-subunit enzymes containing from 13 subunits in the mammalian mitochondrial form to 3-4 subunits in the bacterial forms.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: visual learning
description: Any process in an organism in which a change in behavior of an individual occurs in response to repeated exposure to a visual cue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fibroblast growth factor receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: FGF receptor signaling pathway|FGF receptor signalling pathway|FGFR signaling pathway|fibroblast growth factor receptor signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of a fibroblast growth factor receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: epidermis development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the epidermis over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The epidermis is the outer epithelial layer of an animal, it may be a single layer that produces an extracellular material (e.g. the cuticle of arthropods) or a complex stratified squamous epithelium, as in the case of many vertebrate species.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of synaptic assembly at neuromuscular junction
synonyms: regulation of synaptic growth at neuromuscular junction
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of synaptic assembly at neuromuscular junctions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: male gonad development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the male gonad over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: female gonad development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the female gonad over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of smoothened signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of hedgehog signaling pathway|regulation of hh signaling pathway|regulation of smoothened activity|regulation of smoothened by patched|regulation of smoothened receptor activity by patched|regulation of smoothened signalling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of smoothened signaling.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of Toll signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of Tl signaling pathway|regulation of Tl signalling pathway|regulation of Toll signalling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the Tl signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of Notch signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of N signaling pathway|regulation of N signalling pathway|regulation of Notch signalling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the Notch signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: photoreceptor cell morphogenesis
description: The process in which the structures of a photoreceptor cell are generated and organized. This process occurs while the initially relatively unspecialized cell is acquiring the specialized features of a photoreceptor cell, a sensory cell that reacts to the presence of light. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anterior/posterior axis specification, embryo
description: The specification of the anterior/posterior axis of the embryo by the products of genes expressed maternally and genes expressed in the zygote.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: attachment of spindle microtubules to kinetochore
synonyms: amphotelic attachment|attachment of spindle microtubules to chromosome|bipolar attachment|kinetochore microtubule interaction|kinetochore-microtubule attachment|kinetochore-microtubule interaction|microtubule anchoring at kinetochore|microtubule and chromosome interaction|microtubule and kinetochore interaction|microtubule capture|spindle chromosome attachment|spindle kinetochore attachment|spindle-chromosome interaction
description: The process in which spindle microtubules become physically associated with the proteins making up the kinetochore complex.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipid biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lipids, compounds soluble in an organic solvent but not, or sparingly, in an aqueous solvent.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ether lipid biosynthetic process
synonyms: ether lipid anabolism|ether lipid biosynthesis|ether lipid formation|ether lipid synthesis|plasmalogen biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of ether lipids, lipids that contain (normally) one lipid alcohol in ether linkage to one of the carbon atoms (normally C-1) of glycerol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pyridoxine biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of pyridoxine, 2-methyl-3-hydroxy-4,5-bis(hydroxymethyl)pyridine, one of the vitamin B6 compounds.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: guanosine metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving guanine, guanine riboside, a nucleoside with a wide species distribution.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway via death domain receptors
synonyms: death receptor-mediated apoptosis|induction of apoptosis via death domain receptors|induction of apoptosis via death receptors
description: The series of molecular signals in which a signal is conveyed from the cell surface to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway starts with a ligand binding to a death domain receptor on the cell surface, and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: granzyme-mediated apoptotic signaling pathway
synonyms: apoptotic signaling pathway in response to granzyme|induction of apoptosis by granzyme
description: The series of molecular signals induced by granzymes which triggers the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway starts with reception of a granzyme signal, and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered. Granzymes are serine proteases that are secreted by cytotoxic T cells and natural killer cells to induce apoptosis in target cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to osmotic stress
synonyms: induction of apoptosis by ionic changes
description: The series of molecular signals in which an intracellular signal is conveyed to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway is induced in response to changes in intracellular ion homeostasis, and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hormone-mediated apoptotic signaling pathway
synonyms: apoptotic signaling pathway in response to hormone|induction of apoptosis by hormones
description: The series of molecular signals mediated by the detection of a hormone, and which triggers the apoptotic signaling pathway in a cell. The pathway starts with reception of a hormone signal, and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to DNA damage
synonyms: DNA damage response|signal transduction resulting in induction of apoptosis
description: The series of molecular signals in which an intracellular signal is conveyed to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway is induced by the detection of DNA damage, and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to oxidative stress
synonyms: induction of apoptosis by oxidative stress|oxidative stress-induced intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals in which an intracellular signal is conveyed to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway is induced in response to oxidative stress, a state often resulting from exposure to high levels of reactive oxygen species, and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: apoptotic mitochondrial changes
description: The morphological and physiological alterations undergone by mitochondria during apoptosis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: carbohydrate transport
description: The directed movement of carbohydrate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Carbohydrates are a group of organic compounds based of the general formula Cx(H2O)y.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hexose transmembrane transport
synonyms: hexose membrane transport|hexose transport|high-affinity hexose transport|low-affinity hexose transport
description: The process in which hexose is transported across a membrane. Hexoses are aldoses with a chain of six carbon atoms in the molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: amino acid biosynthetic process
synonyms: amino acid anabolism|amino acid biosynthesis|amino acid formation|amino acid synthesis|cellular amino acid biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids, organic acids containing one or more amino substituents.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phospholipid biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a phospholipid, a lipid containing phosphoric acid as a mono- or diester.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pyrimidine-containing compound salvage
description: Any process that generates a pyrimidine-containing compound, a nucleobase, nucleoside, nucleotide or nucleic acid that contains a pyrimidine base, from derivatives of them without de novo synthesis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dosage compensation by inactivation of X chromosome
synonyms: Barr body formation|X chromosome inactivation|chromosome inactivation
description: Compensating for the two-fold variation in X-chromosome:autosome ratios between sexes by heterochromatin formation leading to a global inactivation of all, or most of, the genes on one of the X-chromosomes in the XX sex.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pentose-phosphate shunt, oxidative branch
synonyms: oxidative branch|pentose pathway|oxidative pentose phosphate pathway|pentose phosphate pathway|oxidative branch|pentose phosphate shunt|oxidative branch|pentose-phosphate pathway|oxidative branch
description: The branch of the pentose-phosphate shunt which involves the oxidation of glucose 6-P and produces ribulose 5-P, reduced NADP+ and carbon dioxide (CO2).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pentose-phosphate shunt, non-oxidative branch
synonyms: pentose phosphate pathway|non-oxidative branch|pentose phosphate shunt|non-oxidative branch|pentose-phosphate pathway|non-oxidative branch
description: The branch of the pentose-phosphate shunt which does not involve oxidation reactions. It comprises a series of sugar phosphate interconversions, starting with ribulose 5-P and producing fructose 6-P and glyceraldehyde 3-P.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: aerobic respiration
description: The enzymatic release of energy from inorganic and organic compounds (especially carbohydrates and fats) which requires oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fatty acid catabolic process
synonyms: fatty acid breakdown|fatty acid catabolism|fatty acid degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a fatty acid, any of the aliphatic monocarboxylic acids that can be liberated by hydrolysis from naturally occurring fats and oils. Fatty acids are predominantly straight-chain acids of 4 to 24 carbon atoms, which may be saturated or unsaturated; branched fatty acids and hydroxy fatty acids also occur, and very long chain acids of over 30 carbons are found in waxes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: amino acid catabolic process
synonyms: amino acid breakdown|amino acid catabolism|amino acid degradation|cellular amino acid catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids, organic acids containing one or more amino substituents.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: aromatic amino acid metabolic process
synonyms: aromatic amino acid family metabolic process|aromatic amino acid family metabolism
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving aromatic amino acid family, amino acids with aromatic ring (phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: aromatic amino acid catabolic process
synonyms: aromatic amino acid family breakdown|aromatic amino acid family catabolism|aromatic amino acid family degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of an amino acid whose structure includes an aromatic ring.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: branched-chain amino acid metabolic process
synonyms: branched chain family amino acid metabolism
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids containing a branched carbon skeleton, comprising isoleucine, leucine and valine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: branched-chain amino acid biosynthetic process
synonyms: branched chain family amino acid anabolism|branched chain family amino acid biosynthesis|branched chain family amino acid biosynthetic process|branched chain family amino acid formation|branched chain family amino acid synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids containing a branched carbon skeleton, comprising isoleucine, leucine and valine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: branched-chain amino acid catabolic process
synonyms: branched chain family amino acid breakdown|branched chain family amino acid catabolic process|branched chain family amino acid catabolism|branched chain family amino acid degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids containing a branched carbon skeleton, comprising isoleucine, leucine and valine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-methionine catabolic process
synonyms: L-methionine catabolic process via Ehrlich pathway|L-methionine degradation via Ehrlich pathway|methionine breakdown|methionine catabolism|methionine degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of L-methionine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glycoprotein metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving glycoproteins, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glycoprotein biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glycoproteins, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipopolysaccharide catabolic process
synonyms: LPS catabolic process|lipopolysaccharide breakdown|lipopolysaccharide catabolism|lipopolysaccharide degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of lipopolysaccharides, any of a group of related, structurally complex components of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipoate biosynthetic process
synonyms: lipoate anabolism|lipoate biosynthesis|lipoate formation|lipoate synthesis|lipoic acid anabolism|lipoic acid biosynthesis|lipoic acid biosynthetic process|lipoic acid formation|lipoic acid synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lipoate, 1,2-dithiolane-3-pentanoate, the anion derived from lipoic acid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: purine nucleobase biosynthetic process
synonyms: purine base anabolism|purine base biosynthesis|purine base biosynthetic process|purine base formation|purine base synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of purine nucleobases, one of the two classes of nitrogen-containing ring compounds found in DNA and RNA, which include adenine and guanine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hypoxanthine catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of hypoxanthine, 6-hydroxy purine, an intermediate in the degradation of adenylate. Its ribonucleoside is known as inosine and its ribonucleotide as inosinate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: xanthine catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of xanthine, 2,6-dihydroxypurine, a purine formed in the metabolic breakdown of guanine but not present in nucleic acids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nucleoside metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleoside, a nucleobase linked to either beta-D-ribofuranose (a ribonucleoside) or 2-deoxy-beta-D-ribofuranose, (a deoxyribonucleoside), e.g. adenosine, guanosine, inosine, cytidine, uridine and deoxyadenosine, deoxyguanosine, deoxycytidine and thymidine (= deoxythymidine).

label: BiologicalProcess

label: BiologicalProcess
name: translational attenuation
description: Translational attenuation is a regulatory mechanism analogous to ribosome-mediated transcriptional attenuation. The system requires the presence of a short ORF, called a leader peptide, encoded in the mRNA upstream of the ribosome-binding site and start codon of the gene whose translation is to be regulated. Certain conditions, such as presence of the antibiotic tetracycline in bacteria or amino acid starvation, may cause slowing or stalling of the ribosome translating the leader peptide. The stalled ribosome masks a region of the mRNA and affects which of two alternative mRNA folded structures will form, therefore controlling whether or not a ribosome will bind and initiate translation of the downstream gene. Translational attenuation is analogous to ribosome-mediated transcriptional attenuation, in which mRNA remodeling caused by ribosome stalling regulates transcriptional termination rather than translational initiation.
