description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a toxic stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to blue light
synonyms: blue light response|blue-light response|response to blue light stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a blue light stimulus. Blue light is electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength of between 440 and 500nm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to light intensity
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a light intensity stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to high light intensity
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a high light intensity stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to low light intensity stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a low light intensity stimulus. Low light intensity is defined as a level of electromagnetic radiation at or below 0.1 micromols/m2.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: photoperiodism
synonyms: response to day length|response to night length|response to photoperiod
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of detection of, or exposure to, a period of light or dark of a given length, measured relative to a particular duration known as the 'critical day length'. The critical day length varies between species.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: entrainment of circadian clock
description: The synchronization of a circadian rhythm to environmental time cues such as light.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: UV protection
synonyms: UV resistance|UV tolerance|ultraviolet protection|ultraviolet resistance|ultraviolet tolerance
description: Any process in which an organism or cell protects itself from ultraviolet radiation (UV), which may also result in resistance to repeated exposure to UV.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to salt stress
synonyms: response to ionic osmotic stress|salinity response
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating an increase or decrease in the concentration of salt (particularly but not exclusively sodium and chloride ions) in the environment.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anatomical structure morphogenesis
description: The process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized. Morphogenesis pertains to the creation of form.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ethylene metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving ethylene (C2-H4, ethene), a simple hydrocarbon gas that can function in plants as a growth regulator.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to hormone
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a hormone stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to carbohydrate
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a carbohydrate stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to sucrose
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a sucrose stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to glucose
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a glucose stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to fructose
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a fructose stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to salicylic acid
synonyms: response to salicylate|response to salicylic acid stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a salicylic acid stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hormone-mediated signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals mediated by the detection of a hormone.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: carbohydrate mediated signaling
description: The series of molecular signals mediated by the detection of carbohydrate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: blue light signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated upon sensing of blue light by photoreceptor molecule, at a wavelength between 400nm and 470nm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of asymmetric cell division
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of asymmetric cell division.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of abscisic acid-activated signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of abscisic acid mediated signaling pathway|regulation of abscisic acid mediated signalling
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of abscisic acid (ABA) signaling.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of abscisic acid-activated signaling pathway
synonyms: activation of abscisic acid mediated signaling|positive regulation of abscisic acid mediated signaling pathway|positive regulation of abscisic acid mediated signalling|stimulation of abscisic acid mediated signaling|up regulation of abscisic acid mediated signaling|up-regulation of abscisic acid mediated signaling|upregulation of abscisic acid mediated signaling
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of abscisic acid (ABA) signaling.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: post-embryonic development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the organism over time, from the completion of embryonic development to the mature structure. See embryonic development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryo development ending in birth or egg hatching
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an embryo over time, from zygote formation until the end of the embryonic life stage. The end of the embryonic life stage is organism-specific and may be somewhat arbitrary; for mammals it is usually considered to be birth, for insects the hatching of the first instar larva from the eggshell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: coumarin metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving coumarins, compounds derived from the phenylacrylic skeleton of cinnamic acids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: flavonoid metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving flavonoids, a group of water-soluble phenolic derivatives containing a flavan skeleton including flavones, flavonols and flavanoids, and anthocyanins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: alkaloid metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving alkaloids, nitrogen containing natural products which are not otherwise classified as peptides, nonprotein amino acids, amines, cyanogenic glycosides, glucosinolates, cofactors, phytohormones or primary metabolites (such as purine or pyrimidine bases).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: alkaloid catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of alkaloids, nitrogen containing natural products not otherwise classified as peptides, nonprotein amino acids, amines, cyanogenic glycosides, glucosinolates, cofactors, phytohormones or primary metabolites (such as purine or pyrimidine bases).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: unidimensional cell growth
synonyms: cell elongation|cell growth along one axis|cell growth in one dimension|cell morphogenesis by unidimensional growth|polar cell growth|polarized cell growth
description: The process in which a cell irreversibly increases in size in one [spatial] dimension or along one axis, resulting in the morphogenesis of the cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic pattern specification
synonyms: embryonic pattern biosynthesis|embryonic pattern formation|ventral/lateral system
description: The process that results in the patterns of cell differentiation that will arise in an embryo.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: animal organ morphogenesis
description: Morphogenesis of an animal organ. An organ is defined as a tissue or set of tissues that work together to perform a specific function or functions. Morphogenesis is the process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized. Organs are commonly observed as visibly distinct structures, but may also exist as loosely associated clusters of cells that work together to perform a specific function or functions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tissue development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a tissue over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of metabolic process
synonyms: activation of metabolic process|positive regulation of metabolism|positive regulation of multicellular organismal metabolic process|positive regulation of organismal metabolism|stimulation of metabolic process|stimulation of organismal metabolic process|up regulation of metabolic process|up-regulation of metabolic process|up-regulation of organismal metabolic process|upregulation of metabolic process
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways within a cell or an organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of catabolic process
synonyms: down regulation of catabolic process|down-regulation of catabolic process|downregulation of catabolic process|inhibition of catabolic process|negative regulation of breakdown|negative regulation of catabolism|negative regulation of degradation
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of substances.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of catabolic process
synonyms: activation of catabolic process|positive regulation of breakdown|positive regulation of catabolism|positive regulation of degradation|stimulation of catabolic process|up regulation of catabolic process|up-regulation of catabolic process|upregulation of catabolic process
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of substances.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: auditory receptor cell fate commitment
description: The process in which the cellular identity of auditory hair cells is acquired and determined.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: epidermal cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an epidermal cell, any of the cells making up the epidermis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hormone transport
description: The directed movement of hormones into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: proximal/distal axis specification
description: The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of the proximal/distal axis. The proximal/distal axis is defined by a line that runs from main body (proximal end) of an organism outward (distal end).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anterior/posterior axis specification
description: The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of the anterior/posterior axis. The anterior-posterior axis is defined by a line that runs from the head or mouth of an organism to the tail or opposite end of the organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: polarity specification of anterior/posterior axis
description: Any process resulting in the establishment of polarity along the anterior/posterior axis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dorsal/ventral axis specification
synonyms: dorsal-ventral axis specification|dorsal/ventral axis determination|dorsoventral axis specification
description: The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of the dorsal/ventral axis. The dorsal/ventral axis is defined by a line that runs orthogonal to both the anterior/posterior and left/right axes. The dorsal end is defined by the upper or back side of an organism. The ventral end is defined by the lower or front side of an organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anterior/posterior pattern specification
description: The regionalization process in which specific areas of cell differentiation are determined along the anterior-posterior axis. The anterior-posterior axis is defined by a line that runs from the head or mouth of an organism to the tail or opposite end of the organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dorsal/ventral pattern formation
synonyms: dorsal-ventral pattern formation|dorsal/ventral pattern specification|dorsoventral pattern formation
description: The regionalization process in which the areas along the dorsal/ventral axis are established that will lead to differences in cell differentiation. The dorsal/ventral axis is defined by a line that runs orthogonal to both the anterior/posterior and left/right axes. The dorsal end is defined by the upper or back side of an organism. The ventral end is defined by the lower or front side of an organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: proximal/distal pattern formation
description: The regionalization process in which specific areas of cell differentiation are determined along a proximal/distal axis. The proximal/distal axis is defined by a line that runs from main body (proximal end) of an organism outward (distal end).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: epidermal cell fate specification
description: The process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into an epidermal cell in an environment that is neutral with respect to the developmental pathway; upon specification, the cell fate can be reversed.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of signal transduction
synonyms: regulation of signaling pathway|regulation of signalling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of signal transduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of signal transduction
synonyms: activation of signal transduction|positive regulation of signaling pathway|positive regulation of signalling pathway|stimulation of signal transduction|up regulation of signal transduction|up-regulation of signal transduction|upregulation of signal transduction
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of signal transduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of signal transduction
synonyms: down regulation of signal transduction|down-regulation of signal transduction|downregulation of signal transduction|inhibition of signal transduction|negative regulation of signaling pathway|negative regulation of signalling pathway
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of signal transduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell-cell recognition
description: Cell recognition between cells. May involve the formation of specialized cell junctions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intracellular water homeostasis
description: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of water within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: oocyte differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized immature germ cell acquires the specialized features of a mature female gamete.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glial cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a glial cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cardioblast differentiation
synonyms: cardiac precursor cell differentiation|cardioblast cell differentiation|cardiomyocyte generation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized mesodermal cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a cardioblast. A cardioblast is a cardiac precursor cell. It is a cell that has been committed to a cardiac fate, but will undergo more cell division rather than terminally differentiating.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: wax biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of wax, which includes C16 and C18 fatty acids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: meiotic chromosome condensation
synonyms: chromosome condensation involved in meiotic cell cycle
description: Compaction of chromatin structure prior to meiosis in eukaryotic cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to acetate
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an acetate stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to carbon dioxide
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a carbon dioxide (CO2) stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to metal ion
synonyms: heavy metal sensitivity/resistance|response to heavy metal|response to metal
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a metal ion stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to iron ion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an iron ion stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to iron(II) ion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an iron(II) ion stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to iron(III) ion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an iron(III) ion stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to manganese ion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a manganese ion stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to zinc ion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a zinc ion stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to aluminum ion
synonyms: response to aluminium ion|response to aluminum
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an aluminum ion stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to nickel cation
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nickel cation stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to mycotoxin
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a mycotoxin stimulus. A mycotoxin is a toxic chemical substance produced by fungi.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: zygote asymmetric cell division
description: The division of the zygote into two daughter cells that will adopt developmentally distinct potentials.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phenylacetate catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of phenylacetate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pyrimidine ribonucleotide salvage
description: The pathway by which pyrimidine bases or pyrimidine ribonucleosides from pyrimidine nucleotide breakdown are converted back to pyrimidine ribonucleotides. The salvage pathway is important where there is no de novo pyrimidine nucleotide biosynthesis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of proton transport
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of proton transport into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to chlorate
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a chlorate stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to X-ray
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of X-ray radiation. An X-ray is a form of electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength in the range of 10 nanometers to 100 picometers (corresponding to frequencies in the range 30 PHz to 3 EHz).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic body morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of the embryonic soma are generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to ozone
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a ozone stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to ionizing radiation
synonyms: response to ionising radiation|response to ionizing radiation stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a ionizing radiation stimulus. Ionizing radiation is radiation with sufficient energy to remove electrons from atoms and may arise from spontaneous decay of unstable isotopes, resulting in alpha and beta particles and gamma rays. Ionizing radiation also includes X-rays.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to UV-B
synonyms: response to UV-B light stimulus|response to UV-B radiation stimulus|response to UVB light stimulus|response to UVB radiation stimulus|response to medium wave ultraviolet light stimulus|response to medium wave ultraviolet radiation stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a UV-B radiation stimulus. UV-B radiation (UV-B light) spans the wavelengths 280 to 315 nm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to UV-C
synonyms: response to UV-C light stimulus|response to UV-C radiation stimulus|response to UVC light stimulus|response to UVC radiation stimulus|response to germicidal ultraviolet light stimulus|response to germicidal ultraviolet radiation stimulus|response to shortwave ultraviolet light stimulus|response to shortwave ultraviolet radiation stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a UV-C radiation stimulus. UV-C radiation (UV-C light) spans the wavelengths 100 to 280 nm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to lithium ion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a lithium (Li+) ion stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment or maintenance of transmembrane electrochemical gradient
description: The directed movement of ions to establish or maintain an electrochemical gradient across a membrane by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glucose mediated signaling pathway
description: The process in which a change in the level of mono- and disaccharide glucose trigger the expression of genes controlling metabolic and developmental processes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endomembrane system organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the endomembrane system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: SCF complex assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form the SKP1-Cullin/Cdc53-F-box protein ubiquitin ligase (SCF) complex.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to vitamin B1
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a vitamin B1 stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to selenium ion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from selenium ion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: detoxification of copper ion
description: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of copper ion. These include transport of copper away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of copper ion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to lead ion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a lead ion stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of hydrogen peroxide metabolic process
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving hydrogen peroxide.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: detoxification of zinc ion
description: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of zinc ion. These include transport of zinc away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of zinc ion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: membrane invagination
description: The infolding of a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to gamma radiation
synonyms: response to gamma ray|response to gamma-ray photon
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a gamma radiation stimulus. Gamma radiation is a form of electromagnetic radiation (EMR) or light emission of a specific frequency produced from sub-atomic particle interaction, such as electron-positron annihilation and radioactive decay. Gamma rays are generally characterized as EMR having the highest frequency and energy, and also the shortest wavelength, within the electromagnetic radiation spectrum.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lithium ion transport
description: The directed movement of lithium ion into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of anion channel activity
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of the anion channel activity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: COP9 signalosome assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a COP9 signalosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle
description: Any signaling pathway that modulates the activity of a cell cycle cyclin-dependent protein kinase to modulate the switch from G2 phase to M phase of the mitotic cell cycle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fatty acid omega-oxidation
description: A fatty acid oxidation process in which the methyl group at the end of the fatty acid molecule (the omega carbon) is first oxidized to a hydroxyl group, then to an oxo group, and finally to a carboxyl group. The long chain dicarboxylates derived from omega-oxidation then enter the beta-oxidation pathway for further degradation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to alkaline pH
synonyms: response to alkalinity|response to basic pH
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a pH stimulus with pH > 7. pH is a measure of the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to acidic pH
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a pH stimulus with pH < 7. pH is a measure of the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cell fate commitment
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell fate commitment. Cell fate commitment is the commitment of cells to specific cell fates and their capacity to differentiate into particular kinds of cells. Positional information is established through protein signals that emanate from a localized source within a cell (the initial one-cell zygote) or within a developmental field.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: centriole-centriole cohesion
description: The cell cycle process in which the two centrioles within a centrosome remain tightly paired.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: exit from mitosis
description: The cell cycle transition where a cell leaves M phase and enters a new G1 phase. M phase is the part of the mitotic cell cycle during which mitosis and cytokinesis take place.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of heart rate
description: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency or rate of heart contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of heart rate
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency or rate of heart contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mesenchymal cell proliferation
description: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of a mesenchymal cell population. A mesenchymal cell is a cell that normally gives rise to other cells that are organized as three-dimensional masses, rather than sheets.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of peptidase activity
description: Any process that stops or reduces the rate of peptidase activity, the hydrolysis of peptide bonds within proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: gene expression
description: The process in which a gene's sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA). This includes the production of an RNA transcript and its processing, as well as translation and maturation for protein-coding genes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of gene expression
synonyms: gene regulation|regulation of gene product expression|regulation of protein expression
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of gene expression. Gene expression is the process in which a gene's coding sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of signaling receptor activity
synonyms: regulation of receptor activity|regulation of signalling receptor activity
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a signaling receptor activity. Receptor activity is when a molecule combines with an extracellular or intracellular messenger to initiate a change in cell activity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of gastrulation
description: Any process that modulates the rate or extent of gastrulation. Gastrulation is the complex and coordinated series of cellular movements that occurs at the end of cleavage during embryonic development of most animals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of epidermal cell division
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the physical partitioning and separation of an epidermal cell into daughter cells. An epidermal cell is any of the cells that make up the epidermis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Lewis a epitope biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a Lewis a epitope, a trisaccharide (Fuc-alpha-(1->4)[Gal-beta-(1->3)]GlcNAc) characteristic of plant protein N-linked oligosaccharides.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intercellular transport
synonyms: single organism intercellular transport|single-organism intercellular transport
description: The movement of substances between cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: proteasomal protein catabolic process
synonyms: proteasome-mediated protein catabolic process|proteasome-mediated protein catabolism
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein or peptide by hydrolysis of its peptide bonds that is mediated by the proteasome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: proteasomal ubiquitin-independent protein catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein or peptide by hydrolysis of its peptide bonds that is mediated by the proteasome but do not involve ubiquitin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of autophagy
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of autophagy. Autophagy is the process in which cells digest parts of their own cytoplasm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of autophagy
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of autophagy. Autophagy is the process in which cells digest parts of their own cytoplasm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of autophagy
description: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the rate of autophagy. Autophagy is the process in which cells digest parts of their own cytoplasm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intracellular polyamine homeostasis
description: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of polyamine within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of pyruvate decarboxylation to acetyl-CoA
synonyms: regulation of acetyl-CoA biosynthetic process from pyruvate
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of acetyl-CoA from pyruvate. In most organisms, this pathway links glycolysis to the TCA cycle, by a series of three reactions carried out by a multisubunit complex called the 'pyruvate dehydrogenase complex', even though pyruvate dehydrogenase activity describes only one of those reactions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of phosphatidylinositol biosynthetic process
description: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of phosphatidylinositol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of phosphatidylinositol biosynthetic process
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of phosphatidylinositol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of phospholipase activity
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of phospholipase activity, the hydrolysis of a phospholipid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of calcium ion transport into cytosol
description: Any process that modulates the rate of the directed movement of calcium ions into the cytosol of a cell. The cytosol is that part of the cytoplasm that does not contain membranous or particulate subcellular components.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of calcium ion transport into cytosol
description: Any process that decreases the rate of the directed movement of calcium ions into the cytosol of a cell. The cytosol is that part of the cytoplasm that does not contain membranous or particulate subcellular components.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of calcium ion transport into cytosol
description: Any process that increases the rate of the directed movement of calcium ions into the cytosol of a cell. The cytosol is that part of the cytoplasm that does not contain membranous or particulate subcellular components.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: transposable element silencing

description: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of centrosome duplication. Centrosome duplication is the replication of a centrosome, a structure comprised of a pair of centrioles and peri-centriolar material from which a microtubule spindle apparatus is organized.

name: regulation of D-glucose transmembrane transport
synonyms: regulation of glucose transmembrane transport|regulation of glucose transport
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of glucose transport across a membrane. Glucose transport is the directed movement of the hexose monosaccharide glucose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of D-glucose transmembrane transport
synonyms: positive regulation of glucose transmembrane transport|positive regulation of glucose transport
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of glucose transport across a membrane. Glucose transport is the directed movement of the hexose monosaccharide glucose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of D-glucose transmembrane transport
synonyms: negative regulation of glucose transmembrane transport|negative regulation of glucose transport
description: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of glucose transport across a membrane. Glucose transport is the directed movement of the hexose monosaccharide glucose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of myotube differentiation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of myotube differentiation. Myotube differentiation is the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a myotube cell. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of myotube differentiation
description: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of myotube differentiation. Myotube differentiation is the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a myotube cell. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of myotube differentiation
description: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of myotube differentiation. Myotube differentiation is the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a myotube cell. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: telomere maintenance via telomere lengthening
description: Any process that contributes to the maintenance of proper telomeric length and structure by affecting and monitoring the activity of telomeric proteins and lengthening the telomeric DNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of protein ADP-ribosylation
synonyms: regulation of protein amino acid ADP-ribosylation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of protein ADP-ribosylation. Protein ADP-ribosylation is the transfer, from NAD, of ADP-ribose to protein amino acids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of protein ADP-ribosylation
synonyms: negative regulation of protein amino acid ADP-ribosylation
description: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of protein ADP-ribosylation. Protein ADP-ribosylation is the transfer, from NAD, of ADP-ribose to protein amino acids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of keratinocyte proliferation
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of keratinocyte proliferation. Keratinocyte proliferation is the multiplication or reproduction of keratinocytes, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of keratinocyte proliferation
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of keratinocyte proliferation. Keratinocyte proliferation is the multiplication or reproduction of keratinocytes, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of keratinocyte proliferation
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of keratinocyte proliferation. Keratinocyte proliferation is the multiplication or reproduction of keratinocytes, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of circadian sleep/wake cycle, wakefulness
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the wakeful phase of the circadian sleep/wake cycle. The wakeful phase is the part of the circadian sleep/wake cycle where the organism is not asleep.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of circadian sleep/wake cycle, wakefulness
description: Any process that increases the frequency, or extent of the wakeful phase of the circadian sleep/wake cycle. The wakeful phase is the part of the circadian sleep/wake cycle where the organism is not asleep.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retina layer formation
description: The process in which the vertebrate retina is organized into three laminae: the outer nuclear layer (ONL), which contains photoreceptor nuclei; the inner nuclear layer (INL), which contains amacrine, bipolar and horizontal cells; and the retinal ganglion cell (RGC) layer. Between the inner and outer nuclear layers, the outer plexiform layer (OPL) contains connections between the photoreceptors and bipolar and horizontal cells. The inner plexiform layer (IPL) is positioned between the INL and the ganglion cell layer and contains the dendrites of RGCs and processes of bipolar and amacrine cells. Spanning all layers of the retina are the radially oriented Mueller glia.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of reciprocal meiotic recombination
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of recombination during meiosis. Reciprocal meiotic recombination is the cell cycle process in which double strand breaks are formed and repaired through a double Holliday junction intermediate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of triglyceride biosynthetic process
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of triglyceride biosynthesis. Triglyceride biosynthesis is the collection of chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of triglyceride, any triester of glycerol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of triglyceride biosynthetic process
synonyms: positive regulation of triacylglycerol biosynthetic process
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of triglyceride biosynthesis. Triglyceride biosynthesis is the collection of chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of triglyceride, any triester of glycerol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of triglyceride biosynthetic process
synonyms: negative regulation of triacylglycerol biosynthetic process
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of triglyceride biosynthesis. Triglyceride biosynthesis is the collection of chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of triglyceride, any triester of glycerol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cholesterol efflux
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cholesterol efflux. Cholesterol efflux is the directed movement of cholesterol, cholest-5-en-3-beta-ol, out of a cell or organelle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of cholesterol efflux
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of cholesterol efflux. Cholesterol efflux is the directed movement of cholesterol, cholest-5-en-3-beta-ol, out of a cell or organelle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipid localization
description: Any process in which a lipid is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipid transport involved in lipid storage
description: The directed movement of lipids into cells that is part of their accumulation and maintenance.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cholesterol storage
description: The accumulation and maintenance in cells or tissues of cholesterol, cholest-5-en-3 beta-ol, the principal sterol of vertebrates and the precursor of many steroids, including bile acids and steroid hormones.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cholesterol transport involved in cholesterol storage
description: The directed movement of cholesterol into cells that is part of their accumulation and maintenance.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of release of sequestered calcium ion into cytosol by sarcoplasmic reticulum
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of release of sequestered calcium ion into cytosol by the sarcoplasmic reticulum, the process in which the release of sequestered calcium ion by sarcoplasmic reticulum into cytosol occurs via calcium release channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cardiac muscle contraction by regulation of the release of sequestered calcium ion
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle contraction via the regulation of the release of sequestered calcium ion by sarcoplasmic reticulum into cytosol. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the endoplasmic reticulum of striated muscle, specialised for the sequestration of calcium ions that are released upon receipt of a signal relayed by the T tubules from the neuromuscular junction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cardiac muscle contraction by calcium ion signaling
synonyms: regulation of cardiac muscle contraction by calcium ion signalling
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle contraction by changing the calcium ion signals that trigger contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of lipid storage
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of lipid storage. Lipid storage is the accumulation and maintenance in cells or tissues of lipids, compounds soluble in organic solvents but insoluble or sparingly soluble in aqueous solvents. Lipid reserves can be accumulated during early developmental stages for mobilization and utilization at later stages of development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of lipid storage
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of lipid storage. Lipid storage is the accumulation and maintenance in cells or tissues of lipids, compounds soluble in organic solvents but insoluble or sparingly soluble in aqueous solvents. Lipid reserves can be accumulated during early developmental stages for mobilization and utilization at later stages of development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of cholesterol storage
description: Any process that increases the rate or extent of cholesterol storage. Cholesterol storage is the accumulation and maintenance in cells or tissues of cholesterol, cholest-5-en-3 beta-ol, the principal sterol of vertebrates and the precursor of many steroids, including bile acids and steroid hormones.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cholesterol storage
description: Any process that decreases the rate or extent of cholesterol storage. Cholesterol storage is the accumulation and maintenance in cells or tissues of cholesterol, cholest-5-en-3 beta-ol, the principal sterol of vertebrates and the precursor of many steroids, including bile acids and steroid hormones.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of lipid storage
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of lipid storage. Lipid storage is the accumulation and maintenance in cells or tissues of lipids, compounds soluble in organic solvents but insoluble or sparingly soluble in aqueous solvents. Lipid reserves can be accumulated during early developmental stages for mobilization and utilization at later stages of development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of triglyceride storage
synonyms: positive regulation of sequestering of triacylglycerol|positive regulation of sequestering of triglyceride|positive regulation of triglyceride sequestration
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of sequestering of triglyceride. Triglyceride sequestration is the process of binding or confining any triester of glycerol such that it is separated from other components of a biological system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of triglyceride storage
synonyms: negative regulation of sequestering of triacylglycerol|negative regulation of sequestering of triglyceride|negative regulation of triglyceride sequestration
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of sequestering of triglyceride. Triglyceride sequestration is the process of binding or confining any triester of glycerol such that it is separated from other components of a biological system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of steroid biosynthetic process
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of steroids, compounds with a 1,2,cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of steroid biosynthetic process
description: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of steroids, compounds with a 1,2,cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of triglyceride catabolic process
synonyms: negative regulation of triacylglycerol catabolic process
description: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate, or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of triglyceride.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of triglyceride catabolic process
synonyms: positive regulation of triacylglycerol catabolic process
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate, or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of triglyceride.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of phosphatidylcholine catabolic process
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of phosphatidylcholine catabolism. Phosphatidylcholine catabolic processes are the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of phosphatidylcholines, any of a class of glycerophospholipids in which the phosphatidyl group is esterified to the hydroxyl group of choline.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of phosphatidylcholine catabolic process
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of phosphatidylcholine catabolism. Phosphatidylcholine catabolic processes are the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of phosphatidylcholines, any of a class of glycerophospholipids in which the phosphatidyl group is esterified to the hydroxyl group of choline.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of very-low-density lipoprotein particle remodeling
synonyms: positive regulation of VLDL remodeling|positive regulation of VLDL remodelling|positive regulation of very-low-density lipoprotein particle remodelling
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of very-low-density lipoprotein particle remodeling. Very-low-density lipoprotein particle remodeling is the acquisition, loss or modification of a protein or lipid within a very-low-density lipoprotein particle, including the hydrolysis of triglyceride by hepatic lipase or lipoprotein lipase and the subsequent loss of free fatty acid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of very-low-density lipoprotein particle remodeling
synonyms: negative regulation of VLDL remodeling|negative regulation of VLDL remodelling|negative regulation of very-low-density lipoprotein particle remodelling
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of very-low-density lipoprotein particle remodeling. Very-low-density lipoprotein particle remodeling is the acquisition, loss or modification of a protein or lipid within a very-low-density lipoprotein particle, including the hydrolysis of triglyceride by hepatic lipase or lipoprotein lipase and the subsequent loss of free fatty acid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of glucose metabolic process
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of glucose metabolism. Glucose metabolic processes are the chemical reactions and pathways involving glucose, the aldohexose gluco-hexose.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of glucose metabolic process
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of glucose metabolism. Glucose metabolic processes are the chemical reactions and pathways involving glucose, the aldohexose gluco-hexose.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of heparan sulfate proteoglycan biosynthetic process
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of heparan sulfate proteoglycan biosynthesis. Heparan sulfate proteoglycan biosynthetic processes are the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of the heparan sulfate proteoglycan, which consists of a core protein linked to a heparan sulfate glycosaminoglycan. The heparan sulfate chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-alpha-(1,4)-hexuronic acid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of very-low-density lipoprotein particle clearance
synonyms: negative regulation of VLDL clearance|negative regulation of VLDL particle clearance
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of very-low-density lipoprotein particle clearance. Very-low-density lipoprotein particle clearance is the process in which a very-low-density lipoprotein particle is removed from the blood via receptor-mediated endocytosis and its constituent parts degraded.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of mitochondrial membrane potential
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of establishment or extent of a mitochondrial membrane potential, the electric potential existing across any mitochondrial membrane arising from charges in the membrane itself and from the charges present in the media on either side of the membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of mitochondrial membrane potential
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of establishment or extent of a mitochondrial membrane potential, the electric potential existing across any mitochondrial membrane arising from charges in the membrane itself and from the charges present in the media on either side of the membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of inositol phosphate biosynthetic process
synonyms: negative regulation of inositol phosphate biosynthesis
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of inositol phosphate biosynthesis. Inositol phosphate biosynthetic processes are the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of an inositol phosphate, 1,2,3,4,5,6-cyclohexanehexol, with one or more phosphate groups attached.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of phosphatase activity
description: Any process that modulates the rate or frequency of phosphatase activity. Phosphatases catalyze the hydrolysis of phosphoric monoesters, releasing phosphate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of phosphatase activity
description: Any process that increases the rate or frequency of phosphatase activity. Phosphatases catalyze the hydrolysis of phosphoric monoesters, releasing inorganic phosphate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of phosphatase activity
description: Any process that decreases the rate or frequency of phosphatase activity. Phosphatases catalyze the hydrolysis of phosphoric monoesters, releasing inorganic phosphate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of macrophage tolerance induction
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate, or extent of B cell tolerance induction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of macrophage cytokine production
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of macrophage cytokine production. Macrophage cytokine production is the appearance of a chemokine due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cell cycle process
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of a cellular process that is involved in the progression of biochemical and morphological phases and events that occur in a cell during successive cell replication or nuclear replication events.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of intestinal phytosterol absorption
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of phytosterols into the blood by absorption from the small intestine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of endopeptidase activity
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of endopeptidase activity, the endohydrolysis of peptide bonds within proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of endopeptidase activity
description: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of endopeptidase activity, the endohydrolysis of peptide bonds within proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of protein processing
synonyms: positive regulation of protein maturation by peptide bond cleavage
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of protein maturation by peptide bond cleavage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of protein processing
synonyms: negative regulation of protein maturation by peptide bond cleavage
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of protein maturation by peptide bond cleavage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of vitamin D biosynthetic process
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of a vitamin D biosynthetic process. Vitamin D biosynthesis is the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of vitamin D, any of a group of related, fat-soluble compounds that are derived from delta-5,7 steroids and play a central role in calcium metabolism. Specific forms of vitamin D include calciferol (ergocalciferol; vitamin D2) and cholecalciferol (calciol; vitamin D3).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of metal ion transport
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of metal ion transport. Metal ion transport is the directed movement of metal ions, any metal ion with an electric charge, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: magnesium ion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of magnesium ions within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intracellular magnesium ion homeostasis
description: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of magnesium ions within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of mitotic sister chromatid separation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of mitotic sister chromatid separation. Mitotic sister chromatid separation is the process in which sister chromatids are physically detached from each other during mitosis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of phosphate transport
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of phosphate transport. Phosphate transport is the directed movement of phosphate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of microtubule nucleation
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of microtubule nucleation. Microtubule nucleation is the 'de novo' formation of a microtubule, in which tubulin heterodimers form metastable oligomeric aggregates, some of which go on to support formation of a complete microtubule. Microtubule nucleation usually occurs from a specific site within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: transport along microtubule
synonyms: establishment of localization by movement along microtubule|microtubule-based transport|movement along microtubule
description: The movement of organelles or other particles from one location in the cell to another along microtubules, driven by motor activity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle
synonyms: positive regulation of cyclin-dependent protein serine/threonine kinase activity involved in G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle|positive regulation of mitotic entry
description: Any signaling pathway that activates or increases the activity of a cell cycle cyclin-dependent protein kinase to modulate the switch from G2 phase to M phase of the mitotic cell cycle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle
description: Any signaling pathway that decreases or inhibits the activity of a cell cycle cyclin-dependent protein kinase to modulate the switch from G2 phase to M phase of the mitotic cell cycle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of neuron projection development
synonyms: regulation of neurite biosynthesis|regulation of neurite development|regulation of neurite formation|regulation of neurite growth
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of neuron projection development. Neuron projection development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a neuron projection over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A neuron projection is any process extending from a neural cell, such as axons or dendrites (collectively called neurites).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of neuron projection development
synonyms: positive regulation of neurite biosynthesis|positive regulation of neurite development|positive regulation of neurite formation|positive regulation of neurite growth
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of neuron projection development. Neuron projection development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a neuron projection over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A neuron projection is any process extending from a neural cell, such as axons or dendrites (collectively called neurites).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of neuron projection development
synonyms: growth cone collapse|negative regulation of neurite biosynthesis|negative regulation of neurite development|negative regulation of neurite formation|negative regulation of neurite growth
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of neuron projection development. Neuron projection development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a neuron projection over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A neuron projection is any process extending from a neural cell, such as axons or dendrites (collectively called neurites).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of high-density lipoprotein particle clearance
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of high-density lipoprotein particle clearance. High-density lipoprotein particle clearance is the process in which a high-density lipoprotein particle is removed from the blood via receptor-mediated endocytosis and its constituent parts degraded.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of high-density lipoprotein particle clearance
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of high-density lipoprotein particle clearance. High-density lipoprotein particle clearance is the process in which a high-density lipoprotein particle is removed from the blood via receptor-mediated endocytosis and its constituent parts degraded.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of low-density lipoprotein particle clearance
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of low-density lipoprotein particle clearance. Low-density lipoprotein particle clearance is the process in which a low-density lipoprotein particle is removed from the blood via receptor-mediated endocytosis and its constituent parts degraded.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of low-density lipoprotein particle clearance
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of low-density lipoprotein particle clearance. Low-density lipoprotein particle clearance is the process in which a low-density lipoprotein particle is removed from the blood via receptor-mediated endocytosis and its constituent parts degraded.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ubiquitin recycling
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of ubiquitin monomers and free ubiquitin chains at the level of the cell by recycling ubiquitin from proteasome-bound ubiquitinated intermediates.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: free ubiquitin chain polymerization
description: The process of creating free ubiquitin chains, compounds composed of a large number of ubiquitin monomers. These chains are not conjugated to a protein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to auditory stimulus
synonyms: response to sound|response to sound stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an auditory stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of translational initiation by eIF2 alpha phosphorylation
synonyms: eIF2 alpha phosphorylation in response to stress|regulation of translational initiation by eIF2 alpha phosphorylation in response to stress
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of translation initiation in response to stress by the phosphorylation of eIF2 alpha.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: programmed cell death
synonyms: PCD|RCD|caspase-independent apoptosis|caspase-independent cell death|non-apoptotic programmed cell death|nonapoptotic programmed cell death|regulated cell death
description: A process which begins when a cell receives an internal or external signal and activates a series of biochemical events (signaling pathway). The process ends with the death of the cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: induction of programmed cell death
synonyms: induction of non-apoptotic programmed cell death|induction of nonapoptotic programmed cell death
description: A process which directly activates any of the steps required for programmed cell death.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: astrocyte development
description: The process aimed at the progression of an astrocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. An astrocyte is the most abundant type of glial cell. Astrocytes provide support for neurons and regulate the environment in which they function.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: oligodendrocyte development
description: The process aimed at the progression of an oligodendrocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. An oligodendrocyte is a type of glial cell involved in myelinating the axons in the central nervous system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: microglia differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a microglial cell. Microglia are glial cells that act as the immune cells of the central nervous system. They form part of the supporting structure of this system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: microglia development
description: The process aimed at the progression of a microglial cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of microglia differentiation
synonyms: activation of microglia differentiation|positive regulation of microglial cell differentiation|stimulation of microglia differentiation|up regulation of microglia differentiation|up-regulation of microglia differentiation|upregulation of microglia differentiation
description: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of microglia differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a microglial cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glial cell proliferation
description: The multiplication or reproduction of glial cells by cell division, resulting in the expansion of their population. Glial cells exist throughout the nervous system, and include Schwann cells, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes among others.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Schwann cell proliferation
description: The multiplication or reproduction of Schwann cells, resulting in the expansion of their population. Schwann cells are a type of glial cell in the peripheral nervous system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: peripheral nervous system axon regeneration
synonyms: axon regeneration in peripheral nervous system
description: The regrowth of axons outside the central nervous system (outside the brain and spinal cord) following an axonal injury.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of gliogenesis
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of gliogenesis, the formation of mature glia.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of gliogenesis
synonyms: down regulation of gliogenesis|down-regulation of gliogenesis|downregulation of gliogenesis|inhibition of gliogenesis
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of gliogenesis, the formation of mature glia.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of gliogenesis
synonyms: activation of gliogenesis|stimulation of gliogenesis|up regulation of gliogenesis|up-regulation of gliogenesis|upregulation of gliogenesis
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of gliogenesis, the formation of mature glia.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuroblast differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuroblast. There are at least four stages through which the pluripotent cells of epiblast or blastula become neuroblasts.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: notochord formation
description: The formation of the notochord from the chordamesoderm. The notochord is composed of large cells packed within a firm connective tissue sheath and is found in all chordates at the ventral surface of the neural tube. In vertebrates, the notochord contributes to the vertebral column.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neural crest formation
description: The formation of the specialized region of ectoderm between the neural ectoderm (neural plate) and non-neural ectoderm. The neural crest gives rise to the neural crest cells that migrate away from this region as neural tube formation proceeds.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mesenchymal cell fate commitment
description: The process in which a cell becomes committed to become a mesenchymal cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mesenchymal cell development
description: The process aimed at the progression of a mesenchymal cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neural crest cell development
description: The process aimed at the progression of a neural crest cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neural crest cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neural crest cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neural crest cell fate commitment
description: The process in which a cell becomes committed to become a neural crest cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neural crest cell fate specification
description: The process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a neural crest cell in an environment that is neutral with respect to the developmental pathway; upon specification, the cell fate can be reversed.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Schwann cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a Schwann cell. Schwann cells are found in the peripheral nervous system, where they insulate neurons and axons, and regulate the environment in which neurons function.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of Schwann cell differentiation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of Schwann cell differentiation
synonyms: activation of Schwann cell differentiation|stimulation of Schwann cell differentiation|up regulation of Schwann cell differentiation|up-regulation of Schwann cell differentiation|upregulation of Schwann cell differentiation
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of neuron maturation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation, the process leading to the attainment of the full functional capacity of a neuron. This process is independent of morphogenetic change.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of neuron maturation
synonyms: activation of neuron maturation|stimulation of neuron maturation|up regulation of neuron maturation|up-regulation of neuron maturation|upregulation of neuron maturation
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of neuron maturation
synonyms: down regulation of neuron maturation|down-regulation of neuron maturation|downregulation of neuron maturation|inhibition of neuron maturation
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Schwann cell development
description: The process aimed at the progression of a Schwann cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. Schwann cells are found in the peripheral nervous system, where they insulate neurons and axons, and regulate the environment in which neurons function.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment of endothelial blood-brain barrier
synonyms: establishment of endothelial BBB|establishment of endothelial blood/brain barrier
description: Establishment of the endothelial barrier between the blood and the brain. The endothelial cells in the brain capillaries are packed tightly together preventing the passage of most molecules from the blood into the brain. Only lipid soluble molecules or those that are actively transported can pass through the blood-brain barrier.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glutamate secretion
description: The controlled release of glutamate by a cell. The glutamate is the most abundant excitatory neurotransmitter in the nervous system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of glutamate secretion
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of glutamate secretion
synonyms: activation of glutamate secretion|stimulation of glutamate secretion|up regulation of glutamate secretion|up-regulation of glutamate secretion|upregulation of glutamate secretion
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate.

description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate.
