name: negative regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
synonyms: down regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion|down-regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion|downregulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion|inhibition of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion|negative regulation of GABA secretion
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
synonyms: activation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion|positive regulation of GABA secretion|stimulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion|up regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion|up-regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion|upregulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission
synonyms: activation of acetylcholine secretion|stimulation of acetylcholine secretion|up regulation of acetylcholine secretion|up-regulation of acetylcholine secretion|upregulation of acetylcholine secretion
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of dopamine secretion
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of dopamine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of norepinephrine secretion
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of norepinephrine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of serotonin secretion
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of serotonin secretion
synonyms: down regulation of serotonin secretion|down-regulation of serotonin secretion|downregulation of serotonin secretion|inhibition of serotonin secretion|positive regulation of serotonin release
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin.

name: positive regulation of serotonin secretion
synonyms: activation of serotonin secretion|positive regulation of serotonin release|stimulation of serotonin secretion|up regulation of serotonin secretion|up-regulation of serotonin secretion|upregulation of serotonin secretion
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to purine-containing compound
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a purine-containing compound stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to amine
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an amine stimulus. An amine is a compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: striated muscle tissue development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a striated muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Striated muscle contain fibers that are divided by transverse bands into striations, and cardiac and skeletal muscle are types of striated muscle. Skeletal muscle myoblasts fuse to form myotubes and eventually multinucleated muscle fibers. The fusion of cardiac cells is very rare and can only form binucleate cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: branchiomeric skeletal muscle development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The branchiomeric muscle is derived from cranial mesoderm and controls facial expression, pharyngeal and laryngeal function, operating the jaw. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle. Branchiomeric muscles of mammals correspond to the gill musculature of fish.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
description: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of activation of satellite cell involved in skeletal muscle regeneration. The activation of satellite cell is the process that initiates satellite cell division by causing it to move from quiescence to the G1 stage of the cell cycle. The cell swells and there are a number of other small changes. The cells then start to divide. Following cell division the cells will differentiate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skeletal muscle satellite cell activation
description: The change of a skeletal muscle satellite cell from a mitotically quiescent to a mitotically active state following exposure to some activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand. In adult muscle, satellite cells become activated to divide and differentiate in response to muscle damage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by calcium ion signaling
synonyms: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by calcium ion signalling
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction by changing the calcium ion signals that trigger contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by modulation of calcium ion sensitivity of myofibril
synonyms: regulation of calcium ion sensitivity of myofibril involved in skeletal muscle contraction
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction by changing calcium ion binding affinity of the myofibril.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of the force of skeletal muscle contraction
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the force of skeletal muscle contraction. The force of skeletal muscle contraction is produced by acto-myosin interaction processes through the formation of cross bridges.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skeletal muscle atrophy
description: A process, occurring in skeletal muscle, that is characterized by a decrease in protein content, fiber diameter, force production and fatigue resistance in response to different conditions such as starvation, aging and disuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of skeletal muscle adaptation
description: Any process in which skeletal muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors. These adaptive events occur in both muscle fibers and associated structures (motoneurons and capillaries), and they involve alterations in regulatory mechanisms, contractile properties and metabolic capacities.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of muscle atrophy
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of muscle atrophy.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of muscle atrophy
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of muscle atrophy.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of muscle hyperplasia
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of muscle hyperplasia.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of muscle hypertrophy
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of muscle hypertrophy.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: smooth muscle adaptation
description: Any process in which smooth muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors. These adaptive events occur in both muscle fibers and associated structures (motoneurons and capillaries), and they involve alterations in regulatory mechanisms, contractile properties and metabolic capacities.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: smooth muscle hyperplasia
description: A process, occurring in smooth muscle, in which there is an increase in cell number by cell division, often leading to an increase in the size of an organ.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of somitogenesis
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of somitogenesis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: release of sequestered calcium ion into cytosol by sarcoplasmic reticulum
synonyms: release of sequestered calcium ion by sarcoplasmic reticulum into cytosol
description: The process in which the release of sequestered calcium ion by sarcoplasmic reticulum into cytosol occurs via calcium release channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by regulation of release of sequestered calcium ion
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction via the regulation of the release of sequestered calcium ion by sarcoplasmic reticulum into cytosol. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the endoplasmic reticulum of striated muscle, specialised for the sequestration of calcium ions that are released upon receipt of a signal relayed by the T tubules from the neuromuscular junction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by regulation of release of sequestered calcium ion
description: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction via the regulation of the release of sequestered calcium ion by sarcoplasmic reticulum into cytosol. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the endoplasmic reticulum of striated muscle, specialised for the sequestration of calcium ions that are released upon receipt of a signal relayed by the T tubules from the neuromuscular junction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: muscle cell migration
description: The orderly movement of a muscle cell from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skeletal muscle satellite cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a satellite cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tonic smooth muscle contraction
description: A process in which force is generated within tonic smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. In the tonic smooth muscle, the muscle contraction occurs without an ordered sarcomeric structure. Tonic smooth muscle contraction occurs as a sustained continuous contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to activity
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an activity stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: artery smooth muscle contraction
description: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the artery. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The artery is a vessel carrying blood away from the heart.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vein smooth muscle contraction
description: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the vein. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The vein is a vessel carrying blood away from the capillary beds.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intestine smooth muscle contraction
description: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the intestine. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The intestine is the section of the alimentary canal from the stomach to the anal canal. It includes the large intestine and small intestine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vascular associated smooth muscle contraction
description: A process, occurring in the vascular tissue, whereby actin/myosin complex activity generates force through ATP hydrolysis resulting in a change in smooth muscle geometry. This process is always coupled to chemo-mechanical energy conversion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: urinary bladder smooth muscle contraction
description: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the urinary bladder. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The urinary bladder is a musculomembranous sac along the urinary tract.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skeletal muscle satellite cell maintenance involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
synonyms: satellite cell compartment self-renewal involved in skeletal muscle regeneration|satellite cell population maintenance|satellite cell self-renewal
description: Any process by which the number of skeletal muscle satellite cells in a skeletal muscle is maintained during muscle regeneration. There are at least three mechanisms by which this is achieved. Skeletal muscle satellite stem cell asymmetric division ensures satellite stem cell numbers are kept constant. Symmetric division of these cells amplifies the number of skeletal muscle satellite stem cells. Some adult skeletal muscle myoblasts (descendants of activated satellite cells) can develop back into quiescent satellite cells, replenishing the overall pool of satellite cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myoblast migration involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
synonyms: mononucleate cell migration involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
description: The process in which a myoblast migrates along an entire fiber to the site of injury. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skeletal muscle satellite cell proliferation
description: The multiplication or reproduction of satellite cells, resulting in the expansion of the cell population. Satellite cells are quiescent cells that are located between the basal lamina and the plasmalemma of the muscle fiber, which are the main contributors to postnatal muscle growth. In adult muscle, satellite cells become activated to divide and differentiate in response to muscle damage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of skeletal muscle satellite cell proliferation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle satellite cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: growth factor dependent regulation of skeletal muscle satellite cell proliferation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of satellite cell proliferation; dependent on specific growth factor activity such as fibroblast growth factors and transforming growth factor beta.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: esophagus smooth muscle contraction
description: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the esophagus. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The esophagus is the muscular membranous segment between the pharynx and the stomach in the upper gastrointestinal tract.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to muscle activity
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a muscle activity stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to inactivity
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an inactivity stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skeletal muscle cell proliferation
description: The multiplication or reproduction of skeletal muscle cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction via regulation of action potential
synonyms: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction via membrane action potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction by depolarization of muscle membrane and ionic fluxes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skeletal myofibril assembly
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the skeletal myofibril over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A skeletal myofibril is a myofibril specific to skeletal muscle cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to muscle inactivity
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a muscle inactivity stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to muscle activity involved in regulation of muscle adaptation
synonyms: response to fatigue|response to muscle activity involved in regulation of muscle plasticity
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a muscle activity stimulus. This process occurs as part of the regulation of muscle adaptation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to electrical stimulus involved in regulation of muscle adaptation
synonyms: response to electrical stimulus involved in regulation of muscle plasticity
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an electrical stimulus. This process occurs as part of the regulation of muscle adaptation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: transition between fast and slow fiber
synonyms: transition between fast and slow fibre|transition fast-slow fiber|transition fast-slow fibre
description: The process of conversion of fast-contracting muscle fibers to a slower character. This may involve slowing of contractile rate, slow myosin gene induction, increase in oxidative metabolic properties, altered electrophysiology and altered innervation. This process also regulates skeletal muscle adapatation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: muscle atrophy
description: A process, occurring in the muscle, that is characterized by a decrease in protein content, fiber diameter, force production and fatigue resistance in response to different conditions such as starvation, aging and disuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: striated muscle atrophy
description: A process, occurring in striated muscle, that is characterized by a decrease in protein content, fiber diameter, force production and fatigue resistance in response to different conditions such as starvation, aging and disuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to denervation involved in regulation of muscle adaptation
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a denervation stimulus. This process occurs as part of the regulation of muscle adaptation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: smooth muscle hypertrophy
description: The enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of an organ due to an increase in size of its smooth muscle cells without cell division. Physiological hypertrophy is a normal process during development, and can also occur in mature structures on demand. In the uterus, smooth muscle cells undergo hypertrophy during pregnancy.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: muscle hypertrophy
description: The muscle system process that results in enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of a muscle organ due to an increase in the size of its muscle cells. Physiological hypertrophy is a normal process during development (it stops in cardiac muscle after adolescence) and can also be brought on in response to demand. In athletes cardiac and skeletal muscles undergo hypertrophy stimulated by increasing muscle activity on exercise. Smooth muscle cells in the uterus undergo hypertrophy during pregnancy.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cardiac muscle hypertrophy in response to stress
description: The physiological enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of the heart muscle due to an increase in size (not length) of individual cardiac muscle fibers, without cell division, as a result of a disturbance in organismal or cellular homeostasis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myotube differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a myotube cell. Myotube differentiation starts with myoblast fusion and the appearance of specific cell markers (this is the cell development step). Then individual myotubes can fuse to form bigger myotubes and start to contract. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myotube cell development
description: The process aimed at the progression of a myotube cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myoblast fusion involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
description: A process in which non-proliferating myoblasts, after migrating to the site of injury, fuse into existing damaged fibers or fuse to myotubes to form new fibers, as part of the process of skeletal muscle regeneration. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myotube cell development involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
description: The process aimed at the progression of a myotube cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. This occurs as part of the process of skeletal muscle regeneration. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myotube differentiation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a myotube cell. Myotube differentiation starts with myoblast fusion and the appearance of specific cell markers (this is the cell development step). Then individual myotubes can fuse to form bigger myotubes and start to contract. This process occurs as part of the process of skeletal muscle regeneration. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: smooth muscle cell migration
description: The orderly movement of a smooth muscle cell from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of smooth muscle cell migration
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of smooth muscle cell migration.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of smooth muscle cell migration
description: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of smooth muscle cell migration.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of smooth muscle cell migration
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of smooth muscle cell migration.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of lung blood pressure
description: The process that modulates the force with which blood travels through the lungs. The process is controlled by a balance of processes that increase pressure and decrease pressure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: heparan sulfate proteoglycan biosynthetic process
synonyms: heparan sulfate proteoglycan anabolism|heparan sulfate proteoglycan biosynthesis|heparan sulfate proteoglycan formation|heparan sulfate proteoglycan synthesis|heparan sulphate proteoglycan biosynthesis|heparan sulphate proteoglycan biosynthetic process|heparin proteoglycan biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of heparan sulfate proteoglycans, which consist of a core protein linked to a heparan sulfate glycosaminoglycan. The heparan sulfate chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-alpha-(1,4)-hexuronic acid, the former being either sulfated or deacetylated on its amino group as well as sulfated on one of its hydroxyl groups, and the latter being e a mixture of sulfated and nonsulfated D-glucuronic and L-iduronic acids. Heparan sulfate chains are covalently linked to serine/threonine residues (O-linked) of the core protein via a tetrasaccharide linker sequence (xylose-galactose-galactose-glucuronate).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein transport
description: The directed movement of proteins into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: DNA integration
description: The process in which a DNA segment is incorporated into another, usually larger, DNA molecule such as a chromosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: carbon dioxide transport
description: The directed movement of carbon dioxide (CO2) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: oxygen transport
description: The directed movement of oxygen (O2) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nickel cation transport
description: The directed movement of nickel (Ni) cations into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vanadium ion transport
description: The directed movement of vanadium (V) ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: copper ion import
description: The directed movement of copper ions into a cell or organelle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: plasma membrane copper ion transport
description: The directed movement of copper ions across the plasma membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lead ion transport
description: The directed movement of lead (Pb) ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: magnesium ion transport
description: The directed movement of magnesium (Mg) ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mercury ion transport
description: The directed movement of mercury (Hg) ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: quaternary ammonium group transport
synonyms: quaternary amine transport|quaternary ammonium compound transport
description: The directed movement into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore of quaternary ammonium compounds, any compound that can be regarded as derived from ammonium hydroxide or an ammonium salt by replacement of all four hydrogen atoms of the NH4+ ion by organic groups.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: inorganic anion transport
description: The directed movement of inorganic anions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Inorganic anions are atoms or small molecules with a negative charge which do not contain carbon in covalent linkage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bicarbonate transport
description: The directed movement of bicarbonate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: iodide transport
description: The directed movement of iodide into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nitrate transmembrane transport
synonyms: low affinity nitrate transport|low-affinity nitrate transport|nitrate transport
description: The directed movement of nitrate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nitrite transport
description: The directed movement of nitrite into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: monocarboxylic acid transport
description: The directed movement of monocarboxylic acids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bile acid and bile salt transport
description: The directed movement of bile acid and bile salts into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: canalicular bile acid transport
description: Enables the transfer of bile acid from one side of a hepatocyte plasma membrane into a bile canaliculus. Bile canaliculi are the thin tubes formed by hepatocyte membranes. Bile acids are any of a group of steroid carboxylic acids occurring in bile, where they are present as the sodium salts of their amides with glycine or taurine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bilirubin transport
description: The directed movement of bilirubin into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: formate transport
description: The directed movement of formate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lactate transport
description: The directed movement of lactate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Lactate is 2-hydroxypropanoate, CH3-CHOH-COOH; L(+)-lactate is formed by anaerobic glycolysis in animal tissues, and DL-lactate is found in sour milk, molasses and certain fruit juices.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mevalonate transport
description: The directed movement of mevalonate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: propanoate transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of propionate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: prostaglandin transport
description: The directed movement of prostaglandins into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: taurine transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of taurine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glucuronate transmembrane transport
description: The process in which glucuronate is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sialic acid transport
description: The directed movement of sialic acid into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: C4-dicarboxylate transport
description: The directed movement of a C4-dicarboxylate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. A C4-dicarboxylate is the anion of a dicarboxylic acid that contains four carbon atoms.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fumarate transport
description: The directed movement of fumarate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: alpha-ketoglutarate transport
description: The directed movement of alpha-ketoglutarate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: citrate transport
description: The directed movement of citrate, 2-hydroxy-1,2,3-propanetricarboxylate, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: urate transport
description: The directed movement of urate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: organophosphate ester transport
description: The directed movement of organophosphate esters into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Organophosphate esters are small organic molecules containing phosphate ester bonds.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pentose transmembrane transport
description: The process in which pentose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. A pentose is any aldose with a chain of five carbon atoms in the molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fructose transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of fructose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Fructose exists in a open chain form or as a ring compound. D-fructose is the sweetest of the sugars and is found free in a large number of fruits and honey.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fucose transmembrane transport
description: The process in which fucose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. Fucose is 6-deoxygalactose and has two enantiomers, D-fucose and L-fucose.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: galactose transmembrane transport
description: The process in which galactose is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. D-galactose is widely distributed in combined form in plants, animals and microorganisms as a constituent of oligo- and polysaccharides; it also occurs in galactolipids and as its glucoside in lactose and melibiose.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glucose-6-phosphate transport
description: The directed movement of glucose-6-phosphate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Glucose-6-phosphate is a monophosphorylated derivative of glucose with the phosphate group attached to C-6.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sucrose transport
description: The directed movement of sucrose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Sucrose is the disaccharide fructofuranosyl-glucopyranoside.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glucuronoside transport
description: The directed movement of glucuronosides into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Glucuronosides are any compound formed by combination of glycosidic linkage of a hydroxy compound (e.g. an alcohol or a saccharide) with the anomeric carbon atom of glucuronate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nucleotide-sugar transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of nucleotide-sugars into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Nucleotide-sugars are any nucleotide in which the distal phosphoric residue of a nucleoside 5'-diphosphate is in glycosidic linkage with a monosaccharide or monosaccharide derivative.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: CMP-N-acetylneuraminate transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of CMP-N-acetylneuraminate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: UDP-glucose transmembrane transport
description: The process in which UDP-glucose is transported across a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: UDP-glucuronate transmembrane transport
synonyms: UDP-glucuronic acid transmembrane transport|UDP-glucuronic acid transport
description: The directed movement of UDP-glucuronic acid into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. UDP-glucuronic acid is a substance composed of glucuronic acid in glycosidic linkage with uridine diphosphate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: UDP-N-acetylgalactosamine transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of UDP-N-acetylgalactosamine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. UDP-N-acetylgalactosamine is a substance composed of N-acetylgalactosamine, a common structural unit of oligosaccharides, in glycosidic linkage with uridine diphosphate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: UDP-xylose transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of UDP-xylose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. UDP-xylose is a substance composed of xylose in glycosidic linkage with uridine diphosphate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: polyol transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of polyols, any polyhydric alcohol, across a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glycerol transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of glycerol across a membrane. Glycerol is 1,2,3-propanetriol, a sweet, hygroscopic, viscous liquid, widely distributed in nature as a constituent of many lipids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mannitol transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of mannitol across a membrane. Mannitol is the alditol derived from D-mannose by reduction of the aldehyde group.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myo-inositol transport
description: The directed movement of myo-inositol into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Myo-inositol is 1,2,3,4,5/4,6-cyclohexanehexol, a growth factor for animals and microorganisms.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: acidic amino acid transport
description: The directed movement of acidic amino acids, amino acids with a pH below 7, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: aromatic amino acid transport
description: The directed movement of aromatic amino acids, amino acids with aromatic ring, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: basic amino acid transport
description: The directed movement of basic amino acids, amino acids with a pH above 7, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: branched-chain amino acid transport
synonyms: branched-chain aliphatic amino acid transport|branched-chain amino-acid anion transport|branched-chain amino-acid anions transport
description: The directed movement of branched-chain amino acids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Branched-chain amino acids are amino acids with a branched carbon skeleton without rings.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neutral amino acid transport
description: The directed movement of neutral amino acids, amino acids with no net charge, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: S-adenosyl-L-methionine transport
description: The directed movement of S-adenosylmethionine, S-(5'-adenosyl)-L-methionine, an important intermediate in one-carbon metabolism, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-amino acid transport
description: The directed movement of L-enantiomer amino acids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-alanine transport
description: The directed movement of L-alanine, the L-enantiomer of 2-aminopropanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: aspartate transmembrane transport
description: The process in which aspartate is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-cystine transport
description: The directed movement of L-cystine (also known as dicysteine) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: gamma-aminobutyric acid transport
description: The directed movement of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA, 4-aminobutyrate), an amino acid which acts as a neurotransmitter in some organisms, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-glutamate transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of L-glutamate across a membrane by means of some agent such as a transporter or a pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glycine transport
description: The directed movement of glycine, aminoethanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: histidine transport
description: The directed movement of histidine, 2-amino-3-(1H-imidazol-4-yl)propanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: isoleucine transport
description: The directed movement of isoleucine, (2R*,3R*)-2-amino-3-methylpentanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lysine transport
description: The directed movement of lysine, 2,6-diaminohexanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-leucine transport
description: The directed movement of L-leucine, 2-amino-4-methylpentanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: methionine transport
description: The directed movement of methionine, 2-amino-4-(methylthio)butanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ornithine transport
description: The directed movement of ornithine, 2,5-diaminopentanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phenylalanine transport
description: The directed movement of phenylalanine, 2-amino-3-phenylpropanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: proline transport
description: The directed movement of proline, pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-serine transport
description: The directed movement of L-serine, the L-enantiomer of 2-amino-3-hydroxypropanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: threonine transport
description: The directed movement of threonine, (2R*,3S*)-2-amino-3-hydroxybutanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tryptophan transport
description: The directed movement of tryptophan, 2-amino-3-(1H-indol-3-yl)propanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tyrosine transport
description: The directed movement of tyrosine, 2-amino-3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)propanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: valine transport
description: The directed movement of valine, 2-amino-3-methylbutanoic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: peptide transport
description: The directed movement of peptides, compounds of two or more amino acids where the alpha carboxyl group of one is bound to the alpha amino group of another, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: peptidoglycan transport
description: The directed movement of peptidoglycans, a class of glycoconjugates found in bacterial cell walls, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: amine transport
description: The directed movement of amines, including polyamines, organic compounds containing one or more amino groups, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: amino-acid betaine transport
description: The directed movement of betaine, the N-trimethyl derivative of an amino acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: urea transport
description: The directed movement of urea into, out of or within the cell. Urea is the water-soluble compound H2N-CO-NH2.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: aminergic neurotransmitter loading into synaptic vesicle
description: The active transport of aminergic neurotransmitters into a synaptic vesicle. This import is fuelled by an electrochemical gradient across the vesicle membrane, established by the action proton pumps.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: methylammonium transport
description: The directed movement of methylammonium into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: putrescine transport
description: The directed movement of putrescine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Putrescine is 1,4-diaminobutane, the polyamine formed by decarboxylation of ornithine and the metabolic precursor of spermidine and spermine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: spermidine transport
description: The directed movement of spermidine, N-(3-aminopropyl)-1,4-diaminobutane, a polyamine formed by the transfer of a propylamine group from decarboxylated S-adenosylmethionine to putrescine, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: organic acid transport
description: The directed movement of organic acids, any acidic compound containing carbon in covalent linkage, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: organic hydroxy compound transport
description: The directed movement of an organic hydroxy compound (organic alcohol) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. An organic hydroxy compound is an organic compound having at least one hydroxy group attached to a carbon atom.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nucleobase transport
description: The directed movement of a nucleobase, any nitrogenous base that is a constituent of a nucleoside, nucleotide, or nucleic acid, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: adenine transport
description: The directed movement of adenine, 6-aminopurine, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: guanine transport
description: The directed movement of guanine, 2-amino-6-hydroxypurine, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pyrimidine nucleobase transport
synonyms: pyrimidine base transmembrane transport|pyrimidine base transport|pyrimidine transmembrane transport|pyrimidine transport
description: The directed movement of pyrimidine nucleobases, one of the two classes of nitrogen-containing ring compounds found in DNA and RNA, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nucleoside transport
description: The directed movement of a nucleoside, a nucleobase linked to either beta-D-ribofuranose (ribonucleoside) or 2-deoxy-beta-D-ribofuranose, (a deoxyribonucleotide), into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: purine nucleoside transmembrane transport
synonyms: purine nucleoside membrane transport|purine nucleoside transport
description: The process in which a purine nucleoside is transported across a membrane. A purine nucleoside is a purine base covalently bonded to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cytidine transport
description: The directed movement of cytidine, cytosine riboside, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: uridine transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of uridine, uracil riboside, across a lipid bilayer, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pyrimidine nucleoside transport
description: The directed movement of a pyrimidine nucleoside, a pyrimidine base covalently bonded to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: purine nucleotide transport
description: The directed movement of a purine nucleotide, any compound consisting of a purine nucleoside esterified with (ortho)phosphate, into, out of or within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ADP transport
description: The directed movement of ADP, adenosine diphosphate, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ATP transport
description: The directed movement of ATP, adenosine triphosphate, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: acetylcholine transport
description: The directed movement of acetylcholine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Acetylcholine is an acetic acid ester of the organic base choline and functions as a neurotransmitter, released at the synapses of parasympathetic nerves and at neuromuscular junctions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: choline transport
description: The directed movement of choline into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Choline (2-hydroxyethyltrimethylammonium) is an amino alcohol that occurs widely in living organisms as a constituent of certain types of phospholipids and in the neurotransmitter acetylcholine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: biotin transport
description: The directed movement of biotin into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Biotin is cis-tetrahydro-2-oxothieno(3,4-d)imidazoline-4-valeric acid; the (+) enantiomer is very widely distributed in cells and serves as a carrier in a number of enzymatic beta-carboxylation reactions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: carnitine transport
description: The directed movement of carnitine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Carnitine is a compound that participates in the transfer of acyl groups across the inner mitochondrial membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: coenzyme A transport
description: The directed movement of coenzyme A into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Coenzyme A, 3'-phosphoadenosine-(5')diphospho(4')pantatheine, is an acyl carrier in many acylation and acyl-transfer reactions in which the intermediate is a thiol ester.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: creatine transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of creatine across a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-ascorbic acid transmembrane transport
synonyms: L-ascorbate transport|L-ascorbic acid transport|vitamin C transport
description: The process in which L-ascorbic acid is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other. L-ascorbate, (2R)-2-[(1S)-1,2-dihydroxyethyl]-4-hydroxy-5-oxo-2,5-dihydrofuran-3-olate, is vitamin C and has co-factor and anti-oxidant activities in many species.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: folic acid transport
synonyms: folate transport|vitamin B9 transport|vitamin M transport
description: The directed movement of folic acid (pteroylglutamic acid) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Folic acid is widely distributed as a member of the vitamin B complex and is essential for the synthesis of purine and pyrimidines.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: heme transport
description: The directed movement of heme, any compound of iron complexed in a porphyrin (tetrapyrrole) ring, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pantothenate transmembrane transport
synonyms: pantothenate membrane transport|pantothenate transport|vitamin B5 transport
description: The process in which pantothenate is transported across a membrane. Pantothenate is the anion of pantothenic acid, the amide of beta-alanine and pantoic acid; it is a B complex vitamin that is a constituent of coenzyme A and is distributed ubiquitously in foods.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: thiamine transport
description: The directed movement of thiamine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Thiamine is vitamin B1, a water soluble vitamin present in fresh vegetables and meats, especially liver.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cobalamin transport
description: The directed movement of cobalamin (vitamin B12), a water-soluble vitamin characterized by possession of a corrin nucleus containing a cobalt atom, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: siderophore transport
description: The directed movement of siderophores, low molecular weight Fe(III)-chelating substances, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tetracycline transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of tetracycline from one side of a membrane to the other. Tetracycline is a broad spectrum antibiotic that blocks binding of aminoacyl tRNA to the ribosomes of both Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms (and those of organelles).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fatty acid transport
description: The directed movement of fatty acids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Fatty acids are aliphatic monocarboxylic acids liberated from naturally occurring fats and oils by hydrolysis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: long-chain fatty acid transport
description: The directed movement of a long-chain fatty acid into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. A long-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing 13 to 22 carbons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: long-chain fatty acid import into peroxisome
synonyms: peroxisomal long-chain fatty acid import|peroxisomal long-chain fatty acid uptake
description: The directed movement of a long-chain fatty acid into a peroxisome. A long-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing 13 to 22 carbons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: long-chain fatty acid import across plasma membrane
synonyms: plasma membrane long-chain fatty acid transport
description: The directed movement of a long-chain fatty acid from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol. A long-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing 13 to 22 carbons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: short-chain fatty acid transport
description: The directed movement of short-chain fatty acids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. A short-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing fewer than 6 carbons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: short-chain fatty acid transmembrane transport
synonyms: short-chain fatty acid import|short-chain fatty acid uptake
description: The directed movement of short-chain fatty acids into a cell or organelle. A short-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing fewer than 6 carbons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phospholipid transport
description: The directed movement of phospholipids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Phospholipids are any lipids containing phosphoric acid as a mono- or diester.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fatty-acyl-CoA transport
synonyms: fatty acyl CoA transport|fatty acyl coenzyme A transport|fatty acyl-CoA transport
description: The directed movement of fatty acyl coenzyme A into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Fatty acyl coenzyme A is an acyl group linked to 3'-phosphoadenosine-(5')diphospho(4')pantatheine (coenzyme A).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: aminophospholipid transport
description: The directed movement of aminophospholipids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Aminophospholipids contain phosphoric acid as a mono- or diester and an amino (NH2) group.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sterol transport
description: The directed movement of sterols into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Sterols are steroids with one or more hydroxyl groups and a hydrocarbon side-chain in the molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: peroxisomal membrane transport
description: The directed movement of substances to, from or across the peroxisomal membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipopolysaccharide transport
description: The directed movement of lipopolysaccharides into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. A lipopolysaccharide is any of a group of related, structurally complex components of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria. Lipopolysaccharides consist three covalently linked regions, lipid A, core oligosaccharide, and an O side chain. Lipid A is responsible for the toxicity of the lipopolysaccharide.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nucleobase-containing compound transport
description: The directed movement of nucleobases, nucleosides, nucleotides and nucleic acids, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: coenzyme A metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving coenzyme A, 3'-phosphoadenosine-(5')diphospho(4')pantatheine, an acyl carrier in many acylation and acyl-transfer reactions in which the intermediate is a thiol ester.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: coenzyme A biosynthetic process
synonyms: CoA biosynthesis|coenzyme A anabolism|coenzyme A biosynthesis|coenzyme A formation|coenzyme A synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of coenzyme A, 3'-phosphoadenosine-(5')diphospho(4')pantatheine, an acyl carrier in many acylation and acyl-transfer reactions in which the intermediate is a thiol ester.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: coenzyme A catabolic process
synonyms: CoA catabolism|coenzyme A breakdown|coenzyme A catabolism|coenzyme A degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of coenzyme A, 3'-phosphoadenosine-(5')diphospho(4')pantatheine, an acyl carrier in many acylation and acyl-transfer reactions in which the intermediate is a thiol ester.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pantothenate metabolic process
synonyms: pantothenate metabolism|vitamin B5 metabolic process|vitamin B5 metabolism
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving pantothenate, the anion of pantothenic acid, the amide of beta-alanine and pantoic acid. It is a B complex vitamin that is a constituent of coenzyme A and is distributed ubiquitously in foods.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: formate metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving formate, also known as methanoate, the anion HCOO- derived from methanoic (formic) acid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: formate biosynthetic process
synonyms: formate anabolism|formate biosynthesis|formate formation|formate synthesis|formic acid biosynthesis|formic acid biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of formate, also known as methanoate, the anion HCOO- derived from methanoic (formic) acid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nucleobase-containing small molecule interconversion
description: The chemical reactions and pathways by which a nucleobase, nucleoside or nucleotide small molecule is synthesized from another nucleobase, nucleoside or nucleotide small molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: diadenosine polyphosphate catabolic process
synonyms: diadenosine polyphosphate breakdown|diadenosine polyphosphate catabolism|diadenosine polyphosphate degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of diadenosine polyphosphate, a derivative of the nucleoside adenosine with phosphate groups attached.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: diadenosine triphosphate catabolic process
synonyms: diadenosine triphosphate breakdown|diadenosine triphosphate catabolism|diadenosine triphosphate degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of diadenosine triphosphate, a derivative of the nucleoside adenosine with three phosphate groups attached.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: diadenosine tetraphosphate biosynthetic process
synonyms: diadenosine tetraphosphate anabolism|diadenosine tetraphosphate biosynthesis|diadenosine tetraphosphate formation|diadenosine tetraphosphate synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of diadenosine tetraphosphate, a derivative of the nucleoside adenosine with four phosphate groups attached.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: energy derivation by oxidation of organic compounds
description: The chemical reactions and pathways by which a cell derives energy from organic compounds; results in the oxidation of the compounds from which energy is released.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: proton motive force-driven ATP synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of ATP driven by transport of protons across a membrane to generate an electrochemical gradient (proton-motive force).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: electron transport coupled proton transport
description: The transport of protons against an electrochemical gradient, using energy from electron transport.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: CDP-diacylglycerol biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of CDP-diacylglycerol, CDP-1,2-diacylglycerol, a substance composed of diacylglycerol in glycosidic linkage with cytidine diphosphate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tRNA import into mitochondrion
synonyms: cytoplasmic tRNA import into mitochondria|cytoplasmic tRNA import into mitochondrion|cytoplasmic tRNA transport into mitochondrion|cytoplasmic tRNA|mitochondrial import|mitochondrial import of cytoplasmic tRNA|nuclear-encoded tRNA import into mitochondrion
description: The process in which a tRNA is transported from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: viral process
description: A multi-organism process in which a virus is a participant. The other participant is the host. Includes infection of a host cell, replication of the viral genome, and assembly of progeny virus particles. In some cases the viral genetic material may integrate into the host genome and only subsequently, under particular circumstances, 'complete' its life cycle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to phosphate starvation
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of deprivation of phosphate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: absorption of visible light
description: The reception of a (visible light) photon by a cell, visible light being defined as having a wavelength within the range 380-780 nm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipid catabolic process
synonyms: lipid breakdown|lipid catabolism|lipid degradation|lipolysis|multicellular organism lipid catabolic process|multicellular organismal lipid catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of lipids, compounds soluble in an organic solvent but not, or sparingly, in an aqueous solvent.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: detection of bacterium
synonyms: detection of bacteria|perception of bacteria|perception of bacterium
description: The series of events in which a stimulus from a bacterium is received and converted into a molecular signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: detection of fungus
synonyms: detection of fungi|detection of parasitic fungi|detection of parasitic fungus|perception of fungi|perception of fungus|perception of parasitic fungi|perception of parasitic fungus
description: The series of events in which a stimulus from a fungus is received and converted into a molecular signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: detection of temperature stimulus
synonyms: detection of temperature|detection of thermal stimulus|perception of temperature
description: The series of events in which a temperature stimulus (hot or cold) is received and converted into a molecular signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vesicle organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a vesicle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: carbohydrate biosynthetic process
synonyms: anabolic carbohydrate metabolic process|anabolic carbohydrate metabolism|carbohydrate anabolism|carbohydrate biosynthesis|carbohydrate formation|carbohydrate synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of carbohydrates, any of a group of organic compounds based of the general formula Cx(H2O)y.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: carbohydrate catabolic process
synonyms: carbohydrate breakdown|carbohydrate catabolism|carbohydrate degradation|catabolic carbohydrate metabolic process|catabolic carbohydrate metabolism|multicellular organismal carbohydrate catabolic process|single-organism carbohydrate catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of carbohydrates, any of a group of organic compounds based of the general formula Cx(H2O)y.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Wnt signaling pathway
synonyms: Wg signaling pathway|Wg signalling pathway|Wingless signaling pathway|Wingless signalling pathway|Wnt receptor signaling pathway|Wnt receptor signalling pathway|Wnt-activated signaling pathway|frizzled signaling pathway|frizzled signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by binding of a Wnt protein to a frizzled family receptor on the surface of a target cell and ending with a change in cell state.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: G protein-coupled opsin signaling pathway
synonyms: G protein-mediated opsin signaling pathway|rhodopsin mediated phototransduction|rhodopsin mediated signaling pathway|rhodopsin mediated signalling pathway|rhodopsin signaling
description: A G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway that starts with an opsin being activated by a photon, and ending with the light signal being trasmitted through the synapses. The signal can be transmitted via different Galpha subunits types: Go, Gs, Gq, and Gt.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of opsin-mediated signaling pathway
synonyms: deactivation of opsin mediated signaling|deactivation of rhodopsin mediated signalling|negative regulation of rhodopsin-mediated signaling pathway|rod response recovery
description: The process of restoring the photoreceptor cell to its unexcited state after termination of the stimulus (photon).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: immunoglobulin mediated immune response
description: An immune response mediated by immunoglobulins, whether cell-bound or in solution.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: type I hypersensitivity
description: An inflammatory response driven by antigen recognition by antibodies bound to Fc receptors on mast cells or basophils, occurring within minutes after exposure of a sensitized individual to the antigen, and leading to the release of a variety of inflammatory mediators such as histamines.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: RNA metabolic process
description: The cellular chemical reactions and pathways involving RNA, ribonucleic acid, one of the two main type of nucleic acid, consisting of a long, unbranched macromolecule formed from ribonucleotides joined in 3',5'-phosphodiester linkage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mRNA metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving mRNA, messenger RNA, which is responsible for carrying the coded genetic 'message', transcribed from DNA, to sites of protein assembly at the ribosomes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: rRNA metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving rRNA, ribosomal RNA, a structural constituent of ribosomes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: rRNA catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of rRNA, ribosomal RNA, a structural constituent of ribosomes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: snRNA catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of snRNA, small nuclear RNA, low-molecular-mass RNA molecules found in the eukaryotic nucleus as components of the small nuclear ribonucleoprotein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sno(s)RNA catabolic process
synonyms: sRNA catabolic process|sno(s)RNA breakdown|sno(s)RNA catabolism|sno(s)RNA degradation|snoRNA catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of snoRNA, small nucleolar RNA, any of a class of small RNAs that are associated with the eukaryotic nucleus as components of small nucleolar ribonucleoproteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tRNA decay
synonyms: tRNA breakdown|tRNA catabolic process|tRNA catabolism|tRNA degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of tRNA, transfer RNA, a class of relatively small RNA molecules responsible for mediating the insertion of amino acids into the sequence of nascent polypeptide chains during protein synthesis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic vesicle exocytosis
description: Fusion of intracellular membrane-bounded vesicles with the pre-synaptic membrane of the neuronal cell resulting in release of neurotransmitter into the synaptic cleft.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic vesicle priming
description: A process that converts synaptic vesicles to a state of competence for calcium triggered fusion with the active zone membrane by bringing the two membranes into very close proximity. Priming typically (but not always) occurs after docking (Jahn and Fasshauer, 2012). Primed vesicles are also capable of spontaneously fusing with the active zone membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: monoterpenoid metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving monoterpenoid compounds, terpenoids having a C10 skeleton.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: diterpenoid metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving diterpenoid compounds, terpenoids with four isoprene units.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: triterpenoid biosynthetic process
synonyms: triterpene biosynthesis|triterpene biosynthetic process|triterpenoid anabolism|triterpenoid biosynthesis|triterpenoid formation|triterpenoid synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of triterpenoid compounds, terpenoids with six isoprene units.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: carotenoid metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving carotenoids, tetraterpenoid compounds in which two units of 4 isoprenoid residues joined head-to-tail are themselves joined tail-to-tail.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: carotene metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving carotenes, hydrocarbon carotenoids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: carotene catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of carotenes, hydrocarbon carotenoids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: xanthophyll catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of xanthophylls, oxygen-containing carotenoids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sterol metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving sterols, steroids with one or more hydroxyl groups and a hydrocarbon side-chain in the molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sterol biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of sterols, steroids with one or more hydroxyl groups and a hydrocarbon side-chain in the molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glycoside catabolic process
synonyms: O-glycoside breakdown|O-glycoside catabolic process|O-glycoside catabolism|O-glycoside degradation|glycoside breakdown|glycoside catabolism|glycoside degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of glycosides, compounds in which a glycosyl group is substituted into a hydroxyl, thiol or selenol group in another compound.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: snRNA processing
description: Any process involved in the conversion of a primary small nuclear RNA (snRNA) transcript into a mature snRNA molecule. The primary function of snRNAs is processing pre-messenger RNA in the nucleus. They have also been shown to aid in the regulation of transcription factors (7SK RNA) or RNA polymerase II (B2 RNA), and maintaining the telomeres.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic vesicle budding from endosome
synonyms: endosome to synaptic vesicle budding|synaptic vesicle budding involved in synaptic vesicle exocytosis
description: Budding of synaptic vesicles during the formation of constitutive recycling vesicles from early endosomes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic vesicle coating
description: The formation of clathrin coated pits in the presynaptic membrane endocytic zone, triggered by the presence of high concentrations of synaptic vesicle components. This process leads to, but does not include budding of the membrane to form new vesicles.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic vesicle budding from presynaptic endocytic zone membrane
synonyms: synaptic vesicle budding from pre-synaptic membrane|synaptic vesicle budding involved in synaptic vesicle endocytosis
description: Evagination of the presynaptic membrane, resulting in the formation of a new synaptic vesicle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic vesicle maturation
description: Steps required to form an initiated synaptic vesicle into a fully formed and transmissible synaptic vesicle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic vesicle to endosome fusion
description: Fusion of a synaptic vesicle with an endosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic vesicle uncoating
synonyms: synaptic vesicle coat depolymerization|synaptic vesicle coat protein depolymerization
description: The removal of the protein coat on a synaptic vesicle following the pinching step at the end of budding from the presynaptic membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vesicle-mediated transport
