name: heparan sulfate proteoglycan metabolic process
synonyms: heparan sulfate proteoglycan metabolism|heparan sulphate proteoglycan metabolic process|heparan sulphate proteoglycan metabolism|heparin proteoglycan metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving heparan sulfate proteoglycans, which consist of a core protein linked to a heparan sulfate glycosaminoglycan. The heparan sulfate chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-alpha-(1,4)-hexuronic acid, the former being either sulfated or deacetylated on its amino group as well as sulfated on one of its hydroxyl groups, and the latter being a mixture of sulfated and nonsulfated D-glucuronic and L-iduronic acids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: heparin proteoglycan metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving heparin proteoglycans, which consist of a core protein linked to a heparin glycosaminoglycan. The heparin chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-alpha-(1,4)-hexuronic acid, the former being either sulfated or deacetylated on its amino group as well as sulfated on one of its hydroxyl groups, and the latter being e a mixture of sulfated and nonsulfated D-glucuronic and L-iduronic acids. Heparin is similar to heparan sulfate but it contains more N-sulfate and O-sulfate groups. Heparin proteoglycans are stored selectively in the secretory granules of mammalian mast cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glycosaminoglycan metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving glycosaminoglycans, any of a group of linear polysaccharides composed of repeating disaccharide units.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan catabolic process
synonyms: chondroitin sulfate breakdown|chondroitin sulfate catabolism|chondroitin sulfate degradation|chondroitin sulphate catabolic process|chondroitin sulphate catabolism
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans, which consist of a core protein linked to a chondroitin sulfate glycosaminoglycan. The chondroitin sulfate chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-D-glucuronic acid-beta-(1,3)-N-acetyl-D-galactosamine, the latter of which can be O-sulfated.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dermatan sulfate proteoglycan catabolic process
synonyms: chondroitin sulfate B catabolic process|chondroitin sulfate B catabolism|dermatan sulfate breakdown|dermatan sulfate catabolism|dermatan sulfate degradation|dermatan sulphate catabolic process|dermatan sulphate catabolism
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of dermatan sulfate proteoglycans, which consist of a core protein linked to a dermatan sulfate glycosaminoglycan. The dermatan sulfate chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-D-hexuronic acid-beta-(1,3)-N-acetyl-D-galactosamine. The former can be a mixture of sulfated and nonsulfated D-glucuronic and L-iduronic acids and the latter can be O-sulfated.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: heparin proteoglycan biosynthetic process
synonyms: heparan sulfate biosynthetic process|heparin anabolism|heparin biosynthesis|heparin formation|heparin synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of heparin proteoglycans, which consist of a core protein linked to a heparin glycosaminoglycan. The heparin chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-alpha-(1,4)-hexuronic acid, the former being either sulfated or deacetylated on its amino group as well as sulfated on one of its hydroxyl groups, and the latter being a mixture of sulfated and nonsulfated D-glucuronic and L-iduronic acids. Heparin is similar to heparan sulfate but it contains more N-sulfate and O-sulfate groups. Heparin chains are covalently linked to serine/threonine residues (O-linked) of the core protein via a tetrasaccharide linker sequence (xylose-galactose-galactose-glucuronate).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: heparin proteoglycan catabolic process
synonyms: heparan sulfate catabolic process|heparin breakdown|heparin catabolism|heparin degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of heparin proteoglycans, which consist of a core protein linked to a heparin glycosaminoglycan. The heparin chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-alpha-(1,4)-hexuronic acid, the former being either sulfated or deacetylated on its amino group as well as sulfated on one of its hydroxyl groups and the latter being a mixture of sulfated and nonsulfated D-glucuronic and L-iduronic acids. Heparin is similar to heparan sulfate but it contains more N-sulfate and O-sulfate groups.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hyaluronan metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving hyaluronan, the naturally occurring anionic form of hyaluronic acid. Hyaluronan is a type of non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta(1,4)-D-glucuronic acid-beta(1,3)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hyaluronan biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of hyaluronan, the naturally occurring anionic form of hyaluronic acid. Hyaluronan is a type of non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta(1,4)-D-glucuronic acid-beta(1,3)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hyaluronan catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of hyaluronan, the naturally occurring anionic form of hyaluronic acid. Hyaluronan is a type of non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta(1,4)-D-glucuronic acid-beta(1,3)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: keratinocyte differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a keratinocyte.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: T cell differentiation
synonyms: T cell development|T lymphocyte differentiation|T-cell differentiation|T-lymphocyte differentiation
description: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires characteristics of a more mature T-cell. A T cell is a type of lymphocyte whose definin characteristic is the expression of a T cell receptor complex.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: erythrocyte differentiation
synonyms: RBC differentiation|erythrocyte cell differentiation|erythropoiesis|red blood cell differentiation
description: The process in which a myeloid precursor cell acquires specializes features of an erythrocyte.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: megakaryocyte differentiation
description: The process in which a myeloid precursor cell acquires specializes features of a megakaryocyte.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: platelet formation
description: The process in which platelets bud from long processes extended by megakaryocytes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: basophil differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires specialized features of a basophil cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: eosinophil differentiation
synonyms: eosinophil cell development|eosinophil cell differentiation|eosinophil development
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specializes features of an eosinophil.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neutrophil differentiation
synonyms: neutrophil cell differentiation|neutrophil granulocyte differentiation|neutrophil granulocytopoiesis
description: The process in which a myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a neutrophil.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: monocyte differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a monocyte.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: macrophage differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized monocyte acquires the specialized features of a macrophage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: female sex determination
description: The specification of female sex of an individual organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: male sex determination
description: The specification of male sex of an individual organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myofibril assembly
description: Formation of myofibrils, the repeating units of striated muscle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skeletal muscle thin filament assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of proteins to form the actin-based thin filaments of myofibrils in skeletal muscle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skeletal muscle myosin thick filament assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of proteins to form the myosin-based thick filaments of myofibrils in skeletal muscle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: growth hormone secretion
description: The regulated release of growth hormone from secretory granules into the blood.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipid modification
description: The covalent alteration of one or more fatty acids in a lipid, resulting in a change in the properties of the lipid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: chromosome condensation
synonyms: DNA condensation|eukaryotic chromosome condensation|nuclear chromosome condensation
description: The progressive compaction of dispersed interphase chromatin into threadlike chromosomes prior to mitotic or meiotic nuclear division, or during apoptosis, in eukaryotic cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: apoptotic nuclear changes
description: Alterations undergone by nuclei at the molecular and morphological level as part of the execution phase of apoptosis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: apoptotic chromosome condensation
description: The compaction of chromatin during apoptosis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear fragmentation involved in apoptotic nuclear change
synonyms: apoptotic nuclear fragmentation|nuclear fragmentation during apoptosis|nucleus fragmentation
description: The breakdown of the nucleus into small membrane-bounded compartments, or blebs, each of which contain compacted DNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: maintenance of gastrointestinal epithelium
description: Protection of epithelial surfaces of the gastrointestinal tract from proteolytic and caustic digestive agents.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of ossification
synonyms: regulation of bone biosynthesis|regulation of bone formation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of ossification, the formation of bone or of a bony substance or the conversion of fibrous tissue or of cartilage into bone or a bony substance.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of ossification
synonyms: down regulation of ossification|down-regulation of ossification|downregulation of ossification|inhibition of ossification|negative regulation of bone biosynthesis|negative regulation of bone formation
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of ossification, the formation of bone or of a bony substance or the conversion of fibrous tissue or of cartilage into bone or a bony substance.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bone mineralization
description: The deposition of hydroxyapatite, a form of calcium phosphate with the formula Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2, in bone tissue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intestinal cholesterol absorption
description: Uptake of cholesterol into the blood by absorption from the small intestine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cholesterol transport
description: The directed movement of cholesterol, cholest-5-en-3-beta-ol, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: deoxynucleotide transport
description: The directed movement of a deoxynucleotide, a deoxyribonucleoside in ester linkage to phosphate, commonly at the 5' position of deoxyribose, into, out of or within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of cell growth
synonyms: activation of cell growth|stimulation of cell growth|up regulation of cell growth|up-regulation of cell growth|upregulation of cell growth
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, extent or direction of cell growth.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cell growth
synonyms: down regulation of cell growth|down-regulation of cell growth|downregulation of cell growth|inhibition of cell growth
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, extent or direction of cell growth.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: poly-N-acetyllactosamine biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of poly-N-acetyllactosamine, a carbohydrate composed of N-acetyllactosamine repeats (Gal-beta-1,4-GlcNAc-beta-1,3)n.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: osteoclast differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized monocyte acquires the specialized features of an osteoclast. An osteoclast is a specialized phagocytic cell associated with the absorption and removal of the mineralized matrix of bone tissue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: flagellated sperm motility
synonyms: flagellated sperm movement|sperm flagellum movement|sperm flagellum movement involved in flagellated sperm motility|sperm flagellum movement involved in flagellated sperm movement|sperm motility|sperm movement
description: The directed, self-propelled movement of a cilium (aka flagellum) that contributes to the movement of a flagellated sperm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: melanocyte differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a melanocyte.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: transepithelial chloride transport
description: The directed movement of chloride ions from one side of an epithelium to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: stabilization of membrane potential
description: The accomplishment of a non-fluctuating membrane potential, the electric potential existing across any membrane arising from charges in the membrane itself and from the charges present in the media on either side of the membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: respiratory tube development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the respiratory tube over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The respiratory tube is assumed to mean any tube in the respiratory tract.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lung development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the lung over time, from its formation to the mature structure. In all air-breathing vertebrates the lungs are developed from the ventral wall of the oesophagus as a pouch which divides into two sacs. In amphibians and many reptiles the lungs retain very nearly this primitive sac-like character, but in the higher forms the connection with the esophagus becomes elongated into the windpipe and the inner walls of the sacs become more and more divided, until, in the mammals, the air spaces become minutely divided into tubes ending in small air cells, in the walls of which the blood circulates in a fine network of capillaries. In mammals the lungs are more or less divided into lobes, and each lung occupies a separate cavity in the thorax.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: adrenal gland development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the adrenal gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. This gland can either be a discrete structure located bilaterally above each kidney, or a cluster of cells in the head kidney that perform the functions of the adrenal gland. In either case, this organ consists of two cells types, aminergic chromaffin cells and steroidogenic cortical cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic limb morphogenesis
description: The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the limb are generated and organized. A limb is an appendage of an animal used for locomotion or grasping.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: prenylated protein catabolic process
synonyms: prenylated protein breakdown|prenylated protein catabolism|prenylated protein degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of prenylated proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: prenylcysteine catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of prenylcysteine, 3-methyl-2-buten-1-yl-cysteine, a derivative of the amino acid cysteine formed by the covalent addition of a prenyl residue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: DNA damage response, signal transduction by p53 class mediator
synonyms: DNA damage response|activation of p53|TP53 signaling pathway|p53 signaling pathway|p53-mediated DNA damage response
description: A cascade of processes induced by the cell cycle regulator phosphoprotein p53, or an equivalent protein, in response to the detection of DNA damage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cell migration
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell migration.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of cell migration
synonyms: activation of cell migration|stimulation of cell migration|up regulation of cell migration|up-regulation of cell migration|upregulation of cell migration
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cell migration.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cell migration
synonyms: down regulation of cell migration|down-regulation of cell migration|downregulation of cell migration|inhibition of cell migration
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cell migration.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fructose 1,6-bisphosphate metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving fructose 1,6-bisphosphate, also known as FBP. The D enantiomer is a metabolic intermediate in glycolysis and gluconeogenesis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fructosamine catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of fructosamine, a fructose molecule containing an amino group in place of a hydroxyl group.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: membrane disassembly
description: The controlled breakdown of any cell membrane in the context of a normal process such as autophagy.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: defecation
description: The expulsion of feces from the rectum.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: siRNA processing
synonyms: RNA interference|production of guide RNAs|RNA interference|production of siRNA|chromatin silencing by small RNA|production of guide RNAs|chromatin silencing by small RNA|production of siRNA|production of guide RNAs involved in RNA interference|production of guide RNAs involved in chromatin silencing by small RNA|production of siRNA|production of siRNA involved in PTGS|production of siRNA involved in RNA interference|production of siRNA involved in chromatin silencing by small RNA|production of siRNA involved in gene silencing by small RNA|production of siRNA involved in post-transcriptional gene silencing by RNA
description: A process leading to the generation of a functional small interfering RNA (siRNA). Includes the cleavage of double-stranded RNA to form small interfering RNA molecules (siRNAs) of 21-23 nucleotides. May also include amplification of the siRNA by RNA-directed RNA polymerase.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sleep
description: Any process in which an organism enters and maintains a periodic, readily reversible state of reduced awareness and metabolic activity. Usually accompanied by physical relaxation, the onset of sleep in humans and other mammals is marked by a change in the electrical activity of the brain.

description: A wavelike sequence of involuntary muscular contraction and relaxation that passes along a tubelike structure, such as the intestine, impelling the contents onwards.

description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of complement activation.

description: A nuclear receptor-mediated signaling pathway initiated by an estrogen binding to an intracellular receptor of the nuclear receptor protein family, and ending with regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: androgen receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: androgen receptor signalling pathway|nuclear-receptor-mediated androgen receptor signaling pathway
description: A nuclear receptor-mediated signaling pathway initiated by an androgen binding to an intracellular receptor of the nuclear receptor protein family, and ending with regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

name: intracellular receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: intracellular receptor mediated signaling pathway|intracellular receptor-mediated signaling pathway|intracellular receptor-mediated signalling pathway

name: adult behavior
synonyms: adult behavioral response to stimulus|adult behaviour|adult behavioural response to stimulus

label: BiologicalProcess
name: male genitalia development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the male genitalia over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: female genitalia development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the female genitalia over time, from formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: collagen catabolic process
description: The proteolytic chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of collagen in the extracellular matrix, usually carried out by proteases secreted by nearby cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear body organization
synonyms: nuclear body organisation|nuclear body organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of any of the extra-nucleolar nuclear domains usually visualized by confocal microscopy and fluorescent antibodies to specific proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Cajal body organization
synonyms: Cajal body organisation|Cajal body organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of Cajal bodies, nuclear bodies that appear ultrastructurally as a tangle of coiled, electron-dense threads roughly 0.5 micrometers in diameter and are enriched in ribonucleoproteins, and certain general RNA polymerase II transcription factors.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: PML body organization
synonyms: PML body organisation|PML body organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of PML bodies, a class of nuclear body; they react against SP100 auto-antibodies (PML = promyelocytic leukemia).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: DNA ADP-ribosylation
description: The covalent attachment of an ADP-ribosyl group to a residue in double-stranded DNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neutrophil chemotaxis
description: The directed movement of a neutrophil cell, the most numerous polymorphonuclear leukocyte found in the blood, in response to an external stimulus, usually an infection or wounding.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: leukocyte chemotaxis
description: The movement of a leukocyte in response to an external stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intracellular phosphate ion homeostasis
synonyms: cellular phosphate ion homeostasis|intracellular Pi homeostasis|intracellular phosphate homeostasis
description: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of phosphate ions within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intracellular chloride ion homeostasis
description: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of chloride ions within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cytoskeleton-dependent intracellular transport
description: The directed movement of substances along cytoskeletal fibers such as microfilaments or microtubules within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: germ-line stem cell population maintenance
description: Any process by which an organism or tissue maintains a population of germ-line stem cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: P granule organization
synonyms: P granule organization and biogenesis|polar granule organisation|polar granule organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of polar granules, cytoplasmic, non-membranous RNA/protein complex aggregates in the primordial germ cells of many higher eukaryotes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ovulation
description: The release of a mature ovum/oocyte from an ovary.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of actin filament length
description: Any process that controls the length of actin filaments in a cell.

name: regulation of actin filament polymerization
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the assembly of actin filaments by the addition of actin monomers to a filament.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of actin filament depolymerization

label: BiologicalProcess
name: prostate gland development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the prostate gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The prostate gland is a partly muscular, partly glandular body that is situated near the base of the mammalian male urethra and secretes an alkaline viscid fluid which is a major constituent of the ejaculatory fluid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: granulocyte differentiation
description: The process in which a myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a granulocyte. Granulocytes are a class of leukocytes characterized by the presence of granules in their cytoplasm. These cells are active in allergic immune reactions such as arthritic inflammation and rashes. This class includes basophils, eosinophils and neutrophils.

synonyms: down regulation of granulocyte differentiation|down-regulation of granulocyte differentiation|downregulation of granulocyte differentiation|inhibition of granulocyte differentiation

synonyms: activation of granulocyte differentiation|stimulation of granulocyte differentiation|up regulation of granulocyte differentiation|up-regulation of granulocyte differentiation|upregulation of granulocyte differentiation
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of granulocyte differentiation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: epithelial cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an epithelial cell, any of the cells making up an epithelium.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of epithelial cell differentiation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of epithelial cell differentiation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of epithelial cell differentiation
synonyms: down regulation of epithelial cell differentiation|down-regulation of epithelial cell differentiation|downregulation of epithelial cell differentiation|inhibition of epithelial cell differentiation
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of epithelial cell differentiation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of epithelial cell differentiation
synonyms: activation of epithelial cell differentiation|stimulation of epithelial cell differentiation|up regulation of epithelial cell differentiation|up-regulation of epithelial cell differentiation|upregulation of epithelial cell differentiation
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of epithelial cell differentiation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: polarized epithelial cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a polarized epithelial cell. The polarized epithelial cell can be any of the cells within an epithelium where the epithelial sheet is oriented with respect to the planar axis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of polarized epithelial cell differentiation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of polarized epithelial cell differentiation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cortical cytoskeleton organization
synonyms: cortical cytoskeleton organisation|cortical cytoskeleton organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures in the cell cortex, i.e. just beneath the plasma membrane.

synonyms: actin cortex stabilization|cortical actin cytoskeleton organisation|cortical actin cytoskeleton organization and biogenesis|cortical actin cytoskeleton stabilization|cortical resistance
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of actin-based cytoskeletal structures in the cell cortex, i.e. just beneath the plasma membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: thyroid gland development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the thyroid gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The thyroid gland is an endoderm-derived gland that produces thyroid hormone.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mammary gland development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mammary gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mammary gland is a large compound sebaceous gland that in female mammals is modified to secrete milk. Its development starts with the formation of the mammary line and ends as the mature gland cycles between nursing and weaning stages.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation
synonyms: down regulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation|down-regulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation|downregulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation|inhibition of myeloid dendritic cell activation
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of myeloid dendritic cell activation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation
synonyms: activation of myeloid dendritic cell activation|stimulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation|up regulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation|up-regulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation|upregulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation
description: Any process that stimulates, induces or increases the rate of myeloid dendritic cell activation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of B cell proliferation
synonyms: regulation of B lymphocyte proliferation|regulation of B-cell proliferation|regulation of B-lymphocyte proliferation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of B cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess

synonyms: down regulation of B cell proliferation|down-regulation of B cell proliferation|downregulation of B cell proliferation|inhibition of B cell proliferation|negative regulation of B lymphocyte proliferation|negative regulation of B-cell proliferation|negative regulation of B-lymphocyte proliferation
description: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the rate or extent of B cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of B cell proliferation
synonyms: activation of B cell proliferation|positive regulation of B lymphocyte proliferation|positive regulation of B-cell proliferation|positive regulation of B-lymphocyte proliferation|stimulation of B cell proliferation|up regulation of B cell proliferation|up-regulation of B cell proliferation|upregulation of B cell proliferation
description: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of B cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: forebrain development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the forebrain over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The forebrain is the anterior of the three primary divisions of the developing chordate brain or the corresponding part of the adult brain (in vertebrates, includes especially the cerebral hemispheres, the thalamus, and the hypothalamus and especially in higher vertebrates is the main control center for sensory and associative information processing, visceral functions, and voluntary motor functions).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: midbrain development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the midbrain over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The midbrain is the middle division of the three primary divisions of the developing chordate brain or the corresponding part of the adult brain (in vertebrates, includes a ventral part containing the cerebral peduncles and a dorsal tectum containing the corpora quadrigemina and that surrounds the aqueduct of Sylvius connecting the third and fourth ventricles).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hindbrain development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the hindbrain over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The hindbrain is the posterior of the three primary divisions of the developing chordate brain, or the corresponding part of the adult brain (in vertebrates, includes the cerebellum, pons, and medulla oblongata and controls the autonomic functions and equilibrium).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: notochord development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the notochord over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The notochord is a mesoderm-derived structure located ventral of the developing nerve cord. In vertebrates, the notochord serves as a core around which other mesodermal cells form the vertebrae. In the most primitive chordates, which lack vertebrae, the notochord persists as a substitute for a vertebral column.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: olfactory placode formation
description: The formation of a thickening of the neural ectoderm in the head region of the vertebrate embryo which develops into the olfactory region of the nasal cavity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: paranodal junction assembly
synonyms: paranodal axoglial junction formation|paranodal junction biosynthesis|paranodal junction formation
description: Formation of the junction between an axon and the glial cell that forms the myelin sheath. Paranodal junctions form at each paranode, i.e. at the ends of the unmyelinated nodes of Ranvier.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: otic vesicle formation
description: The process resulting in the transition of the otic placode into the otic vesicle, a transient embryonic structure formed during development of the vertebrate inner ear.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of VEGF receptor signaling pathway|regulation of VEGF receptor signalling pathway|regulation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signalling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway activity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: down regulation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway|down-regulation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway|downregulation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway|inhibition of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway|negative regulation of VEGF receptor signaling pathway|negative regulation of VEGF receptor signalling pathway|negative regulation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signalling pathway
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway activity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway

description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor signaling pathway activity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment or maintenance of actin cytoskeleton polarity
description: Any cellular process that results in the specification, formation or maintenance of polarized actin-based cytoskeletal structures.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment or maintenance of microtubule cytoskeleton polarity
description: Any cellular process that results in the specification, formation or maintenance of polarized microtubule-based cytoskeletal structures.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: astral microtubule organization
synonyms: astral microtubule organisation|astral microtubule organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of astral microtubules, any of the spindle microtubules that radiate in all directions from the spindle poles.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response
synonyms: ER unfolded protein response|SREBP-mediated signalling pathway|erUPR
description: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of the presence of unfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) or other ER-related stress; results in changes in the regulation of transcription and translation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retrograde protein transport, ER to cytosol
synonyms: protein dislocation from ER|protein retrotranslocation|ER to cytosol|retrograde protein transport|endoplasmic reticulum to cytosol
description: The directed movement of unfolded or misfolded proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum to the cytosol through the translocon.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: thiamine pyrophosphate transmembrane transport
synonyms: TPP transport|thiamin diphosphate transport|thiamin pyrophosphate transport|thiamine diphosphate transport|thiamine pyrophosphate transport
description: The process in which thiamine pyrophosphate is transported across a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of centriole-centriole cohesion
description: Any process that modulates the extent to which the two centrioles within a centrosome remain tightly paired; may be mediated by the assembly and disassembly of a proteinaceous linker.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to caffeine
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a caffeine stimulus. Caffeine is an alkaloid found in numerous plant species, where it acts as a natural pesticide that paralyzes and kills certain insects feeding upon them.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pancreas development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the pancreas over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The pancreas is an endoderm derived structure that produces precursors of digestive enzymes and blood glucose regulating hormones.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: exocrine pancreas development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the exocrine pancreas over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The exocrine pancreas produces and store zymogens of digestive enzymes, such as chymotrypsinogen and trypsinogen in the acinar cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endocrine pancreas development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the endocrine pancreas over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The endocrine pancreas is made up of islet cells that produce insulin, glucagon and somatostatin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear migration along microfilament
description: The directed movement of the nucleus along microfilaments within the cell, mediated by motor proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: microtubule organizing center organization
synonyms: microtubule organising center organisation|microtubule organizing center organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a microtubule organizing center, a structure from which microtubules grow.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: actomyosin structure organization
synonyms: actomyosin organization|actomyosin structure organisation|actomyosin structure organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures containing both actin and myosin or paramyosin. The myosin may be organized into filaments.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myosin filament assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a filament composed of myosin molecules.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulatory ncRNA-mediated gene silencing
synonyms: RNA-dependent gene silencing|RNA-mediated gene silencing|gene silencing by RNA
description: A process in which an regulatory non-coding RNA molecule reduces expression of target genes. This can occur pre-transcriptionally by assembly of heterochromatin and prevention of transcription or co- or post-transcriptionally by targeting RNAs for degradation or by interfering with splicing or translation. This process starts once the inhibitory RNA molecule has been transcribed, and includes processing of the RNA such as cleavage, modifications, transport from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, loading onto the RISC complex, and the effect on transcription or translation.

description: A heterochromatin formation-based gene silencing process mediated by a regulatory non-coding RNA molecule that occur before the beginning of trancription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: primary miRNA processing
synonyms: pri-miRNA processing|primary miRNA methylation|primary miRNA modification|primary microRNA processing
description: A process involved in the conversion of a primary microRNA transcript into a pre-microRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pre-miRNA processing
description: A process involved in the conversion of a pre-microRNA transcript into a mature microRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hair follicle morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of the hair follicle are generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic camera-type eye development
description: The process occurring during the embryonic phase whose specific outcome is the progression of the eye over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: post-embryonic camera-type eye development
description: The process occurring during the post-embryonic phase whose specific outcome is the progression of the camera-type eye over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess

synonyms: deadenylation-independent decapping of nuclear mRNA|deadenylylation-independent decapping
description: Cleavage of the 5'-cap of a nuclear-transcribed mRNA that is independent of poly(A) tail shortening.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: stress-activated protein kinase signaling cascade
synonyms: JNK signaling pathway|JNK signalling pathway|SAPK signaling pathway|SAPK signalling pathway|stress-activated protein kinase signaling pathway|stress-activated protein kinase signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals in which a stress-activated protein kinase (SAPK) cascade relays a signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: animal organ regeneration
description: The regrowth of a lost or destroyed animal organ.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: axon regeneration
description: The regrowth of axons following their loss or damage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dendrite regeneration
description: The regrowth of dendrites in response to their loss or damage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: septin ring organization
description: Control of the formation, spatial distribution, and breakdown of the septin ring.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: microtubule polymerization or depolymerization
description: Assembly or disassembly of microtubules by the addition or removal of tubulin heterodimers from a microtubule.

label: BiologicalProcess

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glycoprotein transport
description: The directed movement of a glycoprotein, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipoprotein lipid oxidation
description: The modification of a lipoprotein by oxidation of the lipid group.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipid oxidation
description: The removal of one or more electrons from a lipid, with or without the concomitant removal of a proton or protons, by reaction with an electron-accepting substance, by addition of oxygen or by removal of hydrogen.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: plasma lipoprotein particle oxidation
description: The modification of a lipid or protein within a plasma lipoprotein particle by oxidation of the lipid or one or more amino acids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of plasma lipoprotein oxidation
synonyms: inhibition of plasma lipoprotein oxidation|negative regulation of plasma lipoprotein particle oxidation
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of lipoprotein particle oxidation, occurring in the blood plasma.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: substrate adhesion-dependent cell spreading
synonyms: cell spreading during cell substrate adhesion|substrate adhesion dependent cell spreading
description: The morphogenetic process that results in flattening of a cell as a consequence of its adhesion to a substrate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: very-low-density lipoprotein particle clearance
description: The process in which a very-low-density lipoprotein particle is removed from the blood via receptor-mediated endocytosis and its constituent parts degraded.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: microtubule anchoring
description: Any process in which a microtubule is maintained in a specific location in a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: microtubule anchoring at centrosome
description: Any process in which a microtubule is maintained in a specific location in a cell by attachment to a centrosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: small-subunit processome assembly
synonyms: SSU processome assembly|small subunit processome assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of proteins and RNA molecules to form a small-subunit processome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to carbon monoxide
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a carbon monoxide (CO) stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: snRNA 3'-end processing
description: Any process involved in forming the mature 3' end of an snRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: U1 snRNA 3'-end processing
description: Any process involved in forming the mature 3' end of a U1 snRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: U2 snRNA 3'-end processing
description: Any process involved in forming the mature 3' end of a U2 snRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: U4 snRNA 3'-end processing
description: Any process involved in forming the mature 3' end of a U4 snRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: U5 snRNA 3'-end processing
description: Any process involved in forming the mature 3' end of a U5 snRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: U6 snRNA 3'-end processing
description: Any process involved in forming the mature 3' end of a U6 snRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phosphatidylglycerol catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of phosphatidylglycerols, any of a class of glycerophospholipids in which the phosphatidyl group is esterified to the hydroxyl group of glycerol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vacuolar transmembrane transport
description: The process in which a solute is transported from one side of the vacuolar membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: basic amino acid transmembrane export from vacuole
description: The directed movement of basic amino acids out of the vacuole, across the vacuolar membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to phagophore assembly site
synonyms: protein localisation to phagophore assembly site|protein localization to PAS|protein localization to pre-autophagosomal structure
description: Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, the phagophore assembly site (PAS).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: early endosome to Golgi transport
synonyms: PGE to Golgi transport|post-Golgi endosome to Golgi transport
description: The directed movement of substances from early endosomes to the Golgi.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: late endosome to Golgi transport
synonyms: PVE to Golgi transport|prevacuolar endosome to Golgi transport
description: The directed movement of substances from late endosomes to the Golgi.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to kinetochore
synonyms: condensin localization to kinetochore|protein localisation to kinetochore
description: Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, the kinetochore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to chromosome
synonyms: condensin localization to chromosome|protein localisation to chromosome
description: Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, a specific location on a chromosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to nucleus
synonyms: protein localisation to nucleus|protein localization in cell nucleus|protein localization in nucleus|protein targeting to nucleus
description: A process in which a protein transports or maintains the localization of another protein to the nucleus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tooth mineralization
description: The process in which calcium salts are deposited into calcareous tooth structures such as dental enamel, dentin and cementum.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial unfolded protein response
description: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of the presence of unfolded proteins in the mitochondrial matrix; results in transcriptional upregulation of nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial stress proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to vitamin B6
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a vitamin B6 stimulus. Vitamin B6 encompasses pyridoxal, pyridoxamine and pyridoxine and the active form, pyridoxal phosphate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ribophagy
description: The selective degradation of mature ribosomes by macroautophagy.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form the cytochrome bc(1) complex (also known as ubiquinol-cytochrome c reductase), in the mitochondrial inner membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial respiratory chain complex II assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form respiratory chain complex II, in the mitochondrial inner membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: piRNA processing
synonyms: PIWI-associated RNA biogenesis|PIWI-associated RNA processing|Piwi-associated RNA biosynthetic process|Piwi-associated RNA metabolic process|piRNA biogenesis|piRNA biosynthetic process|piRNA metabolic process|piRNA metabolism
description: A process leading to the generation of a functional piRNA. piRNAs (Piwi-associated RNAs) are a class of 24- to 30-nucleotide RNAs derived from repeat or complex DNA sequence elements and processed by a Dicer-independent mechanism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hydroxyproline transport
description: The directed movement of hydroxyproline into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to oxidative stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of oxidative stress, a state often resulting from exposure to high levels of reactive oxygen species, e.g. superoxide anions, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and hydroxyl radicals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to heat
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a heat stimulus, a temperature stimulus above the optimal temperature for that organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to tumor necrosis factor
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a tumor necrosis factor stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to reactive oxygen species
synonyms: cellular response to AOS|cellular response to ROI|cellular response to ROS|cellular response to active oxygen species|cellular response to reactive oxidative species|cellular response to reactive oxygen intermediate
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a reactive oxygen species stimulus. Reactive oxygen species include singlet oxygen, superoxide, and oxygen free radicals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to laminar fluid shear stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a laminar fluid shear stress stimulus. Laminar fluid flow is the force acting on an object in a system where the fluid is moving across a solid surface in parallel layers. As an example, laminar shear stress can be seen where blood flows against the luminal side of blood vessel walls.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to unfolded protein
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an unfolded protein stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fatty acid elongation, monounsaturated fatty acid
description: Elongation of a fatty acid chain into which one C-C double bond has been introduced.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fatty acid elongation, polyunsaturated fatty acid
description: Elongation of a fatty acid chain into which two or more C-C double bonds have been introduced.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retinol transport
description: The directed movement of retinol into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Retinol is vitamin A1, 2,6,6-trimethyl-1-(9'-hydroxy-3',7'-dimethylnona-1',3',5',7'-tetraenyl)cyclohex-1-ene, one of the three components that makes up vitamin A.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glutathione transport
description: The directed movement of glutathione, the tripeptide glutamylcysteinylglycine, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phosphatidylcholine catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of phosphatidylcholines, any of a class of glycerophospholipids in which the phosphatidyl group is esterified to the hydroxyl group of choline.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to UV
synonyms: cellular response to UV light stimulus|cellular response to UV radiation stimulus|cellular response to ultraviolet light stimulus|cellular response to ultraviolet radiation stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an ultraviolet radiation (UV light) stimulus. Ultraviolet radiation is electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength in the range of 10 to 380 nanometers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cortisol metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving cortisol, the steroid hormone 11-beta-17,21-trihydroxypregn-4-ene-3,20-dione. Cortisol is synthesized from cholesterol in the adrenal gland and controls carbohydrate, fat and protein metabolism and has anti-inflammatory properties.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cortisol biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of cortisol, the steroid hormone 11-beta-17,21-trihydroxypregn-4-ene-3,20-dione. Cortisol is synthesized from cholesterol in the adrenal gland and controls carbohydrate, fat and protein metabolism and has anti-inflammatory properties.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retinoic acid catabolic process
synonyms: retinoic acid breakdown|retinoic acid catabolism|retinoic acid degradation|vitamin A1 acid catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of retinoic acid, one of the three components that makes up vitamin A.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nucleobase-containing small molecule catabolic process
synonyms: nucleobase|nucleoside and nucleotide breakdown|nucleobase|nucleoside and nucleotide catabolism|nucleobase|nucleoside and nucleotide degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a nucleobase-containing small molecule: a nucleobase, a nucleoside, or a nucleotide.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: chemotaxis to arachidonate
description: The directed movement of a motile cell or organism in response to the presence of arachidonic acid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to prostaglandin E
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a prostagladin E stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to prostaglandin F
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a prostagladin F stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to gonadotropin
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a gonadotropin stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to luteinizing hormone
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a luteinizing hormone stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: piecemeal microautophagy of the nucleus
description: Degradation of a cell nucleus by microautophagy.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nucleosome organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of one or more nucleosomes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: iron ion transmembrane transport
synonyms: ferrous ion transmembrane transport|ferrous iron transmembrane transport|high affinity ferrous ion transmembrane transport|high affinity iron ion transport|high-affinity ferrous ion transmembrane transport|high-affinity iron ion transmembrane transport|high-affinity iron ion transport|iron ion membrane transport|iron(2+) transmembrane transport|low affinity iron ion transport|low-affinity iron ion transmembrane transport|low-affinity iron ion transport|transmembrane iron transport
description: A process in which an iron ion is transported from one side of a membrane to the other by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of iron ion transport
synonyms: regulation of Fe transport|regulation of iron import|regulation of iron ion import|regulation of iron transport
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of iron ions (Fe) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of iron ion transport
synonyms: down regulation of iron ion transport|down-regulation of iron ion transport|downregulation of iron ion transport|inhibition of iron ion transport|negative regulation of iron transport
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of iron ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of transmembrane transport
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of a solute from one side of a membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of transmembrane transport
synonyms: down regulation of transmembrane transport|down-regulation of transmembrane transport|downregulation of transmembrane transport|inhibition of transmembrane transport|negative regulation of membrane transport
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of a solute from one side of a membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of monoatomic ion transmembrane transport
synonyms: regulation of ion membrane transport|regulation of ion transmembrane transport|regulation of transmembrane ion transport
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of ions from one side of a membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of monoatomic ion transmembrane transport
synonyms: down regulation of transmembrane ion transport|down-regulation of transmembrane ion transport|downregulation of transmembrane ion transport|inhibition of transmembrane ion transport|negative regulation of ion membrane transport|negative regulation of ion transmembrane transport|negative regulation of transmembrane ion transport
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of ions from one side of a membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of monoatomic ion transmembrane transport
synonyms: activation of transmembrane ion transport|positive regulation of ion membrane transport|positive regulation of ion transmembrane transport|positive regulation of transmembrane ion transport|stimulation of transmembrane ion transport|up regulation of transmembrane ion transport|up-regulation of transmembrane ion transport|upregulation of transmembrane ion transport
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of ions from one side of a membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: basement membrane disassembly
description: The controlled breakdown of the basement membrane in the context of a normal process such as imaginal disc eversion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glutathione transmembrane transport
description: A process in which glutathione is transported across a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to histamine
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a histamine stimulus. Histamine, the biogenic amine 2-(1H-imidazol-4-yl)ethanamine, is involved in local immune responses as well as regulating physiological function in the gut and acting as a neurotransmitter.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endothelin maturation
description: The process leading to the attainment of the full functional capacity of endothelin by conversion of Big-endothelin substrate into mature endothelin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein folding in endoplasmic reticulum
synonyms: oxidative protein folding|protein folding in ER
description: A protein folding process that takes place in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Secreted, plasma membrane and organelle proteins are folded in the ER, assisted by chaperones and foldases (protein disulphide isomerases), and additional factors required for optimal folding (ATP, Ca2+ and an oxidizing environment to allow disulfide bond formation).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to endoplasmic reticulum stress
synonyms: ER stress response|cellular response to endoplasmic reticulum stress|response to ER stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stress acting at the endoplasmic reticulum. ER stress usually results from the accumulation of unfolded or misfolded proteins in the ER lumen.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial protein processing
description: The peptide cleavage of mitochondrial proteins, including cleavage contributing to their import.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: peptidyl-lysine deacetylation
description: The removal of an acetyl group from an acetylated lysine residue in a peptide or protein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: somatic stem cell population maintenance
description: Any process by which an organism retains a population of somatic stem cells, undifferentiated cells in the embryo or adult which can undergo unlimited division and give rise to cell types of the body other than those of the germ-line.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of Rac protein signal transduction
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of Rac protein signal transduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of Rac protein signal transduction
synonyms: down regulation of Rac protein signal transduction|down-regulation of Rac protein signal transduction|downregulation of Rac protein signal transduction|inhibition of Rac protein signal transduction
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of Rac protein signal transduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of Rac protein signal transduction
synonyms: activation of Rac protein signal transduction|stimulation of Rac protein signal transduction|up regulation of Rac protein signal transduction|up-regulation of Rac protein signal transduction|upregulation of Rac protein signal transduction
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of Rac protein signal transduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of Rho protein signal transduction
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of Rho protein signal transduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of Rho protein signal transduction
synonyms: down regulation of Rho protein signal transduction|down-regulation of Rho protein signal transduction|downregulation of Rho protein signal transduction|inhibition of Rho protein signal transduction
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of Rho protein signal transduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of Rho protein signal transduction
synonyms: activation of Rho protein signal transduction|stimulation of Rho protein signal transduction|up regulation of Rho protein signal transduction|up-regulation of Rho protein signal transduction|upregulation of Rho protein signal transduction
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of Rho protein signal transduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: leading edge cell differentiation
description: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of leading edge cells, cells at the front of a migrating epithelial sheet.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sperm-egg recognition
description: The initial contact step made between the sperm plasma membrane and outer layer of the egg during fertilization.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic heart tube development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the embryonic heart tube over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The heart tube forms as the heart rudiment from the heart field.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cardiocyte differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a cell that will form part of the cardiac organ of an individual.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic heart tube anterior/posterior pattern specification
description: The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of cell differentiation that results in the anterior/posterior subdivision of the embryonic heart tube. In Drosophila this results in subdivision of the dorsal vessel into to the posterior heart proper and the anterior aorta.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear speck organization
synonyms: nuclear speck organisation|nuclear speck organization and biogenesis|nuclear speckle assembly|nuclear speckle organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of nuclear specks, a class of nuclear body in which splicing factors are localized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: axoneme assembly
synonyms: axoneme biogenesis|ciliary axoneme assembly|cilium axoneme assembly|cilium axoneme biogenesis|flagellar axoneme assembly|flagellum axoneme assembly
description: The assembly and organization of an axoneme, the bundle of microtubules and associated proteins that forms the core of cilia (also called flagella) in eukaryotic cells and is responsible for their movements.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment or maintenance of apical/basal cell polarity
description: Any cellular process that results in the specification, formation or maintenance polarization of a cell's architecture along its apical/basal axis so that the apical and basal regions of the cell have different membrane, extracellular matrix and sub-membrane cellular components.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment of apical/basal cell polarity
description: The specification and formation of the polarity of a cell along its apical/basal axis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sperm DNA condensation
synonyms: sperm chromatin condensation|spermatogenesis|exchange of chromosomal proteins
description: The progressive compaction of the spermatid chromatin so that it reaches a level of condensation that is not compatible with nuclear activities such as transcription or DNA replication.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to nicotine
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nicotine stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: behavioral response to nicotine
description: Any process that results in a change in the behavior of an organism as a result of a nicotine stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: operant conditioning
description: Learning to anticipate future events on the basis of past experience with the consequences of one's own behavior.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: limb morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of a limb are generated and organized. A limb is a paired appendage of a tetrapod used for locomotion or grasping.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: genitalia morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of genitalia are generated and organized. The genitalia are the organs of reproduction or generation, external and internal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic forelimb morphogenesis
description: The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the forelimb are generated and organized. The forelimbs are the front limbs of an animal, e.g. the arms of a human.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic hindlimb morphogenesis
description: The process, occurring in the embryo, by which the anatomical structures of the hindlimbs are generated and organized. The hindlimbs are the posterior limbs of an animal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: post-embryonic forelimb morphogenesis
description: The process, occurring after embryonic development, by which the anatomical structures of the forelimb are generated and organized. The forelimbs are the front limbs of an organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: forelimb morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of the forelimb are generated and organized. The forelimbs are the front limbs of an animal, e.g. the arms of a human.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hindlimb morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of the hindlimb are generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tube formation
synonyms: lumen formation in an anatomical structure|tube lumen formation
description: Creation of the central hole of a tube in an anatomical structure through which gases and/or liquids flow.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic hemopoiesis
description: The stages of blood cell formation that take place within the embryo.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: post-embryonic hemopoiesis
description: The stages of blood cell formation that take place after completion of embryonic development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: social behavior
description: Behavior directed towards society, or taking place between members of the same species. Occurs predominantly, or only, in individuals that are part of a group.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulatory ncRNA-mediated post-transcriptional gene silencing
synonyms: PTGS|RNA interference|RNA-dependent post-transcriptional gene silencing|RNA-mediated post-transcriptional gene silencing|RNA-mediated posttranscriptional gene silencing|RNAi|cosuppression|ncRNA-mediated post-transcriptional gene silencing|post-transcriptional gene silencing by RNA|posttranscriptional gene silencing by RNA|quelling
description: A posttranscriptional gene silencing pathway in which regulatory RNAs elicit silencing of specific target genes, either by mRNA destabilization or inhibition of translation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional gene silencing
synonyms: gene silencing by miRNA|gene silencing by microRNA|miRNA-mediated gene silencing|microRNA-mediated gene silencing
description: A post-transcriptional gene silencing pathway in which regulatory microRNAs (miRNAs) elicit silencing of specific target genes. miRNAs are endogenous 21-24 nucleotide small RNAs processed from stem-loop RNA precursors (pre-miRNAs). Once incorporated into a RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC), miRNAs can downregulate protein production by either of two posttranscriptional mechanisms: endonucleolytic cleavage of the RNA (often mRNA) or mRNA translational repression, usually accompanied by poly-A tail shortening and subsequent degradation of the mRNA. miRNAs are present in all the animals and in plants, whereas siRNAs are present in lower animals and in plants.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: miRNA processing
synonyms: gene silencing by miRNA|production of miRNAs|miRNA biogenesis|miRNA biosynthetic process|miRNA maturation|miRNA-mediated gene silencing|production of miRNAs|microRNA biogenesis|microRNA biosynthesis|microRNA biosynthetic process|microRNA metabolic process|microRNA metabolism|microRNA processing|microRNA-mediated gene silencing|production of microRNAs|production of miRNAs involved in gene silencing by miRNA|production of microRNAs involved in gene silencing by microRNA
description: A process leading to the generation of a functional miRNA. Includes the cleavage of stem-loop RNA precursors into microRNAs (miRNAs). miRNAs are a class of small RNAs that primarily silence genes by blocking the translation of mRNA transcripts into protein, or by increasing the degradation of non-protein-coding RNA transcripts.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell competition in a multicellular organism
description: Competitive interactions within multicellular organisms between cell populations that differ in growth rates, leading to the elimination of the slowest-growing cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ionotropic glutamate receptor signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by glutamate binding to a glutamate receptor on the surface of the target cell, followed by the movement of ions through a channel in the receptor complex, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vitamin A biosynthetic process
synonyms: vitamin A anabolism|vitamin A biosynthesis|vitamin A formation|vitamin A synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of any of the vitamin A compounds, retinol, retinal (retinaldehyde) and retinoic acid. Animals cannot synthesize vitamin A de novo, but form it through oxidative cleavage of carotenoids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic transmission, glutamatergic
description: The vesicular release of glutamate from a presynapse, across a chemical synapse, the subsequent activation of glutamate receptors at the postsynapse of a target cell (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) and the effects of this activation on the postsynaptic membrane potential and ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol. This process encompasses both spontaneous and evoked release of neurotransmitter and all parts of synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Evoked transmission starts with the arrival of an action potential at the presynapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: external genitalia morphogenesis
