synonyms: activation of cardiac muscle fiber development|positive regulation of cardiac muscle fibre development|positive regulation of heart muscle fiber development|stimulation of cardiac muscle fiber development|up regulation of cardiac muscle fiber development|up-regulation of cardiac muscle fiber development|upregulation of cardiac muscle fiber development
description: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle fiber development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle tissue development
synonyms: down regulation of cardiac muscle development|down-regulation of cardiac muscle development|downregulation of cardiac muscle development|inhibition of cardiac muscle development|negative regulation of heart muscle development
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle tissue development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anastral spindle assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form the spindle, the array of microtubules and associated molecules that serves to move duplicated chromosomes apart, in the absence of centrosomes. Formation is initiated by the nucleation of microtubules (MTs) in the vicinity of condensed chromatin. MTs then attach to and congress around the chromatin due to activity of microtubule motors. A bipolar spindle is formed by focusing of the terminal ends of the MT array into spindle poles by molecular motors and cross-linking proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: asymmetric neuroblast division
description: The process resulting in the physical partitioning and separation of a neuroblast into two daughter cells with different developmental potentials.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phosphate ion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of phosphate ions within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sulfate ion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of sulfate ions within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: chloride ion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of chloride ions within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: copper ion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of copper ions within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: manganese ion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of manganese ions within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: calcium ion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of calcium ions within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: potassium ion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of potassium ions within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sodium ion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of sodium ions within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: monoatomic cation homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of monoatomic cations within an organism or cell. Monatomic cations (also called simple cations) are cations consisting of exactly one atom.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: monoatomic anion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of monoatomic anions within an organism or cell. Monatomic anions (also called simple anions) are anions consisting of exactly one atom.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: transmembrane transport
synonyms: ATP hydrolysis coupled transmembrane transport|membrane transport
description: The process in which a solute is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nucleobase-containing small molecule metabolic process
synonyms: nucleobase|nucleoside and nucleotide metabolic process|nucleobase|nucleoside and nucleotide metabolism
description: The cellular chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleobase-containing small molecule: a nucleobase, a nucleoside, or a nucleotide.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipid homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of lipid within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fatty acid homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of fatty acid within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: acylglycerol homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of acylglycerol within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phospholipid homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of phospholipid within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sterol homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of sterol within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to hyperoxia
synonyms: response to hyperoxic stress|response to increased oxygen tension
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating increased oxygen tension.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: low-density lipoprotein particle mediated signaling
synonyms: low-density lipoprotein mediated signalling|low-density lipoprotein particle mediated signal transduction|low-density lipoprotein particle-mediated signaling
description: The series of molecular signals mediated by the detection of low-density lipoprotein particle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: high density lipoprotein particle mediated signaling
synonyms: high density lipoprotein mediated signalling|high density lipoprotein particle mediated signal transduction|high density lipoprotein particle-mediated signaling
description: The series of molecular signals mediated by the detection of high density lipoprotein particle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Golgi to secretory granule transport
description: The directed movement of proteins from the Golgi to a secretory granule. The secretory granule is a membrane-bounded particle, usually protein, formed in the granular endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi complex.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ingression involved in gastrulation with mouth forming second
description: The migration of individual cells into the embryo involved in deuterostomic gastrulation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: epiboly involved in gastrulation with mouth forming second
description: The expansion of one cell sheet over other cells involved in deuterostomic gastrulation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cardiac muscle contraction
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle contraction
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: relaxation of cardiac muscle
description: The process in which the extent of cardiac muscle contraction is reduced.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: digestive system development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the digestive system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The digestive system is the entire structure in which digestion takes place. Digestion is all of the physical, chemical, and biochemical processes carried out by multicellular organisms to break down ingested nutrients into components that may be easily absorbed and directed into metabolism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-proline biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of L-proline, an L-enantiomer of a chiral, cyclic, nonessential alpha-amino acid found in peptide linkage in proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: D-alanine catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of D-alanine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: copper ion export
description: The directed movement of copper ions out of a cell or organelle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: reflex
description: An automatic response to a stimulus beginning with a nerve impulse from a receptor and ending with the action of an effector such as a gland or a muscle. Signaling never reaches a level of consciousness.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vestibular reflex
description: A reflex process in which a response to an angular or linear acceleration stimulus begins with an afferent nerve impulse from a receptor in the inner ear and ends with the compensatory action of eye muscles. Signaling never reaches a level of consciousness.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Sertoli cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a Sertoli cell. A Sertoli cell is a supporting cell projecting inward from the basement membrane of seminiferous tubules.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Sertoli cell development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a Sertoli cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a Sertoli cell fate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Sertoli cell fate commitment
description: The process in which the cellular identity of Sertoli cells is acquired and determined.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic transmission, glycinergic
description: The vesicular release of glycine from a presynapse, across a chemical synapse, the subsequent activation of glycine receptors at the postsynapse of a target cell (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) and the effects of this activation on the postsynaptic membrane potential and ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol. This process encompasses both spontaneous and evoked release of neurotransmitter and all parts of synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Evoked transmission starts with the arrival of an action potential at the presynapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: righting reflex
description: A reflex process in which an animal immediately tries to turn over after being placed in a supine position.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: parathyroid gland development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the parathyroid gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The parathyroid gland is an organ specialised for secretion of parathyroid hormone.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: radial glial cell differentiation
description: The process in which neuroepithelial cells of the neural tube give rise to radial glial cells, specialized bipotential progenitors cells of the brain. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: roof of mouth development
description: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of the roof of the mouth from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the structure and ends with the mature structure. The roof of the mouth is the partition that separates the nasal and oral cavities.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hard palate development
description: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of the hard palate from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the structure and ends with the mature structure, whatever form that may be including its natural destruction. The hard palate is the anterior portion of the palate consisting of bone and mucous membranes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: soft palate development
description: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of the soft palate from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the structure and ends with the mature structure, whatever form that may be including its natural destruction. The soft palate is the posterior portion of the palate extending from the posterior edge of the hard palate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: rhythmic synaptic transmission
description: Any process involved in the generation of rhythmic, synchronous synaptic inputs in a neural circuit.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of synaptic activity
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of synaptic activity, the controlled release of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft and their subsequent detection by a postsynaptic cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: convergent extension
description: The morphogenetic process in which an epithelium narrows along one axis and lengthens in a perpendicular axis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: convergent extension involved in gastrulation
description: The morphogenetic process in which an epithelium narrows along one axis and lengthens in a perpendicular axis usually resulting in the formation of the three primary germ layers, ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pharyngeal system development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the pharyngeal system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The pharyngeal system is a transient embryonic complex that is specific to vertebrates. It comprises the pharyngeal arches, bulges of tissues of mesoderm and neural crest derivation through which pass nerves and pharyngeal arch arteries. The arches are separated internally by pharyngeal pouches, evaginations of foregut endoderm, and externally by pharyngeal clefts, invaginations of surface ectoderm. The development of the system ends when the structure it contributes to are forming: the thymus, thyroid, parathyroids, maxilla, mandible, aortic arch, cardiac outflow tract, external and middle ear.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cardiac muscle cell proliferation
synonyms: cardiac myocyte proliferation|cardiomyocyte proliferation|heart muscle cell proliferation
description: The expansion of a cardiac muscle cell population by cell division.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pericardium development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the pericardium over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The pericardium is a double-walled sac that contains the heart and the roots of the aorta, vena cava and the pulmonary artery.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retinal bipolar neuron differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a bipolar cell, the last neuron to be generated in the retina.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retina development in camera-type eye
synonyms: retina development in camera-style eye|retinal development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the retina over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The retina is the innermost layer or coating at the back of the eyeball, which is sensitive to light and in which the optic nerve terminates.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retina morphogenesis in camera-type eye
description: The process in which the anatomical structure of the retina is generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cardiac muscle cell proliferation
synonyms: regulation of cardiomyocyte proliferation|regulation of heart muscle cell proliferation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle cell proliferation
synonyms: negative regulation of heart muscle cell proliferation
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of cardiac muscle cell proliferation
synonyms: positive regulation of heart muscle cell proliferation
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of acrosome reaction
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the acrosome reaction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: heart contraction
description: The multicellular organismal process in which the heart decreases in volume in a characteristic way to propel blood through the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cardiac muscle contraction
description: Muscle contraction of cardiac muscle tissue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neurofilament cytoskeleton organization
synonyms: neurofilament cytoskeleton organisation|neurofilament cytoskeleton organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising neurofilaments and their associated proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of epithelial cell proliferation involved in wound healing
description: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of epithelial cell proliferation, contributing to the restoration of integrity to a damaged tissue following an injury.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: angiogenesis involved in wound healing
description: Blood vessel formation when new vessels emerge from the proliferation of pre-existing blood vessels and contribute to the series of events that restore integrity to a damaged tissue, following an injury.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mammary gland involution
description: The tissue remodeling that removes differentiated mammary epithelia during weaning.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of apoptotic process involved in mammary gland involution
synonyms: positive regulation of apoptosis involved in mammary gland involution
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cell death by apoptotic process of mammary epithelial cells during mammary gland involution.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic retina morphogenesis in camera-type eye
description: The process in which the anatomical structure of the retina is generated and organized in a camera-type eye during the embryonic life stage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Spemann organizer formation
description: Formation of the specialized region on the dorsalmost side of the embryo that acts as the main signaling center establishing the vertebrate body plan.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: uterus development
description: The reproductive developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of the uterus over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: oviduct development
description: The reproductive developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of an oviduct over time, from its formation to the mature structure. An oviduct is a tube through which an ova passes from the ovary to the uterus, or from the ovary to the outside of the organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cervix development
description: The reproductive developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cervix over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vagina development
description: The reproductive developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of the vagina over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: canonical Wnt signaling pathway
synonyms: Wnt receptor signaling pathway through beta-catenin|Wnt receptor signaling pathway via beta-catenin|Wnt receptor signalling pathway through beta-catenin|canonical Wnt receptor signaling pathway|canonical Wnt-activated signaling pathway|frizzled-1 receptor signaling pathway
description: A type of Wnt signaling pathway in which Wnt binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell results in the by propagation of the molecular signals via beta-catenin, and end with a change in transcription of target genes. In this pathway, the activated receptor signals via downstream effectors that result in the inhibition of beta-catenin phosphorylation, thereby preventing degradation of beta-catenin. Stabilized beta-catenin can then accumulate and travel to the nucleus to trigger changes in transcription of target genes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: Wnt signaling pathway, planar cell polarity pathway
synonyms: PCP pathway|Wnt receptor signaling pathway|planar cell polarity pathway|Wnt receptor signalling pathway|planar cell polarity pathway|Wnt-JNK signaling pathway|Wnt-PCP signaling pathway|Wnt-activated signaling pathway|planar cell polarity pathway|non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway|planar cell polarity pathway
description: A type of non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway in which Wnt binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell results in the activation small G proteins such as Rho, Rac, and Cdc42 which, in turn activate effectors, including C-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and Rho kinase (Rok). The signaling ends with change in the transcription of target genes and/or reorganisation of the cytoskeleton.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: micturition
description: The regulation of body fluids process in which parasympathetic nerves stimulate the bladder wall muscle to contract and expel urine from the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synapse maturation
description: The process that organizes a synapse so that it attains its fully functional state. Synaptic maturation plays a critical role in the establishment of effective synaptic connections in early development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of resting membrane potential
description: Any process that modulates the establishment or extent of a resting potential, the electrical charge across the plasma membrane, with the interior of the cell negative with respect to the exterior. The resting potential is the membrane potential of a cell that is not stimulated to be depolarized or hyperpolarized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential
description: Any process that modulates the potential difference across a post-synaptic membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: excitatory postsynaptic potential
synonyms: regulation of EPSP|regulation of excitatory post-synaptic membrane potential
description: A process that leads to a temporary increase in postsynaptic potential due to the flow of positively charged ions into the postsynaptic cell. The flow of ions that causes an EPSP is an excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) and makes it easier for the neuron to fire an action potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: inhibitory postsynaptic potential
synonyms: IPSP|regulation of inhibitory post-synaptic membrane potential
description: A process that causes a temporary decrease in postsynaptic membrane potential due to the flow of negatively charged ions into the postsynaptic cell. The flow of ions that causes an IPSP is an inhibitory postsynaptic current (IPSC) and makes it more difficult for the neuron to fire an action potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: membrane hyperpolarization
description: The process in which membrane potential increases with respect to its steady-state potential, usually from negative potential to a more negative potential. For example, during the repolarization phase of an action potential the membrane potential often becomes more negative or hyperpolarized before returning to the steady-state resting potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: smooth muscle contraction involved in micturition
synonyms: smooth muscle contraction involved in urination|urinary bladder smooth muscle contraction involved in micturition
description: The process leading to shortening and/or development of tension in the urinary bladder smooth muscle tissue involved in the expulsion urine from the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic transmission involved in micturition
description: The process of communication from a neuron to a smooth muscle in the bladder that contributes to the expulsion of urine from the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: circadian temperature homeostasis
synonyms: circadian regulation of body temperature|circadian thermoregulation
description: Any homeostatic process in which an organism modulates its internal body temperature at different values with a regularity of approximately 24 hours.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: relaxation of vascular associated smooth muscle
synonyms: negative regulation of relaxation of vascular smooth muscle|positive regulation of relaxation of vascular smooth muscle|regulation of relaxation of vascular smooth muscle|relaxation of vascular smooth muscle|vascular smooth muscle relaxation
description: A negative regulation of smooth muscle contraction resulting in relaxation of vascular smooth muscle. The relaxation is mediated by a decrease in the phosphorylation state of myosin light chain. This can be achieved by removal of calcium from the cytoplasm to the sarcoplasmic reticulum lumen through the action of Ca2+ ATPases leading to a decrease myosin light chain kinase activity, and through calcium-independent pathways leading to a increase in myosin light chain phosphatase activity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: auditory receptor cell stereocilium organization
synonyms: auditory receptor cell stereocilium organisation|auditory receptor cell stereocilium organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a stereocilium. A stereocilium is an actin-based protrusion from the apical surface of auditory hair cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of synaptic transmission, glycinergic
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of glycinergic synaptic transmission. Glycinergic synaptic transmission is the process of communication from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse using the neurotransmitter glycine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of synaptic transmission, glycinergic
synonyms: positive regulation of glycinergic synaptic transmission
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of glycinergic synaptic transmission. Glycinergic synaptic transmission is the process of communication from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse using the neurotransmitter glycine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of phagocytosis, engulfment
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the internalization of bacteria, immune complexes and other particulate matter or of an apoptotic cell by phagocytosis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of phagocytosis, engulfment
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the internalization of bacteria, immune complexes and other particulate matter or of an apoptotic cell by phagocytosis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: inner ear receptor cell differentiation
description: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells, acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of inner ear receptor cells. Inner ear receptor cells are mechanorecptors found in the inner ear responsible for transducing signals involved in balance and sensory perception of sound.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: auditory receptor cell development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an auditory receptor cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vestibular receptor cell development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a vestibular receptor cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: inner ear receptor cell development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an inner ear receptor cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vestibular receptor cell stereocilium organization
synonyms: vestibular hair cell stereocilium organization|vestibular receptor cell stereocilium organisation|vestibular receptor cell stereocilium organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a stereocilium. A stereocilium is an actin-based protrusion from the apical surface of vestibular hair cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: inner ear receptor cell stereocilium organization
synonyms: inner ear hair cell receptor stereocilium organization|inner ear receptor stereocilium organisation|inner ear receptor stereocilium organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a stereocilium. A stereocilium is an actin-based protrusion from the apical surface of inner ear receptor cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of growth hormone secretion
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of growth hormone from a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of growth hormone secretion
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of growth hormone from a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: somatotropin secreting cell differentiation
synonyms: growth hormone secreting cell differentiation|somatotrope differentiation|somatotroph differentiation|somatotrophin secreting cell differentiation|somatotropic cell differentiation|somatrophic cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a somatotropin secreting cell. A somatotropin secreting cell is an acidophilic cell of the anterior pituitary that produces growth hormone, somatotropin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: prolactin secreting cell differentiation
synonyms: epsilon-acidophil differentiation|lactotrope differentiation|lactotroph differentiation|lactotropic cell differentiation|mammotrope differentiation|mammotroph differentiation|mammotrophic cell differentiation|mammotropic cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a prolactin secreting cell. A prolactin secreting cell is an acidophilic cell of the anterior pituitary that produces prolactin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: corticotropin hormone secreting cell differentiation
synonyms: adrenocorticotrophic hormone secreting cell differentiation|adrenocorticotropic hormone secreting cell differentiation|corticotrope differentiation|corticotroph differentiation|corticotrophin hormone secreting cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a corticotropic hormone secreting cell. An corticotropic hormone secreting cell is a basophil cell of the anterior pituitary that produces corticotropin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting cell differentiation
synonyms: TSH-secreting cell differentiation|beta-basophil differentiation|thyroid stimulating hormone secreting cell differentiation|thyrotrope differentiation|thyrotroph differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting cell. A thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting cell is a basophil cell of the anterior pituitary that produces thyroid-stimulating hormone, thyrotrophin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: prepulse inhibition
description: The process in which a startle magnitude is reduced when the startling stimulus is preceded by a low-intensity prepulse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: maternal process involved in female pregnancy
description: A reproductive process occurring in the mother that allows an embryo or fetus to develop within it.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic process involved in female pregnancy
description: A reproductive process occurring in the embryo or fetus that allows the embryo or fetus to develop within the mother.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: maternal process involved in parturition
description: A reproductive process occurring in the mother that results in birth.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fetal process involved in parturition
description: A reproductive process occurring in the fetus that results in birth.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of syncytium formation by plasma membrane fusion
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the formation of a syncytium, a mass of cytoplasm containing several nuclei enclosed within a single plasma membrane, by the fusion of the plasma membranes of two or more individual cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of post-transcriptional gene silencing
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the inactivation of gene expression by a posttranscriptional mechanism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: microtubule-based peroxisome localization
description: The microtubule-based process in which a peroxisome is transported to, and/or maintained in, a specific location. A peroxisome is a small membrane-bounded organelle that uses dioxygen (O2) to oxidize organic molecules.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: platelet dense granule organization
synonyms: bull\'s eye body organization and biogenesis|platelet dense body organization and biogenesis|platelet dense granule organisation|platelet dense granule organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a platelet dense granule. A platelet dense granule is an electron-dense granule occurring in blood platelets that stores and secretes adenosine nucleotides and serotonin. They contain a highly condensed core consisting of serotonin, histamine, calcium, magnesium, ATP, ADP, pyrophosphate and membrane lysosomal proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: milk ejection reflex
description: A reflex that occurs in response to suckling, beginning with a nerve impulse from a receptor in the mammary gland and ending with the ejection of milk from the gland. Signaling never reaches a level of consciousness.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: urinary bladder development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the urinary bladder over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The urinary bladder is an elastic, muscular sac situated in the anterior part of the pelvic cavity in which urine collects before excretion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phospholipase C-activating dopamine receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: activation of phospholipase C activity by dopamine receptor signaling pathway|activation of phospholipase C activity by dopamine receptor signalling pathway|dopamine receptor|phospholipase C activating pathway
description: A phospholipase C-activating receptor G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by dopamine binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of dopamine receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of dopamine receptor signalling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a dopamine receptor signaling pathway activity. A dopamine receptor signaling pathway is the series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of a dopamine receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of dopamine receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: negative regulation of dopamine receptor signalling pathway
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of dopamine receptor protein signaling pathway activity. A dopamine receptor signaling pathway is the series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of a dopamine receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of dopamine receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: positive regulation of dopamine receptor signalling pathway
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the dopamine receptor protein signaling pathway. A dopamine receptor signaling pathway is the series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of a dopamine receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of adenosine receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: positive regulation of adenosine receptor signalling pathway
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the adenosine receptor signaling pathway. The adenosine receptor pathway is the series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of an adenosine receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of adenosine receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: negative regulation of adenosine receptor signalling pathway
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the adenosine receptor signaling pathway. The adenosine receptor pathway is the series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of an adenosine receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: limb development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a limb over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A limb is an appendage of an animal used for locomotion or grasping. Examples include legs, arms or some types of fin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: limb bud formation
description: The process pertaining to the initial formation of a limb bud from unspecified parts. This process begins with the formation of a local condensation of mesenchyme cells within the prospective limb field, and ends when a limb bud is recognizable.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of angiotensin metabolic process
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving angiotensin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of exocyst localization
description: Any process that modulates the localization of exocysts. An exocyst is a protein complex peripherally associated with the plasma membrane that determines where vesicles dock and fuse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: male mating behavior
description: The specific behavior of a male organism that is associated with reproduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: female mating behavior
description: The specific behavior of a female organism that is associated with reproduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: apelin receptor signaling pathway
description: A G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by apelin binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of lipase activity
description: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of lipase activity, the hydrolysis of a lipid or phospholipid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of lipase activity
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of lipase activity, the hydrolysis of a lipid or phospholipid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cloacal septation
description: The separation of the single opening of the digestive, urinary, and reproductive tracts, the cloaca, into multiple isolated openings during development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of nuclear-transcribed mRNA poly(A) tail shortening
synonyms: negative regulation of 3\' to 5\' mRNA deadenylation|negative regulation of mRNA deadenylation|negative regulation of nuclear mRNA poly(A) tail shortening
description: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of poly(A) tail shortening of a nuclear-transcribed mRNA. Poly(A) tail shortening is the decrease in length of the poly(A) tail of an mRNA from full length to an oligo(A) length.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of nuclear-transcribed mRNA poly(A) tail shortening
synonyms: positive regulation of 3\' to 5\' mRNA deadenylation|positive regulation of mRNA deadenylation|positive regulation of nuclear mRNA poly(A) tail shortening
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of poly(A) tail shortening of a nuclear-transcribed mRNA. Poly(A) tail shortening is the decrease in length of the poly(A) tail of an mRNA from full length to an oligo(A) length.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endocardium formation
description: Formation of the endocardium of the heart. The endocardium is an anatomical structure comprised of an endothelium and an extracellular matrix that forms the innermost layer of tissue of the heart, and lines the heart chambers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: primitive hemopoiesis
description: A first transient wave of blood cell production that, in vertebrates, gives rise to erythrocytes (red blood cells) and myeloid cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: definitive hemopoiesis
description: A second wave of blood cell production that, in vertebrates, generates long-term hemopoietic stem cells that continuously provide erythroid, myeloid and lymphoid lineages throughout adulthood.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hematopoietic stem cell differentiation
synonyms: haematopoietic stem cell differentiation|haemopoietic stem cell differentiation|hemopoietic stem cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a hematopoietic stem cell. A stem cell is a cell that retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: camera-type eye photoreceptor cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a photoreceptor cell in a camera-type eye.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retinal rod cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a retinal rod cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mesenchymal to epithelial transition
synonyms: epithelial cell differentiation from mesenchymal cell|mesenchymal-epithelial transition
description: A transition where a mesenchymal cell establishes apical/basolateral polarity, forms intercellular adhesive junctions, synthesizes basement membrane components and becomes an epithelial cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: delamination
description: The process of negative regulation of cell adhesion that results in a cell or sheet of cells splitting off from an existing epithelial sheet.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuroblast delamination
description: The negative regulation of cell adhesion process in which a neuroblast splits off of a neurectodermal sheet.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lens induction in camera-type eye
description: Signaling at short range between the head ectoderm and the optic vesicle that results in the head ectoderm forming a lens.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of mitotic spindle organization
synonyms: regulation of mitotic spindle organisation|regulation of mitotic spindle organization and biogenesis
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the microtubule spindle during a mitotic cell cycle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: contact inhibition
synonyms: detection of cell density by contact stimulus|detection of cell density by contact stimulus involved in contact inhibition
description: The series of events in which information about the density of cells in a population is received by direct cell-cell contact and is converted into a molecular signal, resulting in the cessation of cell growth or proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cell growth involved in contact inhibition
description: The negative regulation of cell growth in response to increased cell density.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cell proliferation involved in contact inhibition
description: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the rate or extent of cell proliferation in response to cell density.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: detection of cell density
description: The series of events in which information about the density of cells in a population is received and converted into a molecular signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of glial cell proliferation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of glial cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of glial cell proliferation
description: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of glial cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of glial cell proliferation
description: Any process that stops or decreases the rate or extent of glial cell proliferation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of feeding behavior
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the behavior associated with the intake of food.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of transcription initiation by RNA polymerase II
synonyms: regulation of transcription initiation from RNA polymerase II promoter
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of a process involved in starting transcription from an RNA polymerase II promoter.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of transcription initiation by RNA polymerase II
synonyms: positive regulation of transcription initiation from RNA polymerase II promoter
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of a process involved in starting transcription from an RNA polymerase II promoter.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of N-terminal protein palmitoylation
description: Any process that decreases the rate frequency or extent of the covalent attachment of a palmitoyl group to the N-terminal amino acid residue of a protein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of respiratory burst
description: Any process that modulates the rate frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of respiratory burst involved in inflammatory response
synonyms: regulation of respiratory burst involved in acute inflammatory response
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases made as a defense response ; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of respiratory burst involved in inflammatory response
synonyms: positive regulation of respiratory burst involved in acute inflammatory response
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases made as a defense response ; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of respiratory burst involved in inflammatory response
synonyms: negative regulation of respiratory burst involved in acute inflammatory response
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases made as a defense response ; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of respiratory burst
description: Any process that increases the rate frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cilium assembly
synonyms: ciliogenesis|cilium biogenesis|cilium formation|cilium morphogenesis|cilium organization|microtubule-based flagellum assembly
description: The assembly of a cilium, a specialized eukaryotic organelle that consists of a filiform extrusion of the cell surface. Each cilium is bounded by an extrusion of the cytoplasmic membrane, and contains a regular longitudinal array of microtubules, anchored basally in a centriole.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic skeletal joint morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of skeletal joints are generated and organized during the embryonic phase. A skeletal joint is the connecting structure between the bones of the skeleton.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of ovulation
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of ovulation, the release of a mature ovum/oocyte from an ovary.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of oocyte development
description: Any process that decreases the rate or extent of the process whose specific outcome is the progression of an oocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cell development
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the progression of the cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cilium-dependent cell motility
synonyms: ciliary cell motility|cilium cell motility|microtubule-based flagellar cell motility
description: Cell motility due to the motion of one or more eukaryotic cilia. A eukaryotic cilium is a specialized organelle that consists of a filiform extrusion of the cell surface. Each cilium is bounded by an extrusion of the cytoplasmic (plasma) membrane, and contains a regular longitudinal array of microtubules, anchored basally in a centriole.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: epithelial cilium movement involved in determination of left/right asymmetry
synonyms: Kuppfer\'s vesicle cilium movement involved in determination of left/right asymmetry|cilium movement involved in determinationof L/R asymmetry|nodal cilium movement involved in determination of left/right asymmetry
description: The movement of cilia of epithelial cells of the Left Right Organizer (LRO), also referred to as the node in mouse or the Kupffer's vesicle in zebrafish, resulting in the leftward fluid flow across the LRO and generation or transport of a signal which determines asymmetry in an organism's body plan with respect to the left and right halves.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: transdifferentiation
description: The conversion of a differentiated cell of one fate into a differentiated cell of another fate without first undergoing cell division or reversion to a more primitive or stem cell-like fate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: long-term synaptic potentiation
description: A process that modulates synaptic plasticity such that synapses are changed resulting in the increase in the rate, or frequency of synaptic transmission at the synapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: long-term synaptic depression
synonyms: LTD|long term depression|long term synaptic depression
description: A process that modulates synaptic plasticity such that synapses are changed resulting in the decrease in the rate, or frequency of synaptic transmission at the synapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cilium movement involved in cell motility
description: Movement of cilia mediated by motor proteins that contributes to the movement of a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cilium beat frequency involved in ciliary motility
description: Any process that modulates the frequency of cilium beating involved in ciliary motility.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of sarcomere organization
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of myofibril assembly by organization of muscle actomyosin into sarcomeres. The sarcomere is the repeating unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z discs.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of sarcomere organization
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of myofibril assembly by organization of muscle actomyosin into sarcomeres. The sarcomere is the repeating unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z discs.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of sarcomere organization
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of myofibril assembly by organization of muscle actomyosin into sarcomeres. The sarcomere is the repeating unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z discs.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cytokine activity
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the activity of a molecule that controls the survival, growth, differentiation and effector function of tissues and cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cytokine activity
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of the activity of a molecule that controls the survival, growth, differentiation and effector function of tissues and cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of phosphatidylinositol dephosphorylation
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reaction involving the removal of one or more phosphate groups from a phosphatidylinositol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cell diameter
description: Any process that modulates the diameter of a cell, the length of a line segment that crosses through the center of a circular section through a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of membrane repolarization
description: Any process that modulates the establishment or extent of a membrane potential in the polarizing direction towards the resting potential, usually from positive to negative.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of ventricular cardiac muscle cell membrane repolarization
synonyms: electrocardiogram T wave|regulation of ventricular cardiac muscle cell repolarization|regulation of ventricular cardiac muscle repolarization|regulation of ventricular cardiomyocyte membrane repolarization|ventricular repolarization
description: Any process that modulates the establishment or extent of a membrane potential in the polarizing direction towards the resting potential in a ventricular cardiomyocyte.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: elastin catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of elastin. Elastin is a glycoprotein which is randomly coiled and crosslinked to form elastic fibers that are found in connective tissue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of elastin catabolic process
synonyms: down-regulation of elastin catabolic process|negative regulation of elastin breakdown|negative regulation of elastin catabolism|negative regulation of elastin degradation
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of elastin catabolism, the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of elastin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of blood vessel remodeling
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of blood vessel remodeling, the reorganization or renovation of existing blood vessels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of blood vessel remodeling
synonyms: down-regulation of blood vessel remodeling|inhibition of blood vessel remodeling|negative regulation of blood vessel remodelling
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of blood vessel remodeling, the reorganization or renovation of existing blood vessels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of ryanodine-sensitive calcium-release channel activity
description: Any process that modulates the activity of a ryanodine-sensitive calcium-release channel. The ryanodine-sensitive calcium-release channel catalyzes the transmembrane transfer of a calcium ion by a channel that opens when a ryanodine class ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of ryanodine-sensitive calcium-release channel activity
description: Any process that decreases the activity of a ryanodine-sensitive calcium-release channel. The ryanodine-sensitive calcium-release channel catalyzes the transmembrane transfer of a calcium ion by a channel that opens when a ryanodine class ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cardiac epithelial to mesenchymal transition
description: A transition where a cardiac epithelial cell loses apical/basolateral polarity, severs intercellular adhesive junctions, degrades basement membrane components and becomes a migratory mesenchymal cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: definitive erythrocyte differentiation
synonyms: definitive RBC differentiation|definitive erythropoiesis|definitive red blood cell differentiation
description: Erythrocyte differentiation which occurs as part of the process of definitive hemopoiesis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: primitive erythrocyte differentiation
synonyms: primitive RBC differentiation|primitive erythropoiesis|primitive red blood cell differentiation
description: Erythrocyte differentiation which occurs as part of the process of primitive hemopoiesis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: head development
description: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a head from an initial condition to its mature state. The head is the anterior-most division of the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: head morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of the head are generated and organized. The head is the anterior-most division of the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: face development
description: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a face from an initial condition to its mature state. The face is the ventral division of the head.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: face morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of the face are generated and organized. The face is the ventral division of the head.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell chemotaxis
description: The directed movement of a motile cell guided by a specific chemical concentration gradient. Movement may be towards a higher concentration (positive chemotaxis) or towards a lower concentration (negative chemotaxis).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cytoplasmic actin-based contraction involved in cell motility
description: The actin filament-based movement by which cytoplasmic actin filaments slide past one another resulting in a contraction that propels the cell from one place to another.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of response to type II interferon
synonyms: regulation of response to gamma-interferon|regulation of response to immune interferon|regulation of response to interferon-gamma|regulation of response to type II IFN
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of a response to type II interferon (interferon-gamma). Response to interferon gamma is a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an interferon-gamma stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: type II interferon-mediated signaling pathway
synonyms: gamma-interferon-mediated signaling pathway|immune interferon signaling pathway|interferon-gamma-mediated signaling pathway|interferon-gamma-mediated signalling pathway|type II IFN-mediated signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by interferon-gamma binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription. Interferon gamma is the only member of the type II interferon found so far.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of type II interferon-mediated signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of gamma-interferon-mediated signaling pathway|regulation of immune interferon signaling pathway|regulation of interferon-gamma-mediated signaling pathway|regulation of interferon-gamma-mediated signalling pathway|regulation of type II IFN-mediated signaling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of an interferon-gamma-mediated signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of type II interferon-mediated signaling pathway
synonyms: positive regulation of gamma-interferon-mediated signaling pathway|positive regulation of immune interferon-mediated signaling pathway|positive regulation of interferon-gamma-mediated signaling pathway|positive regulation of interferon-gamma-mediated signalling pathway|positive regulation of type II IFN-mediated pathway
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of an interferon-gamma-mediated signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of type II interferon-mediated signaling pathway
synonyms: negative regulation of gamma-interferon-mediated signaling pathway|negative regulation of immune interferon-mediated signaling pathway|negative regulation of interferon-gamma-mediated signaling pathway|negative regulation of interferon-gamma-mediated signalling pathway|negative regulation of type II IFN-mediated signaling pathway
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of an interferon-gamma-mediated signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: type I interferon-mediated signaling pathway
synonyms: type I interferon signaling pathway|type I interferon-activated signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by type I interferon binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription. Type I interferons include the interferon-alpha, beta, delta, episilon, zeta, kappa, tau, and omega gene families.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of type I interferon-mediated signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of type I interferon-mediated signalling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of a type I interferon-mediated signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of type I interferon-mediated signaling pathway
synonyms: negative regulation of type I interferon-mediated signalling pathway
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of a type I interferon-mediated signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of type I interferon-mediated signaling pathway
synonyms: positive regulation of type I interferon-mediated signalling pathway
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of a type I interferon-mediated signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cellular localization
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a process in which a cell, a substance, or a cellular entity is transported to, or maintained in a specific location within or in the membrane of a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bone trabecula formation
synonyms: bone trabecula biogenesis|bone trabeculation|skeletal trabecula biogenesis|skeletal trabecula formation|skeletal trabeculation
description: The process of creating a trabecula in the bone. A trabecula is a tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: heart trabecula formation
synonyms: cardiac trabecula formation|cardiac trabeculation|heart trabecula biogenesis|heart trabeculation
description: The process of creating a trabecula in the heart. A trabecula is a tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bone development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of bone over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Bone is the hard skeletal connective tissue consisting of both mineral and cellular components.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bone morphogenesis
description: The process in which bones are generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endochondral bone morphogenesis
description: The process in which bones are generated and organized as a result of the conversion of initial cartilaginous anlage into bone.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cartilage development involved in endochondral bone morphogenesis
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cartilage that will provide a scaffold for mineralization of endochondral bones.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell adhesion molecule production
description: The appearance of a cell adhesion molecule due to biosynthesis or secretion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cell adhesion molecule production
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of cell adhesion molecule production. Cell adhesion molecule production is the appearance of a cell adhesion molecule as a result of its biosynthesis or a decrease in its catabolism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cell adhesion molecule production
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of cell adhesion molecule production. Cell adhesion molecule production is the appearance of a cell adhesion molecule as a result of its biosynthesis or a decrease in its catabolism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of cell adhesion molecule production
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of cell adhesion molecule production. Cell adhesion molecule production is the appearance of a cell adhesion molecule as a result of its biosynthesis or a decrease in its catabolism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to ammonium ion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an ammonium stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cranial suture morphogenesis
description: The process in which any suture between cranial bones is generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: frontal suture morphogenesis
description: The process in which the frontal suture is generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of Fc receptor mediated stimulatory signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of Fc receptor mediated stimulatory signalling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the Fc receptor mediated stimulatory signaling pathway..

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of Fc receptor mediated stimulatory signaling pathway
synonyms: positive regulation of Fc receptor mediated stimulatory signalling pathway
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of the Fc receptor mediated stimulatory signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: susceptibility to T cell mediated cytotoxicity
description: The process of causing a cell to become susceptible to T cell mediated cytotoxicity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of atrial cardiac muscle cell membrane depolarization
synonyms: atrial depolarization|electrocardiogram PR interval|regulation of atrial cardiac muscle cell depolarization|regulation of atrial cardiomyocyte membrane depolarization
description: Any process that modulates the establishment or extent of a membrane potential in the depolarizing direction away from the resting potential in an atrial cardiomyocyte.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of atrial cardiac muscle cell membrane repolarization
synonyms: atrial repolarization|electrocardiogram QRS complex|regulation of atrial cardiac muscle cell repolarization|regulation of atrial cardiomyocyte membrane repolarization
description: Any process that modulates the establishment or extent of a membrane potential in the polarizing direction towards the resting potential in an atrial cardiomyocyte.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of ventricular cardiac muscle cell membrane depolarization
synonyms: electrocardiogram QRS complex|regulation of ventricular cardiomyocyte membrane depolarization|ventricular depolarization
description: Any process that modulates the establishment or extent of a membrane potential in the depolarizing direction away from the resting potential in a ventricular cardiomyocyte.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mast cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a mast cell. A mast cell is a cell that is found in almost all tissues containing numerous basophilic granules and capable of releasing large amounts of histamine and heparin upon activation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of mast cell differentiation
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of mast cell differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a mast cell. A mast cell is a cell that is found in almost all tissues containing numerous basophilic granules and capable of releasing large amounts of histamine and heparin upon activation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of brood size
description: Any process that modulates brood size. Brood size is the number of progeny that survive embryogenesis and are cared for at one time.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cardiac muscle cell myoblast differentiation
synonyms: cardiac myoblast differentiation|myocardial precursor cell differentiation
description: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a cardiac myoblast. A cardiac myoblast is a precursor cell that has been committed to a cardiac muscle cell fate but retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of DNA strand elongation
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of DNA strand elongation. DNA strand elongation is the DNA metabolic process in which an existing DNA strand is extended by activities including the addition of nucleotides to the 3' end of the strand.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of DNA strand elongation
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of DNA strand elongation. DNA strand elongation is the DNA metabolic process in which an existing DNA strand is extended by activities including the addition of nucleotides to the 3' end of the strand.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: innervation
description: The process in which a nerve invades a tissue and makes functional synaptic connection within the tissue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: axonogenesis involved in innervation
description: The neurite development process that generates a long process of a neuron, as it invades a target tissue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synapse assembly involved in innervation
synonyms: synapse biogenesis involved in innervation|synaptogenesis involved in innervation
description: The assembly of a synapse within a target tissue in which a nerve is invading.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of SMAD protein signal transduction
synonyms: positive regulation of SMAD protein import into nucleus|positive regulation of SMAD protein nuclear translocation
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of SMAD protein signal transduction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of SMAD protein signal transduction
synonyms: negative regulation of SMAD protein import into nucleus|negative regulation of SMAD protein nuclear translocation
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of the SMAD protein signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: SMAD protein signal transduction
description: An intracellular signaling cassette that starts with the activation of a SMAD protein, leading to the formation of a complex with co-SMADs, which translocates to the nucleus and regulates transcription of specific target genes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: growth hormone receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: GH receptor signaling pathway|cellular response to growth hormone|growth hormone receptor signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of growth hormone receptor binding to its physiological ligand.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: growth hormone receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT
synonyms: JAK-STAT cascade involved in growth hormone signalling pathway
description: The process in which STAT proteins (Signal Transducers and Activators of Transcription) are activated by members of the JAK (janus activated kinase) family of tyrosine kinases, following the binding of physiological ligands to the growth hormone receptor. Once activated, STATs dimerize and translocate to the nucleus and modulate the expression of target genes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of growth hormone receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of growth hormone receptor signalling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the growth hormone receptor signaling pathway. The growth hormone receptor signaling pathway is the series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of growth hormone receptor binding to its physiological ligand.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of growth hormone receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: positive regulation of growth hormone receptor signalling pathway
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of the growth hormone receptor signaling pathway. The growth hormone receptor signaling pathway is the series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of growth hormone receptor binding to its physiological ligand.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of growth hormone receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: negative regulation of growth hormone receptor signalling pathway
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of the growth hormone receptor signaling pathway. The growth hormone receptor signaling pathway is the series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of growth hormone receptor binding to its physiological ligand.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: calcium ion transport into cytosol
description: The directed movement of calcium ions (Ca2+) into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of penile erection
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of penile erection. Penile erection is the hardening, enlarging and rising of the penis which often occurs in the sexually aroused male and enables sexual intercourse. Achieved by increased inflow of blood into the vessels of erectile tissue, and decreased outflow.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cardiac septum morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structure of a cardiac septum is generated and organized. A cardiac septum is a partition that separates parts of the heart.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ventricular septum morphogenesis
description: The developmental process in which a ventricular septum is generated and organized. A ventricular septum is an anatomical structure that separates the lower chambers (ventricles) of the heart from one another.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: atrial septum morphogenesis
description: The developmental process in which atrial septum is generated and organized. The atrial septum separates the upper chambers (the atria) of the heart from one another.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: aorta smooth muscle tissue morphogenesis
description: The process in which the structure of the smooth muscle tissue surrounding the aorta is generated and organized. An aorta is an artery that carries blood from the heart to other parts of the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: muscle tissue morphogenesis
description: The process in which the anatomical structures of muscle tissue are generated and organized. Muscle tissue consists of a set of cells that are part of an organ and carry out a contractive function.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to growth hormone
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a growth hormone stimulus. Growth hormone is a peptide hormone that binds to the growth hormone receptor and stimulates growth.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of heart growth
description: Any process that modulates the rate or extent of heart growth. Heart growth is the increase in size or mass of the heart.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of heart growth
description: Any process that increases the rate or extent of heart growth. Heart growth is the increase in size or mass of the heart.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lung morphogenesis
