description: A protein deubiquitination process in which a K63-linked ubiquitin chain, i.e. a polymer of ubiquitin formed by linkages between lysine residues at position 63 of the ubiquitin monomers, is removed from a protein.

description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of protein processing, a protein maturation process achieved by the cleavage of a peptide bond or bonds within a protein.

label: BiologicalProcess

description: The release of intracellular molecules contained within the zymogen granule by fusion of the granule with the plasma membrane of the oocyte, requiring calcium ions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: transepithelial transport
description: The directed movement of a substance from one side of an epithelium to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess

description: The directed movement of ammonium ions from one side of an epithelium to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess

description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving vitamin D3, (3S,5Z,7E)-9,10-secocholesta-5,7,10(19)-trien-3-ol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein modification by small protein removal
description: A protein modification process in which one or more covalently attached groups of a small protein, such as ubiquitin or a ubiquitin-like protein, are removed from a target protein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: formin-nucleated actin cable assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a formin-nucleated actin cable. A formin-nucleated actin cable is an actin filament bundle that consists of short filaments organized into bundles of uniform polarity, and is nucleated by formins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nonfunctional rRNA decay
description: An rRNA catabolic process that results in the targeted detection and degradation of aberrant rRNAs contained within translationally defective ribosomes, thereby acting as a quality-control system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: leukocyte proliferation
description: The expansion of a leukocyte population by cell division.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mast cell proliferation
description: The expansion of a mast cell population by cell division.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of leukocyte proliferation

label: BiologicalProcess
name: glutaminyl-tRNAGln biosynthesis via transamidation
description: A tRNA aminoacylation process in which glutaminyl-tRNAGln is formed by a tRNA-dependent two-step pathway. In the first step a non-discriminating glutamyl-tRNAGlx synthetase generates the misacylated L-glutamyl-tRNAGln species, and in the second step it is amidated to the correctly charged L-glutaminyl-tRNAGln by a glutamyl-tRNAGln amidotransferase.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: proteasome regulatory particle assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a mature, active proteasome regulatory particle complex.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: seminal clot liquefaction
description: The reproductive process in which coagulated semen becomes liquid following ejaculation, allowing the progressive release of motile spermatozoa.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sodium-dependent organic cation transport
description: The directed, sodium-dependent, movement of organic cations into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mismatch repair involved in maintenance of fidelity involved in DNA-dependent DNA replication
synonyms: mismatch repair involved in maintenance of fidelity during DNA-dependent DNA replication
description: A mismatch repair process that corrects errors introduced that ensures the accuracy of DNA replication.

label: BiologicalProcess

description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a cholesterol stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cyclic nucleotide transport
description: The directed movement of a cyclic nucleotide, any nucleotide in which phosphate group is in diester linkage to two positions on the sugar residue, into, out of or within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cAMP transport
description: The directed movement of cyclic AMP (cAMP), into, out of or within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cGMP transport
description: The directed movement of cyclic GMP (cGMP), into, out of or within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to interleukin-6
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an interleukin-6 stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: interleukin-35-mediated signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by interleukin-35 binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: D-aspartate transmembrane transport
description: The process in which D-aspartate, the D-enantiomer of the anion of (2R)-2-aminobutanedioic acid  is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-aspartate transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of L-aspartate across a membrane by means of some agent such as a transporter or a pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: D-aspartate import across plasma membrane
synonyms: D-aspartate import|D-aspartate import into cell|D-aspartate uptake
description: The directed import of D-aspartate from the extracellular region across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to biotin
synonyms: response to Bios IIB|response to coenzyme R|response to vitamin B7|response to vitamin H
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a biotin stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phosphatidylserine exposure on apoptotic cell surface
description: A phospholipid scrambling process that results in the appearance of phosphatidylserine on the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane of an apoptotic cell, which acts as an 'eat-me' signal for engulfing cells. Phosphatidylserine is exposed on the apoptotic cell surface by a phospholipid scramblase activity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hydrogen sulfide biosynthetic process
synonyms: hydrogen sulfide anabolism|hydrogen sulfide biosynthesis|hydrogen sulfide formation|hydrogen sulfide synthesis|hydrogen sulphide biosynthesis|hydrogen sulphide biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of hydrogen sulfide, H2S.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: heterochromatin organization
description: Any process that results in the specification, formation or maintenance of the physical structure of eukaryotic heterochromatin, a compact and highly condensed form of chromatin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bicellular tight junction assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a tight junction, an occluding cell-cell junction that is composed of a branching network of sealing strands that completely encircles the apical end of each cell in an epithelial sheet.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: basement membrane assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a basement membrane, a part of the extracellular region that consists of a thin layer of dense material found in various animal tissues interposed between the cells and the adjacent connective tissue.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: caveola assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a caveola. A caveola is a plasma membrane raft that forms a small pit, depression, or invagination that communicates with the outside of a cell and extends inward, indenting the cytoplasm and the cell membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dehydroascorbic acid transport
description: The directed movement of dehydroascorbate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Dehydroascorbate, 5-(1,2-dihydroxyethyl)furan-2,3,4(5H)-trione, is an oxidized form of vitamin C.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: aggresome assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form an aggresome; requires the microtubule cytoskeleton and dynein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: polyubiquitinated misfolded protein transport
synonyms: misfolded polyubiquitinated protein transport|polyubiquitylated misfolded protein transport
description: The directed movement of misfolded polyubiquitinated proteins in a cell, including the movement of proteins between specific compartments or structures within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to growth factor
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a growth factor stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess

synonyms: response to EGF stimulus|response to epidermal growth factor stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an epidermal growth factor stimulus.

synonyms: down regulation of calcineurin-NFAT signaling cascade|down-regulation of calcineurin-NFAT signaling cascade|downregulation of calcineurin-NFAT signaling cascade|inhibition of NFAT protein import into nucleus|inhibition of calcineurin-NFAT signaling cascade|negative regulation of NFAT protein import into nucleus|negative regulation of calcineurin-NFAT signaling pathway|negative regulation of calcineurin-NFAT signalling cascade|termination of calcineurin-NFAT signaling cascade

label: BiologicalProcess
name: platelet alpha granule organization
synonyms: platelet alpha granule organisation|platelet alpha granule organization and biogenesis|platelet alpha-granule organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a platelet alpha granule. A platelet alpha granule is a secretory organelle found in blood platelets.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: transcription preinitiation complex assembly
synonyms: DNA-dependent transcriptional preinitiation complex assembly|DNA-templated transcriptional preinitiation complex assembly|bacterial-type RNA polymerase preinitiation complex assembly|bacterial-type RNA polymerase transcription PIC formation|bacterial-type RNA polymerase transcriptional preinitiation complex formation|transcription PIC biosynthesis|transcription PIC formation|transcriptional preinitiation complex formation
description: The formation of a large multiprotein-DNA complex that self-assembles on gene promoter through the sequential recruitment of the general initiation factors that compose the preinitiation complex (PIC). The PIC engages the RNA polymerase on its DNA template strand and sparks polymerization of the first few RNA nucleotides.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: RNA polymerase III preinitiation complex assembly
synonyms: RNA polymerase III hybrid type promoter transcriptional preinitiation complex assembly|RNA polymerase III transcription PIC biosynthesis|RNA polymerase III transcription PIC formation|RNA polymerase III transcriptional preinitiation complex assembly|RNA polymerase III transcriptional preinitiation complex formation|RNA polymerase III type 1 promoter transcriptional preinitiation complex assembly|RNA polymerase III type 2 promoter transcriptional preinitiation complex assembly|RNA polymerase III type 3 promoter transcriptional preinitiation complex assembly

The PIC engages RNA polymerase III on its DNA template strand and sparks polymerization of the first few RNA nucleotides.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial tRNA modification
description: The covalent alteration of one or more nucleotides within a mitochondrial tRNA molecule to produce a mitochondrial tRNA molecule with a sequence that differs from that coded genetically.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial tRNA methylation
description: The posttranscriptional addition of methyl groups to specific residues in a mitochondrial tRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial tRNA pseudouridine synthesis
description: The intramolecular conversion of uridine to pseudouridine in a mitochondrial tRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: global genome nucleotide-excision repair
synonyms: GG-NER|GGR|global genome NER|global genomic nucleotide-excision repair|global genomic repair
description: The nucleotide-excision repair process in which DNA lesions are removed from nontranscribed strands and from transcriptionally silent regions over the entire genome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: UV-damage excision repair
synonyms: AER|UV-damaged DNA endonuclease-dependent excision repair|UVDE-dependent excision repair|UVER|alternative excision repair
description: A DNA repair process that is initiated by an endonuclease that introduces a single-strand incision immediately 5' of a UV-induced damage site. UV-damage excision repair acts on both cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs) and pyrimidine-pyrimidone 6-4 photoproducts (6-4PPs).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of regulatory ncRNA processing
synonyms: regulation of gene silencing by RNA|production of guide RNA|regulation of gene silencing by RNA|production of small RNA|regulation of production of small RNA involved in gene silencing by RNA
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of regulatory non-coding RNA processing.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of siRNA processing
synonyms: regulation of RNA interference|production of siRNA|regulation of chromatin silencing by small RNA|production of siRNA|regulation of production of siRNA involved in PTGS|regulation of production of siRNA involved in RNA interference|regulation of production of siRNA involved in chromatin silencing by small RNA|regulation of production of siRNA involved in gene silencing by small RNA|regulation of production of siRNA involved in post-transcriptional gene silencing by RNA|regulation of siRNA production
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of siRNA processing.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: RISC complex assembly
synonyms: RISC assembly|gene silencing by RNA|small RNA loading onto RISC|miRISC assembly|miRNA loading onto RISC|siRNA loading onto RISC involved in RNA interference|siRNA loading onto RISC involved in gene silencing by small RNA|small RNA loading onto RISC
description: The process in which a single-stranded small RNA is incorporated within the RNA-initiated silencing complex (RISC). The assembly includes the maturation of the small RNA, the stabilization of the complex by accessory proteins of the RISC complex, duplex separation and the release of the second strand, forming a base-pairing complement complex that mediates gene silencing by small RNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: organelle assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form an organelle. An organelle is an organized structure of distinctive morphology and function. Includes the nucleus, mitochondria, plastids, vacuoles, vesicles, ribosomes and the cytoskeleton. Excludes the plasma membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: CRD-mediated mRNA stabilization
description: An mRNA stabilization process in which one or more RNA-binding proteins associate with a sequence in the open reading frame called the coding region instability determinant (CRD).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: 3'-UTR-mediated mRNA stabilization
description: An mRNA stabilization process in which one or more RNA-binding proteins associate with the 3'-untranslated region (UTR) of an mRNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein K48-linked ubiquitination
description: A protein ubiquitination process in which a polymer of ubiquitin, formed by linkages between lysine residues at position 48 of the ubiquitin monomers, is added to a protein. K48-linked ubiquitination targets the substrate protein for degradation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neutrophil-mediated killing of symbiont cell
synonyms: neutrophil mediated killing of symbiont cell
description: The directed killing of a symbiont target cell by a neutrophil. The symbiont is defined as the smaller of the organisms involved in a symbiotic interaction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neutrophil-mediated killing of bacterium
description: The directed killing of a bacterium by a neutrophil.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neutrophil-mediated killing of gram-negative bacterium
synonyms: neutrophil mediated killing of gram-negative bacterium
description: The directed killing of a gram-negative bacterium by a neutrophil.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neutrophil-mediated killing of fungus
description: The directed killing of a fungal cell by a neutrophil.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of neutrophil mediated cytotoxicity
synonyms: regulation of neutrophil mediated cell killing
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of neutrophil mediated killing of a target cell, the directed killing of a target cell by a neutrophil.

label: BiologicalProcess

synonyms: no-go decay|no-go mRNA decay|nuclear-transcribed mRNA breakdown|no-go decay|nuclear-transcribed mRNA catabolism|no-go decay|nuclear-transcribed mRNA degradation|no-go decay
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of the transcript body of a nuclear-transcribed mRNA with stalls in translation elongation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to endoplasmic reticulum
synonyms: protein localisation in endoplasmic reticulum|protein localization in ER|protein localization in endoplasmic reticulum
description: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a location within the endoplasmic reticulum.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bone maturation
description: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for bone to attain its fully functional state.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein K11-linked ubiquitination
description: A protein ubiquitination process in which ubiquitin monomers are attached to a protein, and then ubiquitin polymers are formed by linkages between lysine residues at position 11 of the ubiquitin monomers. K11-linked polyubiquitination targets the substrate protein for degradation. The anaphase-promoting complex promotes the degradation of mitotic regulators by assembling K11-linked polyubiquitin chains.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-asparagine biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of asparagine, (2S)-2-amino-3-carbamoylpropanoic acid.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: left/right axis specification
description: The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of the left/right axis. The left/right axis is defined by a line that runs orthogonal to both the anterior/posterior and dorsal/ventral axes. Each side is defined from the viewpoint of the organism rather of the observer (as per anatomical axes).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: error-free translesion synthesis
description: The conversion of DNA-damage induced single-stranded gaps into large molecular weight DNA after replication by using a specialized DNA polymerase or replication complex to insert a defined nucleotide across the lesion. This process does not remove the replication-blocking lesions but does not causes an increase in the endogenous mutation level. For S. cerevisiae, RAD30 encodes DNA polymerase eta, which incorporates two adenines. When incorporated across a thymine-thymine dimer, it does not increase the endogenous mutation level.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: demethylation
description: The process of removing one or more methyl groups from a molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: oxidative demethylation
description: The process of removing one or more methyl groups from a molecule, involving the oxidation (i.e. electron loss) of one or more atoms in the substrate.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: detection of oxidative stress
description: The series of events in which a stimulus indicating oxidative stress is received and converted into a molecular signal.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to magnetism
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a magnetic stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: RNA surveillance
synonyms: RNA quality control|aberrant RNA catabolic process
description: A process that identifies and degrades defective or aberrant RNAs.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear RNA surveillance
synonyms: nuclear RNA quality control|nuclear aberrant RNA catabolic process
description: A process that identifies and degrades defective or aberrant RNAs within the nucleus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear mRNA surveillance
synonyms: nuclear aberrant mRNA catabolic process|nuclear mRNA quality control|nuclear retention of pre-mRNA at the site of transcription|nuclear retention of pre-mRNA with aberrant 3\'-ends at the site of transcription|nuclear retention of unspliced pre-mRNA at the site of transcription
description: A process that identifies and degrades defective or aberrant mRNAs within the nucleus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear mRNA surveillance of spliceosomal pre-mRNA splicing
synonyms: nuclear RNA catabolic process of incorrectly spliced pre-mRNA|nuclear mRNA quality control of incorrectly spliced pre-mRNA
description: The set of processes involved in identifying and degrading incorrectly spliced pre-mRNAs within the nucleus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear mRNA surveillance of mRNA 3'-end processing
synonyms: nuclear mRNA catabolic process of mRNA with aberrant 3\'-ends|nuclear mRNA quality control of mRNAs with aberrant 3\'-ends
description: The set of processes involved in identifying and degrading mRNAs with incorrectly formed 3'-ends within the nucleus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear mRNA surveillance of mRNP export
synonyms: nuclear mRNA catabolic process of mRNAs in aberrant mRNPs|nuclear mRNA quality control of mRNAs in aberrant mRNPs
description: The set of processes involved in identifying and degrading incorrectly formed or aberrant nuclear mRNPs docked at the nuclear pore complex prior to export to the cytoplasm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: CUT catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of cryptic unstable transcripts (CUTs).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear polyadenylation-dependent rRNA catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways occurring in the nucleus and resulting in the breakdown of a ribosomal RNA (rRNA) molecule, including RNA fragments released as part of processing the primary transcript into multiple mature rRNA species, initiated by the enzymatic addition of a sequence of adenylyl residues (polyadenylation) at the 3' end the target rRNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear polyadenylation-dependent snoRNA catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways occurring in the nucleus and resulting in the breakdown of a small nucleolar RNA (snoRNA) molecule, initiated by the enzymatic addition of a sequence of adenylyl residues (polyadenylation) at the 3' end the target snoRNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear polyadenylation-dependent snRNA catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways occurring in the nucleus and resulting in the breakdown of a small nuclear RNA (snRNA) molecule, initiated by the enzymatic addition of a sequence of adenylyl residues (polyadenylation) at the 3' end the target snRNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: TRAMP-dependent tRNA surveillance pathway
description: A nuclear tRNA surveillance pathway, dependent on the TRAMP exosome adaptor and the nuclear exosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear polyadenylation-dependent CUT catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways occurring in the nucleus and resulting in the breakdown of a cryptic unstable transcript (CUT), initiated by the enzymatic addition of a sequence of adenylyl residues (polyadenylation) at the 3' end the target CUT.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear polyadenylation-dependent antisense transcript catabolic process
synonyms: nuclear poly(A)-dependent antisense transcript catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways occurring in the nucleus and resulting in the breakdown of an antisense transcript, initiated by the enzymatic addition of a sequence of adenylyl residues (polyadenylation) at the 3' end the target antisense transcript.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear polyadenylation-dependent mRNA catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways occurring in the nucleus and resulting in the breakdown of a messenger RNA (mRNA) molecule, initiated by the enzymatic addition of a sequence of adenylyl residues (polyadenylation) at the 3' end the target mRNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: histone mRNA catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of histone messenger RNA (mRNA).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear histone mRNA catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of histone messenger RNA (mRNA) within the nucleus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: poly(A)-dependent snoRNA 3'-end processing
description: Any process involved in forming the mature 3' end of a snoRNA molecule linked to prior polyadenylation of the 3'-end of the precursor snoRNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of phospholipid biosynthetic process
synonyms: regulation of phospholipid anabolism|regulation of phospholipid biosynthesis|regulation of phospholipid formation|regulation of phospholipid synthesis
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of phospholipids.

description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of phospholipids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: DNA conformation change
description: A cellular process that results in a change in the spatial configuration of a DNA molecule. A conformation change can bend DNA, or alter the, twist, writhe, or linking number of a DNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to interleukin-9
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an interleukin-9 stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to interleukin-11
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an interleukin-11 stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to parathyroid hormone
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a parathyroid hormone stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein K48-linked deubiquitination
description: A protein deubiquitination process in which a K48-linked ubiquitin chain, i.e. a polymer of ubiquitin formed by linkages between lysine residues at position 48 of the ubiquitin monomers, is removed from a protein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: superior temporal gyrus development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the superior temporal gyrus over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The superior temporal gyrus is a portion of the cerebral cortex that extends from the lateral sulcus to the superior temporal sulcus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: resolution of DNA recombination intermediates
description: The cleavage and rejoining of intermediates, such as Holliday junctions, formed during DNA recombination to produce two intact molecules in which genetic material has been exchanged.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: resolution of mitotic recombination intermediates
description: The cleavage and rejoining of intermediates, mitotic recombination to produce two intact molecules in which genetic material has been exchanged.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: DNA replication preinitiation complex assembly
synonyms: DNA replication preinitiation complex formation|pre-IC complex assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form the DNA replication preinitiation complex, a protein-DNA complex that is assembled at DNA replication origins as part of initiation of DNA replication. The complex consists of proteins that initiate the DNA binding, melt the helix and enable helicase activity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ribonucleoprotein complex localization
synonyms: RNP localization|cellular ribonucleoprotein complex localization|establishment and maintenance of ribonucleoprotein complex localization|ribonucleoprotein complex localisation
description: Any process in which a ribonucleoprotein complex is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to chromatin

name: cellular response to purine-containing compound
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a purine-containing compound stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to amine stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an amine stimulus. An amine is a compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to histamine
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a histamine stimulus. Histamine, the biogenic amine 2-(1H-imidazol-4-yl)ethanamine, is involved in local immune responses as well as regulating physiological function in the gut and acting as a neurotransmitter.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: manganese ion transmembrane transport
synonyms: manganese ion membrane transport|transmembrane manganese transport
description: A process in which a manganese ion is transported from one side of a membrane to the other by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: succinate transmembrane transport
description: The process in which succinate is transported across a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: malate transmembrane transport
description: A process in which a malate ion is transported across a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hematopoietic stem cell proliferation
description: The expansion of a hematopoietic stem cell population by cell division. A hematopoietic stem cell is a stem cell from which all cells of the lymphoid and myeloid lineages develop.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to hydroperoxide
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a hydroperoxide stimulus. Hydroperoxides are monosubstitution products of hydrogen peroxide, HOOH.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to lipid hydroperoxide
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a lipid hydroperoxide stimulus. Lipid hydroperoxide is the highly reactive primary oxygenated products of polyunsaturated fatty acids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to superoxide
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a superoxide stimulus. Superoxide is the anion, oxygen-, formed by addition of one electron to dioxygen (O2) or any compound containing the superoxide anion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to oxygen levels
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus reflecting the presence, absence, or concentration of oxygen.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to anoxia
synonyms: cellular response to anaerobic conditions|cellular response to anoxic stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating a decline in oxygen levels to trace amounts, <0.1%.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to hyperoxia
synonyms: cellular response to hyperoxic stress|cellular response to increased oxygen tension
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating increased oxygen tension.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to hypoxia
synonyms: cellular response to hypoxic stress|cellular response to lowered oxygen tension
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating lowered oxygen tension. Hypoxia, defined as a decline in O2 levels below normoxic levels of 20.8 - 20.95%, results in metabolic adaptation at both the cellular and organismal level.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to chromosome, centromeric region
synonyms: protein localisation to chromosome|centromeric region|protein localization to centromere|protein localization to chromosome|centric region
description: Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, the centromeric region of a chromosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to cell-matrix adhesion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of cell-matrix adhesion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to redox state
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating redox state. Redox state refers to the balance of oxidized versus reduced forms of electron donors and acceptors in an organelle, cell or organ; plastoquinone, glutathione (GSH/GSSG), and nicotinamide nucleotides (NAD+/NADH and NADP+/NADPH) are among the most important.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to hydrostatic pressure
synonyms: cellular response to biomechanical stress|cellular response to static fluid pressure
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a hydrostatic pressure stimulus. Hydrostatic pressure is the force acting on an object in a system where the fluid is at rest (as opposed to moving). The weight of the fluid above the object creates pressure on it.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to xenobiotic stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a xenobiotic, a compound foreign to the organism exposed to it. It may be synthesized by another organism (like ampicilin) or it can be a synthetic chemical.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to pH
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a pH stimulus. pH is a measure of the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to acidic pH
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a pH stimulus with pH < 7. pH is a measure of the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to alkaline pH
synonyms: cellular response to alkalinity|cellular response to basic pH
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a pH stimulus with pH > 7. pH is a measure of the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to osmotic stress
synonyms: cellular osmotic response|cellular osmotic stress response
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating an increase or decrease in the concentration of solutes outside the organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to non-ionic osmotic stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating an increase or decrease in the concentration of non-ionic solutes (e.g. mannitol, sorbitol) in the environment.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to salt stress
synonyms: cellular response to ionic osmotic stress|cellular salinity response
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating an increase or decrease in the concentration of salt (particularly but not exclusively sodium and chloride ions) in the environment.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular hyperosmotic response
synonyms: cellular HOG response|cellular hypertonic response|cellular response to hypertonicity
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of detection of, or exposure to, a hyperosmotic environment, i.e. an environment with a higher concentration of solutes than the organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular hyperosmotic salinity response
synonyms: cellular response to hyperosmotic salt stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of detection of, or exposure to, an increase in the concentration of salt (particularly but not exclusively sodium and chloride ions) in the environment.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular hypotonic response
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of detection of, or exposure to, a hypotonic environment, i.e. an environment with a lower concentration of solutes than the organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular hypotonic salinity response
synonyms: cellular response to hypotonic salt stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of detection of, or exposure to, a decrease in the concentration of salt (particularly but not exclusively sodium and chloride ions) in the environment.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to ionizing radiation
synonyms: cellular response to ionising radiation|cellular response to ionizing radiation stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a ionizing radiation stimulus. Ionizing radiation is radiation with sufficient energy to remove electrons from atoms and may arise from spontaneous decay of unstable isotopes, resulting in alpha and beta particles and gamma rays. Ionizing radiation also includes X-rays.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to gamma radiation
synonyms: cellular response to gamma ray|cellular response to gamma-ray photon
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a gamma radiation stimulus. Gamma radiation is a form of electromagnetic radiation (EMR) or light emission of a specific frequency produced from sub-atomic particle interaction, such as electron-positron annihilation and radioactive decay. Gamma rays are generally characterized as EMR having the highest frequency and energy, and also the shortest wavelength, within the electromagnetic radiation spectrum.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to X-ray
synonyms: cellular response to X-ray radiation stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of X-ray radiation. An X-ray is a form of electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength in the range of 10 nanometers to 100 picometers (corresponding to frequencies in the range 30 PHz to 3 EHz).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to light stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a light stimulus, electromagnetic radiation of wavelengths classified as infrared, visible or ultraviolet light.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to high light intensity
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a high light intensity stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to UV-A
synonyms: cellular response to UV-A light stimulus|cellular response to UV-A radiation stimulus|cellular response to UVA light stimulus|cellular response to UVA radiation stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a UV-A radiation stimulus. UV-A radiation (UV-A light) spans the wavelengths 315 to 400 nm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to UV-B
synonyms: cellular response to UV-B light stimulus|cellular response to UV-B radiation stimulus|cellular response to UVB light stimulus|cellular response to UVB radiation stimulus|cellular response to medium wave ultraviolet light stimulus|cellular response to medium wave ultraviolet radiation stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a UV-B radiation stimulus. UV-B radiation (UV-B light) spans the wavelengths 280 to 315 nm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to UV-C
synonyms: cellular response to UV-C light stimulus|cellular response to UV-C radiation stimulus|cellular response to UVC light stimulus|cellular response to UVC radiation stimulus|cellular response to germicidal ultraviolet light stimulus|cellular response to germicidal ultraviolet radiation stimulus|cellular response to shortwave ultraviolet light stimulus|cellular response to shortwave ultraviolet radiation stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a UV-C radiation stimulus. UV-C radiation (UV-C light) spans the wavelengths 100 to 280 nm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to fluid shear stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a fluid shear stress stimulus. Fluid shear stress is the force acting on an object in a system where the fluid is moving across a solid surface.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to laminar fluid shear stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a laminar fluid shear stress stimulus. Laminar fluid flow is the force acting on an object in a system where the fluid is moving across a solid surface in parallel layers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to nitrosative stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nitrosative stress stimulus. Nitrosative stress is a state often resulting from exposure to high levels of nitric oxide (NO) or the highly reactive oxidant peroxynitrite, which is produced following interaction of NO with superoxide anions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to temperature stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a temperature stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to heparin
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a heparin stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to heparin
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a heparin stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to mycophenolic acid
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a mycophenolic acid stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: genomic imprinting
synonyms: DNA imprinting|establishment of genomic imprinting|genetic imprinting
description: The establishment of epigenetic modifications (imprints) during gametogenesis, and propagation of these imprints during the organism's life. Genomic imprinting leads to an asymmetry between the maternal and paternal alleles and differential expression of the corresponding alleles. This can happen through heterochromatin formation or differential chromatin loop formation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: semaphorin-plexin signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of a semaphorin receptor (composed of a plexin and a neurophilin) binding to a semaphorin ligand.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tRNA re-export from nucleus
description: The directed movement from the nucleus to the cytoplasm of a tRNA that was previously exported to the cytoplasm and then imported back into the nucleus. The processes of primary tRNA export and secondary export (re-export) can be distinguished because in organisms in which tRNA splicing occurs in the cytoplasm, the export of a mature tRNA must occur by re-export.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cementum mineralization
description: The process in which calcium salts, mainly carbonated hydroxyapatite, are deposited into the initial acellular cementum.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to centrosome
description: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, the centrosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dopaminergic neuron differentiation
description: The process in which a neuroblast acquires the specialized structural and functional features of a dopaminergic neuron, a neuron that secretes dopamine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: diphosphoinositol polyphosphate catabolic process
synonyms: diphosphoinositol polyphosphate breakdown|diphosphoinositol polyphosphate catabolism|diphosphoinositol polyphosphate degradation
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a diphosphoinositol polyphosphate, 1,2,3,4,5,6-cyclohexanehexol with one or more diphosphate groups and multiple monophosphate groups attached.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: inositol phosphate catabolic process
synonyms: inositol phosphate breakdown|inositol phosphate catabolism|inositol phosphate degradation|myo-inositol phosphate catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of an inositol phosphate, 1,2,3,4,5,6-cyclohexanehexol, with one or more phosphate groups attached.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to dexamethasone
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a dexamethasone stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to dexamethasone stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a dexamethasone stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: death-inducing signaling complex assembly
synonyms: DD-mediated complex assembly|DISC assembly|DISC formation|death domain-mediated complex assembly|death domain-mediated complex assembly involved in extrinsic apoptotic pathway|death-inducing signaling complex formation|death-inducing signalling complex assembly
description: A process of protein complex assembly in which the arrangement and bonding together of the set of components that form the protein complex is mediated by a death domain (DD) interaction, as part of the extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to transforming growth factor beta
synonyms: response to TGF-beta stimulus|response to TGFbeta stimulus|response to transforming growth factor beta stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a transforming growth factor beta stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to transforming growth factor beta stimulus
synonyms: cellular response to TGF-beta stimulus|cellular response to TGFbeta stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a transforming growth factor beta stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein ufmylation
description: Covalent attachment of the ubiquitin-like protein UFM1 to another protein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: zinc ion transmembrane transport
synonyms: zinc II ion transmembrane transport|zinc ion membrane transport|zinc transmembrane transport
description: A process in which a zinc II ion is transported from one side of a membrane to the other by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: zinc ion import across plasma membrane
synonyms: high-affinity zinc II ion transmembrane import|high-affinity zinc II ion transport|low-affinity zinc II ion transport|zinc II ion plasma membrane import|zinc II ion transmembrane import|zinc import|zinc ion import into cell|zinc ion transmembrane import|zinc uptake
description: The directed movement of zinc(2+) ions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of zinc ion transport
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of zinc ions (Zn2+) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of zinc ion transmembrane import
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of zinc ion import.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: detoxification of cadmium ion
description: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of cadmium ion. These may include transport of cadmium away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of cadmium ion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: CAAX-box protein processing
description: The second process in a series of specific posttranslational modifications to the CAAX box region of CAAX box proteins, in which the last three amino acids of the protein (AAX) are removed by proteolysis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lymphocyte aggregation
description: The adhesion of one lymphocyte to one or more other lymphocytes via adhesion molecules.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process via the N-end rule pathway
synonyms: ubiquitin-dependent protein breakdown via the N-end rule pathway|ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolism via the N-end rule pathway|ubiquitin-dependent protein degradation via the N-end rule pathway
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein or peptide covalently tagged with ubiquitin, via the N-end rule pathway. In the N-end rule pathway, destabilizing N-terminal residues (N-degrons) in substrates are recognized by E3 ligases (N-recognins), whereupon the substrates are linked to ubiquitin and then delivered to the proteasome for degradation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: otic vesicle development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the otic vesicle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The otic vesicle is a transient embryonic structure formed during development of the vertebrate inner ear.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: phytosphingosine biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of phytosphingosine, (2S,3S,4R)-2-aminooctadecane-1,3,4-triol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endothelial cell-cell adhesion
description: The attachment of an endothelial cell to another endothelial cell via adhesion molecules.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: transforming growth factor beta production
synonyms: TGF-B production|TGF-beta production|TGFb production|TGFbeta production|transforming growth factor-beta production|transforming growth factor-beta secretion
description: The appearance of any member of the transforming growth factor-beta family of cytokines due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels. Transforming growth factor-beta family members include TGF-B1, TGF-B2, and TGF-B3.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: acyl-CoA biosynthetic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of acyl-CoA, any derivative of coenzyme A in which the sulfhydryl group is in thiolester linkage with an acyl group.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: granulocyte chemotaxis
description: The movement of a granulocyte in response to an external stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of granulocyte chemotaxis
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of granulocyte chemotaxis. Granulocyte chemotaxis is the movement of a granulocyte in response to an external stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of granulocyte chemotaxis
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of granulocyte chemotaxis. Granulocyte chemotaxis is the movement of a granulocyte in response to an external stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vocalization behavior
description: The behavior in which an organism produces sounds by a mechanism involving its respiratory system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mastication
description: The process of biting and mashing food with the teeth prior to swallowing.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cytoplasm protein quality control by the ubiquitin-proteasome system
synonyms: cytoplasm-associated proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent protein breakdown|cytoplasm-associated proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolism|cytoplasm-associated proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent protein degradation|ubiquitin-dependent catabolism of misfolded proteins by cytoplasm-associated proteasome
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of misfolded proteins in the cytoplasm, which are targeted to cytoplasmic proteasomes for degradation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear protein quality control by the ubiquitin-proteasome system
synonyms: nucleus-associated proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent protein breakdown|nucleus-associated proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolism|nucleus-associated proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent protein degradation|ubiquitin-dependent catabolism of misfolded proteins by nucleus-associated proteasome
description: A protein quality control pathway that results in the breakdown of misfolded, damaged or unassembled proteins via a mechanism in which the proteins are ubiquitinated, and then targeted to nuclear proteasomes for degradation.

description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of production of transforming growth factor-beta.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of transforming growth factor beta production
synonyms: positive regulation of TGF-B production|positive regulation of TGF-beta production|positive regulation of TGFB production|positive regulation of TGFbeta production|positive regulation of transforming growth factor-beta production|positive regulation of transforming growth factor-beta secretion
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, or extent of production of transforming growth factor-beta.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of monocyte chemotactic protein-1 production
synonyms: negative regulation of CCL2 production|negative regulation of MCP-1 production
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of production of monocyte chemotactic protein-1.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of monocyte chemotactic protein-1 production
synonyms: positive regulation of CCL2 production|positive regulation of MCP-1 production
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, or extent of production of monocyte chemotactic protein-1.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of macrophage inflammatory protein 1 alpha production

description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of production of macrophage inflammatory protein 1 alpha.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of macrophage inflammatory protein 1 alpha production
synonyms: negative regulation of CCL3 production|negative regulation of MIP-1a production|negative regulation of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 3 production|negative regulation of macrophage inflammatory protein production
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of production of macrophage inflammatory protein 1 alpha.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of macrophage inflammatory protein 1 alpha production
synonyms: positive regulation of CCL3 production|positive regulation of MIP-1a production|positive regulation of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 3 production|positive regulation of macrophage inflammatory protein production
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, or extent of production of macrophage inflammatory protein 1 alpha.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 4 production
synonyms: negative regulation of CCL4 production|negative regulation of MIP-1b production|negative regulation of macrophage inflammatory protein production
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of production of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 4.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 5 production
synonyms: negative regulation of CCL5 production|negative regulation of RANTES production|negative regulation of Regulated upon Activation|Normal T-cell Expressed|and Secreted production
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of production of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 5.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 5 production

description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, or extent of production of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 5.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 1 production
synonyms: positive regulation of CCL1 production|positive regulation of T cell activation 3 production|positive regulation of TCA-3 production
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, or extent of production of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 1.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor production
synonyms: negative regulation of CSF3 production|negative regulation of G-CSF production|negative regulation of colony stimulating factor 3 (granulocyte) production|negative regulation of filgrastim production|negative regulation of granulocyte colony stimulating factor production|negative regulation of lenograstim production|negative regulation of pluripoietin production

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of IP-10 production

description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of production of IP-10.

description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, or extent of production of IP-10.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of granzyme B production
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, or extent of production of granzyme B.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
description: The directed movement of a smooth muscle cell in response to an external stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
synonyms: down regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis|down-regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis|downregulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis|inhibition of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
synonyms: activation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis|stimulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis|up regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis|up-regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis|upregulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, or extent of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mononuclear cell migration
description: The movement of a mononuclear cell within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of mononuclear cell migration
synonyms: down regulation of mononuclear cell migration|down-regulation of mononuclear cell migration|downregulation of mononuclear cell migration|inhibition of mononuclear cell migration
description: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of mononuclear cell migration. Mononuclear cell migration is the movement of a mononuclear cell within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of mononuclear cell migration
synonyms: activation of mononuclear cell migration|stimulation of mononuclear cell migration|up regulation of mononuclear cell migration|up-regulation of mononuclear cell migration|upregulation of mononuclear cell migration
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of mononuclear cell migration. Mononuclear cell migration is the movement of a mononuclear cell within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: commissural neuron axon guidance
description: The process in which the migration of an axon growth cone of a commissural neuron is directed to its target in the brain in response to a combination of attractive and repulsive cues.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to indole-3-methanol
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an indole-3-methanol stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to indole-3-methanol
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an indole-3-methanol stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cardiac muscle thin filament assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of proteins to form the actin-based thin filaments of myofibrils in cardiac muscle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein transport within extracellular region
description: The directed movement of proteins in the extracellular region, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: immunoglobulin heavy chain V-D-J recombination
synonyms: immunoglobulin V(D)J joining|immunoglobulin V(D)J recombination|immunoglobulin V-D-J joining
description: The process in which immunoglobulin heavy chain V, D, and J gene segments are recombined within a single locus utilizing the conserved heptamer and nonomer recombination signal sequences (RSS).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: membrane assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: basement membrane organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the basement membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: leukotriene transport
description: The directed movement of leukotrienes into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Leukotrienes are linear C20 endogenous metabolites of arachidonic acid (icosa-5,8,11,14-tetraenoic acid) containing a terminal carboxy function and four or more double bonds (three or more of which are conjugated) as well as other functional groups.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: detoxification of arsenic-containing substance
description: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of compounds containing arsenic, including arsenates, arsenites, and arsenides. These include transport of such compounds away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of arsenic or arsenic-containing compounds.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to diacyl bacterial lipopeptide
synonyms: cellular response to diacylated bacterial lipoprotein
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a diacylated bacterial lipopeptide stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to triacyl bacterial lipopeptide
synonyms: cellular response to triacylated bacterial lipoprotein
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a triacylated bacterial lipopeptide stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to nitric oxide
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nitric oxide stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to nitric oxide
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nitric oxide stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear membrane organization
synonyms: nuclear membrane organisation|nuclear membrane organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the nuclear inner or outer membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear inner membrane organization
synonyms: nuclear inner membrane organisation|nuclear inner membrane organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the nuclear inner membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to BMP stimulus
synonyms: cellular response to bone morphogenetic protein stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to fibroblast growth factor
synonyms: response to FGF stimulus|response to fibroblast growth factor stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a fibroblast growth factor stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endoplasmic reticulum tubular network organization
synonyms: ER tubular network organisation|ER tubular network organization|endoplasmic reticulum tubular network organisation
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) tubular network. The ER tubular network is the ER part that that has membranes with high curvature in cross-section.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endoplasmic reticulum tubular network formation
synonyms: ER tubular network assembly|ER tubular network formation|endoplasmic reticulum tubular network assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) tubular network. The ER tubular network is the ER part that comprises the membranes with high curvature in cross-section.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endoplasmic reticulum tubular network maintenance
description: The organization process that preserves the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) tubular network in a stable functional or structural state. The ER tubular network is the ER part that comprises the membranes with high curvature in cross-section.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to prostaglandin D stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a prostagladin D stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: podosome assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a podosome, an actin-rich adhesion structure characterized by formation upon cell substrate contact and localization at the substrate-attached part of the cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of podosome assembly
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of podosome assembly.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of podosome assembly
synonyms: activation of podosome assembly|stimulation of podosome assembly|up regulation of podosome assembly|up-regulation of podosome assembly|upregulation of podosome assembly
description: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of podosome assembly.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: potassium ion transmembrane transport
synonyms: high affinity potassium ion import|high affinity potassium ion uptake|high-affinity potassium ion import|high-affinity potassium ion uptake|potassium ion membrane transport
description: A process in which a potassium ion is transported from one side of a membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein transmembrane transport
description: The process in which a protein is transported across a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of fever generation by positive regulation of prostaglandin secretion
description: Any process that increases the rate or extent of fever generation via positive regulation of the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of a prostaglandin from a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: tail-anchored membrane protein insertion into ER membrane
synonyms: protein insertion of tail-anchored membrane proteins into ER membrane|tail-anchored membrane protein insertion into endoplasmic reticulum membrane|type II transmembrane protein insertion into ER membrane
description: A process of protein insertion into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane in which a tail-anchored (TA) transmembrane protein is incorporated into an endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane. TA transmembrane protein, also named type II transmembrane proteins, contain a single C- terminal transmembrane region.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: triglyceride-rich lipoprotein particle clearance
description: The process in which a triglyceride-rich lipoprotein particle is removed from the blood via receptor-mediated endocytosis and its constituent parts degraded.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intermediate-density lipoprotein particle clearance
description: The process in which a intermediate-density lipoprotein particle is removed from the blood via receptor-mediated endocytosis and its constituent parts degraded.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell proliferation in bone marrow
description: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population in the bone marrow.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: actin filament debranching
description: An actin filament severing process that results in the removal of actin filament branches specifically at the branch points.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cell proliferation in bone marrow
synonyms: regulation of bone marrow cell proliferation
description: A process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell proliferation in the bone marrow.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of cell proliferation in bone marrow
synonyms: activation of cell proliferation in bone marrow|positive regulation of bone marrow cell proliferation|stimulation of cell proliferation in bone marrow|up regulation of cell proliferation in bone marrow|up-regulation of cell proliferation in bone marrow|upregulation of cell proliferation in bone marrow
description: A process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cell proliferation in the bone marrow.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of apoptotic process in bone marrow cell
synonyms: down regulation of apoptosis in bone marrow|down-regulation of apoptosis in bone marrow|downregulation of apoptosis in bone marrow|inhibition of apoptosis in bone marrow|negative regulation of apoptosis in bone marrow|negative regulation of apoptotic process in bone marrow|negative regulation of bone marrow cell apoptosis|negative regulation of bone marrow cell programmed cell death by apoptosis|negative regulation of killing of bone marrow cells|negative regulation of programmed cell death of bone marrow cells by apoptosis|negative regulation of programmed cell death|bone marrow cells
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the occurrence or rate of cell death by apoptotic process in the bone marrow.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to monoamine
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a monoamine stimulus. A monoamine is any of a group of molecular messengers that contain one amino group that is connected to an aromatic ring by ethylene group (-CH2-CH2-). Monoamines are derived from the aromatic amino acids phenylalanine, tyrosine, histidine and tryptophan.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to catecholamine
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a catecholamine stimulus. A catecholamine is any of a group of biogenic amines that includes 4-(2-aminoethyl)pyrocatechol [4-(2-aminoethyl)benzene-1,2-diol] and derivatives formed by substitution.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to catecholamine stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a catecholamine stimulus. A catecholamine is any of a group of biogenic amines that includes 4-(2-aminoethyl)pyrocatechol [4-(2-aminoethyl)benzene-1,2-diol] and derivatives formed by substitution.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to epinephrine
synonyms: response to adrenaline stimulus|response to epinephrine stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an epinephrine stimulus. Epinephrine is a catecholamine that has the formula C9H13NO3; it is secreted by the adrenal medulla to act as a hormone, and released by certain neurons to act as a neurotransmitter active in the central nervous system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to epinephrine stimulus
