description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a dendritic spine. A dendritic spine is a specialized protrusion from a neuronal dendrite and is involved in synaptic transmission.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dendritic spine maintenance
description: The organization process that preserves a dendritic spine in a stable functional or structural state. A dendritic spine is a specialized protrusion from a neuronal dendrite and is involved in synaptic transmission.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to thyroid hormone
description: A change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a thyroid hormone stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to thyroid hormone stimulus
description: A change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a thyroid hormone stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to thyroxine
synonyms: response to T4|response to T4 stimulus|response to thyroxine stimulus
description: A change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a thyroxine stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to thyroxine stimulus
description: A change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a thyroxine stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ductus arteriosus closure
description: The morphogenesis process in which the ductus arteriosus changes to no longer permit blood flow after birth. The ductus arteriosus is the shunt between the aorta and the pulmonary artery which allows blood to bypass the fetus' lungs.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: plasma membrane selenite transport
description: The directed movement of inorganic selenite (HSeO3-1 at physiological pH) across a plasma membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vascular associated smooth muscle cell development
description: The process aimed at the progression of a vascular smooth muscle cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. A vascular smooth muscle cell is a non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cell found lining the blood vessels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: methyl-branched fatty acid metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving methyl-branched fatty acids, aliphatic monocarboxylic acids with methyl branches on the main chain.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: presynaptic membrane organization
description: A process which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a presynaptic membrane, including any proteins associated with the membrane, but excluding other cellular components. A presynaptic membrane is a specialized area of membrane of the axon terminal that faces the plasma membrane of the neuron or muscle fiber with which the axon terminal establishes a synaptic junction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic vesicle clustering
description: The process that results in grouping synaptic vesicles in presynaptic structures.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: craniofacial suture morphogenesis
description: The process in which any suture between cranial and/or facial bones is generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: blood vessel endothelial cell fate specification
description: The process involved in the specification of identity of a blood vessel endothelial cell. Once specification has taken place, a cell will be committed to differentiate down a specific pathway if left in its normal environment. A blood vessel endothelial cell is an endothelial cell of the vascular tree, which includes blood vessels and lymphatic vessels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endothelial tip cell fate specification
description: The process involved in the specification of identity of an endothelial tip cell. Once specification has taken place, a cell will be committed to differentiate down a specific pathway if left in its normal environment. An endothelial tip cell is a specialized endothelial cell localized to the leading edge of an angiogenic sprout that senses extracellular signals and guides the directed growth of blood vessels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endothelial stalk cell fate specification
description: The process involved in the specification of identity of an endothelial stalk cell. Once specification has taken place, a cell will be committed to differentiate down a specific pathway if left in its normal environment. An endothelial stalk cell is a specialized endothelial cell which follows behind the tip cell of an angiogenic sprout.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: postsynaptic membrane assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a postsynaptic membrane, a specialized area of membrane facing the presynaptic membrane on the tip of the nerve ending and separated from it by a minute cleft (the synaptic cleft).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: presynaptic membrane assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a presynaptic membrane, including any proteins associated with the membrane, but excluding other cellular components. A presynaptic membrane is a specialized area of membrane of the axon terminal that faces the plasma membrane of the neuron or muscle fiber with which the axon terminal establishes a synaptic junction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: postsynaptic density organization
synonyms: PSD organization|post synaptic density organization|post-synaptic density organization|postsynaptic density organisation
description: A process that results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a postsynaptic density, a region that lies adjacent to the cytoplasmic face of the postsynaptic membrane at excitatory synapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: postsynaptic density assembly
synonyms: PSD assembly|post synaptic density assembly|post-synaptic density assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a postsynaptic density, a region that lies adjacent to the cytoplasmic face of the postsynaptic membrane at excitatory synapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi intermediate compartment organization
synonyms: ER-Golgi intermediate compartment organization|ERGIC organization|endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi intermediate compartment organisation|endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi intermediate compartment organization and biogenesis
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-Golgi intermediate compartment.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: gamma-aminobutyric acid receptor clustering
description: The receptor clustering process in which gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptors are localized to distinct domains in the cell membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: AMPA glutamate receptor clustering
synonyms: AMPA receptor clustering|alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazole propionate selective glutamate receptor clustering
description: The glutamate receptor clustering process in which alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazole propionate (AMPA) receptors are localized to distinct domains in the cell membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: NMDA glutamate receptor clustering
description: The receptor clustering process in which N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors are localized to distinct domains in the cell membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neurexin clustering involved in presynaptic membrane assembly
description: The receptor clustering process involved in assembly of the presynaptic membrane in which neurexins are localized to distinct domains in the cell membrane. Neurexins are synaptic cell surface proteins which act as cell recognition molecules at nerve terminals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: gephyrin clustering involved in postsynaptic density assembly
description: The clustering process in which gephyrin molecules are localized to distinct domains in the postsynaptic density as part of postsynaptic density assembly. Gephyrin is a component of the postsynaptic protein network of inhibitory synapses.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: guanylate kinase-associated protein clustering
description: The clustering process in which guanylate kinase-associated proteins (GKAPs) are localized to distinct domains in the cell membrane. GKAP facilitates assembly of the post synaptic density of neurons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuroligin clustering involved in postsynaptic membrane assembly
description: The receptor clustering process involved in assembly of the postsynaptic membrane in which neuroligins are localized to distinct domains in the cell membrane. Neuroligins are neuronal cell surface proteins on the postsynaptic membrane that mediate synapse formation between neurons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: postsynaptic density protein 95 clustering
synonyms: Dlg4 clustering|PSD-95 clustering|post-synaptic density protein 95 clustering
description: The clustering process in which postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD-95) molecules are localized to distinct domains in the cell membrane. PSD-95 is mostly located in the post synaptic density of neurons, and is involved in anchoring synaptic proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: receptor localization to synapse
description: Any process in which a receptor is transported to, and/or maintained at the synapse, the junction between a nerve fiber of one neuron and another neuron or muscle fiber or glial cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuronal stem cell population maintenance
description: Any process in by an organism or tissue maintains a population of neuronal stem cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of inhibitory postsynaptic potential
synonyms: positive regulation of IPSP|positive regulation of inhibitory post-synaptic membrane potential
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of inhibitory postsynaptic potential (IPSP). IPSP is a temporary decrease in postsynaptic membrane potential due to the flow of negatively charged ions into the postsynaptic cell. The flow of ions that causes an IPSP is an inhibitory postsynaptic current (IPSC) and makes it more difficult for the neuron to fire an action potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mesenchymal cell apoptotic process
description: Any apoptotic process in a mesenchymal cell. A mesenchymal cell is a loosely associated cell that is part of the connective tissue in an organism. Mesenchymal cells give rise to more mature connective tissue cell types.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: GABAergic neuron differentiation
description: The process in which a neuroblast acquires the specialized structural and functional features of a GABAergic neuron.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fasciculation of sensory neuron axon
description: The collection of sensory neuron axons into a bundle of rods, known as a fascicle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fasciculation of motor neuron axon
description: The collection of motor neuron axons into a bundle of rods, known as a fascicle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: circadian regulation of translation
synonyms: regulation of mRNA translation in response to circadian clock
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of mRNA translation with a regularity of approximately 24 hours.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mesenchymal stem cell proliferation
description: The multiplication or reproduction of mesenchymal stem cells, resulting in the expansion of a stem cell population. A mesenchymal stem cell, or MSC, is a cell that retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized mesenchymal cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: epoxide metabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways involving epoxides, compounds in which an oxygen atom is directly attached to two adjacent or non-adjacent carbon atoms of a carbon chain or ring system; thus cyclic ethers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ruffle assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a ruffle, a projection at the leading edge of a crawling cell; the protrusions are supported by a microfilament meshwork. The formation of ruffles (also called membrane ruffling) is thought to be controlled by a group of enzymes known as Rho GTPases, specifically RhoA, Rac1 and cdc42.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to azide
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an azide stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: amelogenesis
description: The process whose specific outcome is the formation of tooth enamel, occurring in two stages: secretory stage and maturation stage.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dentinogenesis
description: The process whose specific outcome is the formation of dentin, the mineralized tissue that constitutes the major bulk of teeth. Dentin may be one of three types: primary dentin, secondary dentin, and tertiary dentin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: apoptotic signaling pathway
synonyms: apoptotic signalling pathway|induction of apoptosis by extracellular signals
description: The series of molecular signals which triggers the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway starts with reception of a signal, and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway
synonyms: death receptor-mediated apoptosis|extrinsic apoptosis|extrinsic apoptotic pathway|extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in presence of ligand|extrinsic apoptotic signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals in which a signal is conveyed from the cell surface to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway starts with either a ligand binding to a cell surface receptor, or a ligand being withdrawn from a cell surface receptor (e.g. in the case of signaling by dependence receptors), and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in absence of ligand
synonyms: dependence receptor signaling pathway|extrinsic apoptosis in absence of ligand|extrinsic apoptotic signalling pathway in absence of ligand
description: The series of molecular signals in which a signal is conveyed from the cell surface to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway starts with withdrawal of a ligand from a cell surface receptor, and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway
synonyms: induction of apoptosis by intracellular signals|intrinsic apoptosis|intrinsic apoptotic pathway|intrinsic apoptotic signalling pathway|mitochondrial-mediated apoptotic pathway
description: The series of molecular signals in which an intracellular signal is conveyed to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway starts with reception of an intracellular signal (e.g. DNA damage, endoplasmic reticulum stress, oxidative stress etc.), and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered. The intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway is crucially regulated by permeabilization of the mitochondrial outer membrane (MOMP).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: execution phase of apoptosis
description: A stage of the apoptotic process that starts with the controlled breakdown of the cell through the action of effector caspases or other effector molecules (e.g. cathepsins, calpains etc.). Key steps of the execution phase are rounding-up of the cell, retraction of pseudopodes, reduction of cellular volume (pyknosis), chromatin condensation, nuclear fragmentation (karyorrhexis), plasma membrane blebbing and fragmentation of the cell into apoptotic bodies. When the execution phase is completed, the cell has died.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pilomotor reflex
description: The reflex process in which the arrectores pilorum (hair follicle) muscles contract and cause the hair to stand erect.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: renal filtration
description: A renal system process in which fluid circulating through the body is filtered through a barrier system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to gonadotropin-releasing hormone
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulus. Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is a peptide hormone responsible for the release of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) from the anterior pituitary. GnRH is synthesized and released by the hypothalamus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to gonadotropin-releasing hormone
synonyms: cellular response to GnRH|cellular response to gonadotrophin-releasing hormone
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulus. Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is a peptide hormone responsible for the release of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) from the anterior pituitary. GnRH is synthesized and released by the hypothalamus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lysosomal membrane organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a lysosomal membrane. A lysosomal membrane is the lipid bilayer surrounding the lysosome and separating its contents from the cell cytoplasm.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of lysosomal membrane permeability
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the passage or uptake of molecules by the lysosomal membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of lysosomal membrane permeability
synonyms: positive regulation of lysosome membrane permeability
description: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the passage or uptake of molecules by the lysosomal membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial mRNA polyadenylation
description: The enzymatic addition of a sequence of 40-60 adenylyl residues at the 3' end of a eukaryotic mitochondrial mRNA primary transcript. Mitochondria contain both stabilizing and destabilizing poly(A) tails.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to toxic substance
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a toxic stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hematopoietic stem cell migration to bone marrow
synonyms: hematopoietic stem cell homing|hemopoietic stem cell migration to bone marrow|progenitor cell homing
description: The orderly movement of a hematopoietic stem cell into the bone marrow, and its subsequent positioning within defined functional compartments in that microenvironment. A hematopoietic stem cell is a cell from which all cells of the lymphoid and myeloid lineages develop, including blood cells and cells of the immune system.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: amyloid-beta clearance
description: The process in which amyloid-beta is removed from extracellular brain regions by mechanisms involving cell surface receptors.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial respirasome assembly
synonyms: mitochondrial respiratory chain supercomplex assembly|mitochondrial respiratory supercomplex assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of respiratory enzyme complexes I, III and IV of the mitochondrial inner membrane to form a large supercomplex.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: oligodendrocyte apoptotic process
description: Any apoptotic process in an oligodendrocyte. Oligodendrocytes belong to a class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system, where they form the insulating myelin sheath of axons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: renal tubular secretion
description: The elimination of substances from peritubular capillaries (or surrounding hemolymph in invertebrates) into the renal tubules to be incorporated subsequently into the urine. Substances that are secreted include organic anions, ammonia, potassium and drugs.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: self proteolysis
description: The hydrolysis of proteins into smaller polypeptides and/or amino acids by cleavage of their own peptide bonds.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: omega-hydroxylase P450 pathway
description: The chemical reactions and pathways by which arachidonic acid is converted to other compounds initially by omega-hydroxylation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ammonium homeostasis
description: Any biological process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of ammonium.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intracellular ammonium homeostasis
description: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of ammonium within a cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: complement-dependent cytotoxicity
description: Cell killing caused by the membrane attack complex formed following complement activation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hepatocyte apoptotic process
description: Any apoptotic process in a hepatocyte, the main structural component of the liver.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: renal phosphate ion absorption
description: A renal system process in which phosphate ions are taken up from the collecting ducts and proximal and distal loops of the nephron. In non-mammalian species, absorption may occur in related structures.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: 'de novo' XMP biosynthetic process
synonyms: \'de novo\' XMP anabolism|\'de novo\' XMP biosynthesis|\'de novo\' XMP formation|\'de novo\' XMP synthesis
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of XMP, xanthosine monophosphate, from simpler precursors.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of nucleus size
synonyms: regulation of nuclear size|regulation of nuclear volume
description: Any process that modulates the size of the nucleus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: programmed necrotic cell death
synonyms: programmed cell death by necrosis|regulated necrosis
description: A necrotic cell death process that results from the activation of endogenous cellular processes, such as signaling involving death domain receptors or Toll-like receptors.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to alcohol
synonyms: process resulting in tolerance to alcohol
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an alcohol stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: plasma membrane tubulation
description: A membrane tubulation process occurring in a plasma membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: B cell adhesion
description: The attachment of a B cell to another cell via adhesion molecules.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: melanocyte migration
description: The orderly movement of melanocytes from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism. A melanocyte is a pigment cell derived from the neural crest. It contains melanin-filled pigment granules, which give a brown to black appearance.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: melanocyte proliferation
description: The multiplication or reproduction of melanocytes, resulting in the expansion of a cell population. A melanocyte is a pigment cell derived from the neural crest. It contains melanin-filled pigment granules, which give a brown to black appearance.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: melanocyte adhesion
description: The attachment of a melanocyte to another cell via adhesion molecules.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to antineoplastic agent
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an antineoplastic agent stimulus. An antineoplastic agent is a substance that inhibits or prevents the proliferation of neoplasms.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to antipsychotic drug
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an antipsychotic drug stimulus. Antipsychotic drugs are agents that control agitated psychotic behaviour, alleviate acute psychotic states, reduce psychotic symptoms, and exert a quieting effect.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: zymogen inhibition
description: Any process that prevents the proteolytic processing of an inactive enzyme to an active form.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ripoptosome assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a ripoptosome, a protein complex whose formation can induce an extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway or a necroptotic signaling pathway. The composition of this protein complex may depend on several factors including nature of the signal, cell type and more.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization
synonyms: MOMP|mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization during apoptotic cell death|mitochondrion outer membrane permeabilization
description: The process by which the mitochondrial outer membrane becomes permeable to the passing of proteins and other molecules from the intermembrane space to the cytosol as part of the apoptotic signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neutrophil clearance
description: The selective elimination of senescent neutrophils from the body by autoregulatory mechanisms.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: autophagosome maturation
synonyms: autophagic vacuole fusion|autophagic vacuole maturation|autophagosome fusion
description: Removal of PI3P and Atg8/LC3 after the closure of the phagophore and before the fusion with the endosome/lysosome (e.g. mammals and insects) or vacuole (yeast), and that very likely destabilizes other Atg proteins and thus enables their efficient dissociation and recycling.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to heterochromatin
description: Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, a part of a chromosome that is organized into heterochromatin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: UDP-glucosylation
description: The covalent attachment of a UDP-glucose residue to a substrate molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment of Sertoli cell barrier
synonyms: establishment of BTB|establishment of SCB|establishment of blood-testis barrier
description: Establishment of a structure near the basement membrane in adjacent Sertoli cells of the seminiferous epithelium for maintaining spermatogenesis. The structure consists of tight junctions, basal ectoplasmic specializations, and desmosome-like junctions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sensory neuron axon guidance
description: The process in which the migration of an axon growth cone of a sensory neuron is directed to a specific target site in response to a combination of attractive and repulsive cues. A sensory neuron is an afferent neuron conveying sensory impulses.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dorsal spinal cord interneuron posterior axon guidance
description: The process in which the migration of an axon growth cone of a dorsal spinal cord interneuron is directed to a specific target site in the posterior direction along the anterior-posterior body axis in response to a combination of attractive and repulsive cues. The anterior-posterior axis is defined by a line that runs from the head or mouth of an organism to the tail or opposite end of the organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dorsal spinal cord interneuron anterior axon guidance
description: The process in which the migration of an axon growth cone of a dorsal spinal cord interneuron is directed to a specific target site in the anterior direction along the anterior-posterior body axis in response to a combination of attractive and repulsive cues. The anterior-posterior axis is defined by a line that runs from the head or mouth of an organism to the tail or opposite end of the organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to interleukin-17
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an interleukin-17 stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: interleukin-17-mediated signaling pathway
synonyms: IL-17-mediated signaling pathway|IL-17-mediated signalling pathway|interleukin-17-mediated signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by interleukin-17 binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synaptic vesicle lumen acidification
synonyms: synaptic vesicle lumen pH reduction|synaptic vesicle proton loading
description: The acidification of the synaptic vesicle lumen via transport of protons into the vesicle. The resulting electrochemical gradient powers neurotransmitter loading.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuroblast migration
description: The orderly movement of a neuroblast from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism or multicellular structure. A neuroblast is any cell that will divide and give rise to a neuron.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to raffinose
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a raffinose stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha signaling pathway
synonyms: HIF1alpha pathway|hypoxia-inducible factor signaling|hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals mediated by hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF1) in response to lowered oxygen levels (hypoxia). Under hypoxic conditions, the oxygen-sensitive alpha-subunit of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1 dimerizes with a HIF1-beta subunit (also called ARNT or aryl-hydrocarbon-receptor nuclear translocator), translocates to the nucleus and activates transcription of genes whose products participate in responding to hypoxia.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: liver regeneration
description: The regrowth of lost or destroyed liver.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: supramolecular fiber organization
synonyms: extracellular fibril organisation|extracellular fibril organization|extracellular fibril organization and biogenesis|fibril organisation|fibril organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a supramolecular fiber, a polymer consisting of an indefinite number of protein or protein complex subunits that have polymerised to form a fiber-shaped structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ubiquitin-dependent glycoprotein ERAD pathway
synonyms: ER-associated glycoprotein degradation|glycoprotein ERAD|gpERAD|misfolded or incompletely synthesized glycoprotein catabolic process
description: An ERAD pathway whereby endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident glycoproteins are targeted for degradation. Includes differential processing of the glycoprotein sugar chains, retrotranslocation to the cytosol and degradation by the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. A glycoprotein is a compound in which a carbohydrate component is covalently bound to a protein component.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: programmed cell death in response to reactive oxygen species
synonyms: PCD in response to oxidative stress|PCD in response to reactive oxygen species|programmed cell death in response to oxidative stress|reactive oxygen species-mediated PCD|reactive oxygen species-mediated programmed cell death
description: Cell death resulting from activation of endogenous cellular processes and occurring as a result of a reactive oxygen species stimulus. Reactive oxygen species include singlet oxygen, superoxide, and oxygen free radicals.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: motor neuron migration
description: The orderly movement of a motor neuron from one site to another. A motor neuron is an efferent neuron that passes from the central nervous system or a ganglion toward or to a muscle and conducts an impulse that causes movement.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lateral motor column neuron migration
description: The orderly movement of a lateral motor column neuron from one site to another. A lateral motor column neuron is a motor neuron that is generated only on limb levels and send axons into the limb mesenchyme.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dendrite extension
description: Long distance growth of a single dendrite involved in cellular development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuron projection guidance
synonyms: neurite guidance|neuron process guidance|neuron protrusion guidance|neuronal cell projection guidance
description: The process in which the migration of a neuron projection is directed to a specific target site in response to a combination of attractive and repulsive cues.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sympathetic neuron projection extension
synonyms: sympathetic neurite extension|sympathetic neuron process extension|sympathetic neuron protrusion extension|sympathetic neuronal cell projection extension
description: Long distance growth of a single sympathetic neuron projection involved in cellular development. A neuron projection is a prolongation or process extending from a nerve cell, e.g. an axon or dendrite.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sympathetic neuron projection guidance
synonyms: sympathetic neurite guidance|sympathetic neuron process guidance|sympathetic neuron protrusion guidance|sympathetic neuronal cell projection guidance
description: The process in which the migration of a sympathetic neuron projection is directed to a specific target site in response to a combination of attractive and repulsive cues.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sympathetic neuron axon guidance
synonyms: sympathetic neuron axon chemotaxis|sympathetic neuron axon growth cone guidance|sympathetic neuron axon pathfinding
description: The chemotaxis process that directs the migration of a sympathetic neuron axon growth cone to a specific target site in response to a combination of attractive and repulsive cues.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of vesicle size
description: Any process that modulates the size of a vesicle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: blood vessel endothelial cell delamination
description: The process of negative regulation of cell adhesion that results in blood vessel endothelial cells splitting off from an existing endothelial sheet.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to non-motile cilium
synonyms: protein localization to nonmotile primary cilium
description: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a location within a non-motile cilium.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: receptor localization to non-motile cilium
synonyms: receptor localization to nonmotile primary cilium
description: A process in which a receptor is transported to, or maintained in, a location within a non-motile cilium.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sialylation
description: The covalent attachment of sialic acid to a substrate molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: base-excision repair, AP site formation via deaminated base removal
description: A base-excision repair, AP site formation process occurring via excision of a deaminated base.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: necroptotic signaling pathway
synonyms: necroptosis signaling|necroptosis signaling pathway|necroptotic signal transduction|necroptotic signalling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals which triggers the necroptotic death of a cell. The pathway starts with reception of a signal, is characterized by activation of receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 and/or 3 (RIPK1/3, also called RIP1/3), and ends when the execution phase of necroptosis is triggered.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: execution phase of necroptosis
synonyms: execution phase of necroptotic process|necroptosis|necroptotic execution phase
description: A stage of the necroptotic process that starts after a necroptotic signal has been relayed to the execution machinery. Key steps of the execution phase are swelling of organelles, minor ultrastructural modifications of the nucleus (specifically, dilatation of the nuclear membrane and condensation of chromatin into small, irregular, circumscribed patches) and increased cell volume (oncosis), culminating in the disruption of the plasma membrane and subsequent loss of intracellular contents. The execution phase ends when the cell has died.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: granulocyte migration
description: The movement of a granulocyte within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular stress response to acid chemical
synonyms: cellular response to acid stress|cellular stress response to acid
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a disturbance in cellular homeostasis caused by the chemical structure of the anion portion of a dissociated acid (rather than the acid acting as a proton donor). The acid chemical may be in gaseous, liquid or solid form.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lymphoid lineage cell migration into thymus
synonyms: lymphoid lineage restricted progenitor cell migration into thymus
description: The movement of a lymphoid lineage cell (also called a lymphoid lineage restricted progenitor cell) into the thymus. Lymphoid lineage cells enter and exit the thymus several times as part of this process.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: thymus epithelium morphogenesis
description: The process in which the thymus epithelium is generated and organized.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial double-strand break repair via homologous recombination
description: The repair of a double-strand break in mitochondrial DNA in which the broken DNA molecule is repaired using homologous sequences.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: calcium ion transmembrane import into cytosol
synonyms: calcium transmembrane import into cytosol|cytosolic calcium ion transport
description: A process in which a calcium ion is transported from one side of a membrane to the other into the cytosol by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vacuole fusion
description: Merging of two or more vacuoles, or of vacuoles and vesicles within a cell to form a single larger vacuole.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lamellipodium organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a lamellipodium. A lamellipodium is a thin sheetlike process extended by the leading edge of a crawling fibroblast; contains a dense meshwork of actin filaments.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: potassium ion export across plasma membrane
synonyms: potassium export|potassium export across plasma membrane|potassium ion export|potassium ion export from cell
description: The directed movement of potassium ions from inside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the extracellular region.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-arginine import across plasma membrane
description: The directed movement of L-arginine from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-lysine import across plasma membrane
description: The directed movement of L-lysine from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-ornithine import across plasma membrane
description: The directed movement of L-ornithine from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: calcitonin family receptor signaling pathway
description: A G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by an extracellular member of the calcitonin family (e.g. adrenomedullin, adrenomedullin 2 (intermedin), amylin, calcitonin and calcitonin gene-related peptides (CGRPs)) binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: amylin receptor signaling pathway
description: A G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway initiated by amylin binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: double-strand break repair via classical nonhomologous end joining
description: An instance of double-strand break repair via nonhomologous end joining that requires a number of factors important for V(D)J recombination, including the KU70/80 heterodimer (KU), XRCC4, ligase IV, and DNA-PKcs in mammals. It does not produce translocations (as opposed to the alternative nonhomologous end joining).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: double-strand break repair via alternative nonhomologous end joining
synonyms: A-NHEJ|MMEJ|alt-NHEJ|double-strand break repair via microhomology-mediated end joining
description: An instance of double-strand break repair via nonhomologous end joining that is independent of factors important for V(D)J recombination (as opposed to classical nonhomologous end joining). It often results in a deletion with microhomology (i.e. 5-25bp homology) at the repair junction. Among different subclasses of nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ), alternative NHEJ appears to play a significant role in the etiology of mutations that arise during cancer development and treatment.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment of RNA localization to telomere
synonyms: establishment of RNA localisation to telomere
description: The directed movement of RNA to a specific location in the telomeric region of a chromosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment of protein-containing complex localization to telomere
synonyms: establishment of macromolecular complex localisation to telomere|establishment of macromolecular complex localization to telomere
description: The directed movement of a protein-containing macromolecular complex to a specific location in the telomeric region of a chromosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell surface receptor signaling pathway via STAT
synonyms: STAT signalling pathway|kinase activated-STAT cascade|kinase-STAT cascade|receptor signaling pathway via STAT
description: An intracellular signal transduction process in which STAT proteins (Signal Transducers and Activators of Transcription) convey a signal to trigger a change in the activity or state of a cell. The STAT cascade begins with receptor activation followed by activation of STAT proteins by kinases. It proceeds through STA dimerization and subsequent nuclear translocation of STAT proteins, and ends with regulation of target gene expression by STAT proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: telomere maintenance via base-excision repair
description: A telomere maintenance process that occurs by base-excision repair of telomeric DNA in response to DNA damage. Telomeric sequences are particularly susceptible to oxidative DNA damage, due to their G-rich nature.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vascular endothelial cell response to fluid shear stress
synonyms: blood vessel endothelial cell response to fluid shear stress
description: Any response to fluid shear stress in a vascular endothelial cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vascular endothelial cell response to laminar fluid shear stress
synonyms: blood vessel endothelial cell response to laminar fluid shear stress
description: Any response to laminar fluid shear stress in a vascular endothelial cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vascular endothelial cell response to oscillatory fluid shear stress
synonyms: blood vessel endothelial cell response to oscillatory fluid shear stress
description: Any response to oscillatory fluid shear stress that occurs in a vascular endothelial cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ferroptosis
description: A programmed cell death characterized morphologically by the presence of smaller than normal mitochondria with condensed mitochondrial membrane densities, reduction or vanishing of mitochondria crista, and outer mitochondrial membrane rupture. Activation of mitochondrial voltage-dependent anion channels and mitogen-activated protein kinases, upregulation of endoplasmic reticulum stress, and inhibition of cystine/glutamate antiporter are involved in the induction of ferroptosis. This process is characterized by the accumulation of lipid peroxidation products and lethal reactive oxygen species (ROS) derived from iron metabolism. Glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), heat shock protein beta-1, and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 function as negative regulators of ferroptosis by limiting ROS production and reducing cellular iron uptake, respectively. In contrast, NADPH oxidase and p53 act as positive regulators of ferroptosis by promotion of ROS production and inhibition of expression of SLC7A11 (a specific light-chain subunit of the cystine/glutamate antiporter), respectively. Misregulated ferroptosis has been implicated in multiple physiological and pathological processes.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neural tissue regeneration
description: The regrowth of neural tissue following its loss or destruction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: calcineurin-mediated signaling
description: Any intracellular signal transduction in which the signal is passed on within the cell by activation of a transcription factor as a consequence of dephosphorylation by Ca(2+)-activated calcineurin. The process begins with calcium-dependent activation of the phosphatase calcineurin. Calcineurin is a calcium- and calmodulin-dependent serine/threonine protein phosphatase with a conserved function in eukaryotic species from yeast to humans. In yeast and fungi, calcineurin regulates stress signaling and cell cycle, and sporulation and virulence in pathogenic fungi. In metazoans, calcineurin is involved in cell commitment, organogenesis and organ development and immune function of T-lymphocytes. By a conserved mechanism, calcineurin phosphatase activates fungal Crz1 and mammalian NFATc by dephosphorylation and translocation of these transcription factors to the nucleus to regulate gene expression.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: extracellular exosome biogenesis
synonyms: ILV assembly|exosome assembly or secretion|exosome biogenesis|exosome production|intraluminal vesicle assembly
description: The assembly and secretion of an extracellular exosome, a membrane-bounded vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: renal urate salt excretion
description: The elimination of urate salt or uric acid from peritubular capillaries (or surrounding hemolymph in invertebrates) into the renal tubules to be incorporated subsequently into the urine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial tRNA 5'-end processing
description: The process in which the 5' end of a pre-tRNA molecule is converted to that of a mature tRNA in the mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: blood vessel diameter maintenance
synonyms: blood vessel diameter homeostasis|regulation of blood vessel diameter|regulation of blood vessel size|regulation of vasodilatation|regulation of vasodilation
description: Any process that modulates the diameter of blood vessels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: membrane tubulation
description: A membrane organization process resulting in the formation of a tubular projection. This may face inwardly (as in tubular membrane invaginations) or outwardly (as in endosomal tubules).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endosome membrane tubulation
description: A membrane tubulation process occurring in an endosome membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of DNA stability
description: Any process that modulates the stability of DNA.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: membrane bending
description: A membrane organization process resulting in the bending of a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endothelial to hematopoietic transition
description: The generation of hematopoietic stem cells from hemogenic endothelial cells by a process that includes tight-junction dissolution and loss of cell polarity followed by delamination from the endothelium.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuromuscular junction development, skeletal muscle fiber
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a neuromuscular junction that targets a skeletal muscle fiber.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of strand invasion
synonyms: positive regulation of D-loop biosynthesis|positive regulation of D-loop formation|positive regulation of Rad51-mediated strand invasion
description: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of strand invasion. Strand invasion is the process in which the nucleoprotein complex (composed of the broken single-strand DNA and the recombinase) searches and identifies a region of homology in intact duplex DNA. The broken single-strand DNA displaces the like strand and forms Watson-Crick base pairs with its complement, forming a duplex in which each strand is from one of the two recombining DNA molecules.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: centriole assembly
description: A cellular process that results in the assembly of one or more centrioles.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: de novo centriole assembly involved in multi-ciliated epithelial cell differentiation
synonyms: centriole amplification|de novo centriole assembly|de novo centriole assembly via deuterosome|deuterosomal basal body biogenesis|deuterosome pathway|deuterosome-mediated centriole biogenesis|multiciliation|multiciliogenesis
description: Centriole assembly in which a centriole arises de novo by a process involving an electron-dense structure known as a deuterosome, rather than by duplication of an existing centriole, and occurring as part of multi-ciliated epithelial cell differentiation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: defense response to other organism
synonyms: defence response incompatible interaction|defence response to pathogen|incompatible interaction|defense response|incompatible interaction|resistance response to pathogen
description: Reactions triggered in response to the presence of another organism that act to protect the cell or organism from damage caused by that organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: learned vocalization behavior
description: A vocalization behavior that is the result of learning.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to virus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a virus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell-cell adhesion
description: The attachment of one cell to another cell via adhesion molecules.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: trans-Golgi network membrane organization
description: A process which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a trans-Golgi network membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: monoatomic cation transmembrane transport
synonyms: ATP hydrolysis coupled cation transmembrane transport|cation transmembrane transport
description: The process in which a monoatomic cation is transported across a membrane. Monatomic cations (also called simple cations) are positively charged ions consisting of exactly one atom.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: monoatomic anion transmembrane transport
synonyms: ATP hydrolysis coupled anion transmembrane transport|anion transmembrane transport
description: The process in which a monoatomic anion is transported across a membrane. Monatomic anions (also called simple anions) are negatively charged ions consisting of exactly one atom.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: import into cell
description: The directed movement of some substance from outside of a cell into a cell. This may occur via transport across the plasma membrane or via endocytosis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: inorganic anion import across plasma membrane
description: The directed movement of inorganic anions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: inorganic cation import across plasma membrane
description: The directed movement of inorganic cations from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: G protein-coupled serotonin receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: G-protein coupled serotonin receptor signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of a G protein-coupled serotonin receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: entry receptor-mediated virion attachment to host cell
synonyms: viral attachment to host entry receptor
description: The process by which a virion attaches to a host cell by binding to a receptor on the host cell surface that mediates/triggers viral entry by endocytosis/pinocytosis or by inducing fusion/penetration.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of synaptic vesicle cycle
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the synaptic vesicle cycle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of synaptic vesicle budding from presynaptic endocytic zone membrane
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of synaptic vesicle budding from presynaptic endocytic zone membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of neurotransmitter receptor localization to postsynaptic specialization membrane
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of neurotransmitter receptor localization to postsynaptic specialization membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: postsynaptic specialization assembly
description: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a postsynaptic specialization, a region that lies adjacent to the cytoplasmic face of the postsynaptic membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neurotransmitter loading into synaptic vesicle
synonyms: neurotransmitter import into synaptic vesicle|neurotransmitter uptake into synaptic vesicle|synaptic vesicle neurotransmitter loading
description: The active transport of neurotransmitters into a synaptic vesicle. This import is fuelled by an electrochemical gradient across the vesicle membrane, established by the action of proton pumps.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: calcium ion import across plasma membrane
synonyms: calcium ion import into cell|calcium ion uptake into cell
description: The directed movement of calcium ions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: D-glucose import across plasma membrane
synonyms: glucose import across plasma membrane|glucose import into cell|high affinity glucose import
description: The directed movement of D-glucose from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: iron ion import across plasma membrane
synonyms: ferrous ion import into cell|ferrous iron import across plasma membrane|ferrous iron import into cell|iron import into cell|iron ion import into cell
description: The directed movement of iron ions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: L-glutamate import across plasma membrane
synonyms: L-glutamate import into cell|L-glutamate(1-) import across plasma membrane|L-glutamate(1-) import into cell
description: The directed movement of L-glutamate from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sodium ion import across plasma membrane
synonyms: sodium import|sodium ion import|sodium ion import into cell
description: The directed movement of sodium ions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: symmetric cell division
description: Cell division in which both daughter cells are of the same type.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: maintenance of cell number
description: Any process by which the numbers of cells of a particular type or in a tissue are maintained.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: macromolecule depalmitoylation
description: The removal of palymitoyl groups from a macromolecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of the force of heart contraction
description: Any process that increases the force of heart muscle contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of the force of heart contraction
description: Any process that decreases the force of heart muscle contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein insertion into plasma membrane
description: The process that results in the incorporation of a protein into a plasma membrane. Incorporation in this context means having some part or covalently attached group that is inserted into the the hydrophobic region of one or both bilayers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: import across plasma membrane
description: The directed movement of some substance from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cell aggregation
description: The clustering together and adhesion of initially separate cells to form an aggregate. Examples include the clustering of unicellular organisms or blood cells in suspension and the condensation of mesenchymal cells during cartilage formation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fast, calcium ion-dependent exocytosis of neurotransmitter
description: The fast, initial phase of calcium ion-induced neurotransmitter release, via exocytosis, into the synaptic cleft. This depends on low affinity calcium sensors and typically begins a fraction of a millisecond after Ca2+ influx, and decays rapidly (1-10ms) with a decay constant of around 5-10ms. The underlying molecular mechanisms of this process are distinct from those of the later, slow phase of release.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: detoxification
description: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of a toxic substance. These may include transport of the toxic substance away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of the toxic substance.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to interleukin-8
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an interleukin-8 stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to interleukin-7
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an interleukin-7 stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: inorganic ion homeostasis
description: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of inorganic ions within an organism or cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: skin epidermis development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the skin epidermis over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to mitochondrial depolarisation
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) in response to the depolarization of one or more mitochondria.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: biofilm matrix disassembly
description: A process that results in the disassembly of a biofilm matrix.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: xenophagy
description: The selective degradation of intracellular pathogen or some part of an intracellular pathogen (e.g. viral capsid) by macroautophagy.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: global gene silencing by mRNA cleavage
synonyms: RNA interference|targeting of mRNA for destruction|gene silencing by mRNA cleavage|mRNA cleavage involved in gene silencing|mRNA destabilization-mediated gene silencing|targeting of mRNA for destruction involved in RNA interference
description: A posttranscriptional gene silencing pathway that involves the cleavage of mRNAs in a non-gene-specific manner.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neurotransmitter reuptake
description: The directed movement of neurotransmitter molecules from the extrasynaptic space into the presynaptic cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nuclear chromosome segregation
description: The process in which genetic material, in the form of nuclear chromosomes, is organized into specific structures and then physically separated and apportioned to two or more sets. Nuclear chromosome segregation begins with the condensation of chromosomes, includes chromosome separation, and ends when chromosomes have completed movement to the spindle poles.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: spontaneous synaptic transmission
description: The low level of synaptic transmission that occurs via spontaneous neurotransmitter release into the synaptic cleft in the absence of a presynaptic action potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: modulation of excitatory postsynaptic potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of excitatory postsynaptic potential (EPSP). EPSP is a process that leads to a temporary increase in postsynaptic potential due to the flow of positively charged ions into the postsynaptic cell. The flow of ions that causes an EPSP is an excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) and makes it easier for the neuron to fire an action potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: modulation of inhibitory postsynaptic potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of inhibitory postsynaptic potential (IPSP). IPSP is a temporary decrease in postsynaptic membrane potential due to the flow of negatively charged ions into the postsynaptic cell. The flow of ions that causes an IPSP is an inhibitory postsynaptic current (IPSC) and makes it more difficult for the neuron to fire an action potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intestinal folate absorption
description: Uptake of folic into the blood by absorption from the small intestine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: folate transmembrane transport
synonyms: folic acid transmembrane transport|reduced folate transmembrane transport
description: The process in which a folic acid, or one of its derivatives (dihydrofolate, tetrahydrofolate, methylene-tetrahydrofolate or methyl-tetrahydrofolate) is transported across a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein transport along microtubule
description: The directed movement of a protein along a microtubule, mediated by motor proteins.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular detoxification of cadmium ion
description: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of cadmium cations in a cell. These include transport of cadmium cations away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intestinal lipid absorption
description: A process in which lipids are taken up from the contents of the intestine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intramembranous bone growth
description: The increase in size or mass of an intramembranous bone that contributes to the shaping of the bone.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bone growth
description: The increase in size or mass of a bone that contributes to the shaping of that bone.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular oxidant detoxification
description: Any process carried out at the cellular level that reduces or removes the toxicity superoxide radicals or hydrogen peroxide.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: action potential propagation
description: The propagation of an action potential along the plane of an excitable membrane. Action potentials typically propagate once triggered because the depolarization of adjacent membrane regions due to an action potential crosses the firing threshold.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vesicle-mediated transport to the plasma membrane
description: The directed movement of substances to the plasma membrane in transport vesicles that fuse with the plasma membrane by exocytosis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: maintenance of postsynaptic specialization structure
description: A process which maintains the organization and the arrangement of proteins in the presynaptic specialization.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: synapse pruning
description: A cellular process that results in the controlled breakdown of synapse. After it starts the process is continuous until the synapse has disappeared.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: postsynaptic neurotransmitter receptor internalization
description: A receptor-mediated endocytosis process that results in the internalization of a neurotransmitter receptor from the postsynaptic membrane endocytic zone into an endocytic vesicle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: modification of postsynaptic actin cytoskeleton
description: Any process that modifies the structure of a postsynaptic actin cytoskeleton.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neurotransmitter receptor transport, endosome to postsynaptic membrane
description: The directed movement of neurotransmitter receptor from the postsynaptic endosome to the postsynaptic membrane in transport vesicles.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of action potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cardiac muscle cell action potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a cardiac muscle cell. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of membrane depolarization during action potential
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of membrane depolarization during an action potential. Membrane depolarization is the process in which membrane potential changes in the depolarizing direction from the resting potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of membrane repolarization during action potential
description: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of membrane repolarization during an action potential. Membrane repolarization is the process in which membrane potential changes in the repolarizing direction, towards the resting potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of AV node cell action potential
synonyms: regulation of AV node cardiac muscle cell action potential|regulation of atrioventricular node cardiac muscle cell action potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in an atrioventricular node myocyte. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of bundle of His cell action potential
synonyms: regulation of bundle of His cardiac muscle cell action potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a cardiac muscle cell of the bundle of His. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of Purkinje myocyte action potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a Purkinje myocyte. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of SA node cell action potential
synonyms: regulation of SA node cardiac muscle cell action potential|regulation of SAN cardiac muscle cell action potential|regulation of sinoatrial node cardiac muscle cell action potential|regulation of sinus node cardiac muscle cell action potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in an SA node cardiac myocyte. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of neuronal action potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a neuron. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cardiac muscle cell action potential involved in regulation of contraction
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a cardiac muscle cell contributing to the regulation of its contraction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of atrial cardiac muscle cell action potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in an atrial cardiac muscle cell contributing to the regulation of its contraction. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of ventricular cardiac muscle cell action potential
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a ventricular cardiac muscle cell contributing to the regulation of its contraction. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: membrane depolarization during atrial cardiac muscle cell action potential
synonyms: atrial cardiac muscle cell depolarization|atrial depolarization|electrocardiogram PR interval
description: The process in which atrial cardiac muscle cell membrane potential changes in the depolarizing direction from the negative resting potential towards the positive membrane potential that will be the peak of the action potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: membrane repolarization during atrial cardiac muscle cell action potential
description: The process in which ions are transported across a membrane such that the atrial cardiomyocyte membrane potential changes in the direction from the positive membrane potential at the peak of the action potential towards the negative resting potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: membrane repolarization during ventricular cardiac muscle cell action potential
synonyms: electrocardiogram T wave|regulation of ventricular cardiac muscle repolarization|ventricular repolarization
description: The process in which ions are transported across a membrane such that the ventricular cardiomyocyte membrane potential changes in the direction from the positive membrane potential at the peak of the action potential towards the negative resting potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retrograde trans-synaptic signaling by endocannabinoid
description: Cell-cell signaling from postsynapse to presynapse, across the synaptic cleft, mediated by an endocannabinoid ligand.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retrograde trans-synaptic signaling by nitric oxide, modulating synaptic transmission
description: Modulation of synaptic transmission by cell-cell signaling from postsynapse to presynapse, across the synaptic cleft, mediated by nitric oxide.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: postsynaptic signal transduction
description: Signal transduction in which the initial step occurs in a postsynapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: axonal transport
description: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules in axons.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dendritic transport
description: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules in dendrites.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anterograde dendritic transport
description: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules from the cell body toward the postsynapse in dendrites.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dendritic transport of mitochondrion
description: The directed movement of mitochondria along microtubules in nerve cell dendrites.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retrograde trans-synaptic signaling by trans-synaptic protein complex
description: Cell-cell signaling from postsynapse to presynapse, across the synaptic cleft, mediated by trans-synaptic protein complex.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neurotransmitter receptor transport, postsynaptic endosome to lysosome
description: The directed movement of neurotransmitter receptor from the postsynaptic endosome in tranpsort vesicles to the lysosome for degradation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anterograde axonal transport of mitochondrion
description: The directed movement of mitochondria along microtubules in axons away from the cell body and towards the presynapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: retrograde axonal transport of mitochondrion
description: The directed movement of mitochondria along microtubules in axons towards the cell body and away from the presynapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dendritic transport of messenger ribonucleoprotein complex
synonyms: dendritic transport of mRNA RNP complex
description: The directed movement of a messenger ribonucleoprotein complex along microtubules in nerve cell dendrites.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anterograde dendritic transport of messenger ribonucleoprotein complex
synonyms: anterograde dendritic transport of mRNA RNP complex
description: The directed movement of a messenger ribonucleoprotein complex along microtubules in nerve cell dendrites towards the postsynapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: exocytic insertion of neurotransmitter receptor to postsynaptic membrane
description: The exocytic fusion of neurotransmitter receptor containing vesicles with the postsynaptic membrane resulting in the integration of NT receptors, enabling them to participate in neurotransmitter reception. This process includes tethering and docking steps that prepare vesicles for fusion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neurotransmitter receptor transport postsynaptic membrane to endosome
description: Vesicle-mediated transport of a neurotransmitter receptor complex from the postsynaptic membrane to the postsynaptic early endosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: postsynaptic neurotransmitter receptor diffusion trapping
description: The process by which diffusing neurotransmitter receptor becomes trapped at the postsynaptic specialization membrane. This is typically due to interaction with components of the post-synaptic specialization.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anterograde dendritic transport of neurotransmitter receptor complex
description: The directed movement of a neurotransmitter receptor complex along microtubules in nerve cell dendrites towards the postsynapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: postsynaptic actin cytoskeleton organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising actin filaments and their associated proteins in the postsynaptic actin cytoskeleton.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: excitatory chemical synaptic transmission
description: Synaptic transmission that results in an excitatory postsynaptic potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: inhibitory chemical synaptic transmission
description: Synaptic transmission that results in an inhibitory postsynaptic potential.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of modification of synapse structure, modulating synaptic transmission
description: Any process that regulates the modification of synaptic structure and as a result regulates synaptic transmission.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: NMDA selective glutamate receptor signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by glutamate binding to an NMDA-selective glutamate receptor on the surface of the target cell, followed by the movement of ions through a channel in the receptor complex, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: AMPA selective glutamate receptor signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by glutamate binding to an AMPA-selective glutamate receptor on the surface of the target cell, followed by the movement of ions through a channel in the receptor complex, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vesicle-mediated transport in synapse
description: Any vesicle-mediated transport that occurs in a synapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: modification of postsynaptic structure
description: Any process that modifies the structure of a postsynapse.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuronal dense core vesicle exocytosis
description: The secretion of molecules (e.g. neuropeptides, insulin-related peptides or neuromodulators such as serotonin and dopamine) contained within a neuronal dense core vesicle by fusion of the granule with the plasma membrane of a neuron in response to increased cytosolic calcium levels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: maintenance of protein localization at cell tip
synonyms: maintenance of protein location at cell tip
description: Any process in which localization of a protein is maintained at the cell tip.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: sphingolipid translocation
description: The movement of a sphingolipid molecule from one leaflet of a membrane bilayer to the opposite leaflet.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ceramide translocation
description: The movement of a ceramide molecule from one leaflet of a membrane bilayer to the opposite leaflet.

label: BiologicalProcess
