A paranodal junction flanks the node of Ranvier in myelinated nerve, electrically isolates the myelinated from unmyelinated nerve segments, and physically separates the voltage-gated sodium channels at the node from the cluster of potassium channels underneath the myelin sheath.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to leucine starvation
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of deprivation of leucine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: signal clustering
description: Grouping of multiple copies of a signal at a cellular location. May promote receptor clustering and alter the signal transduction response.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pre-mRNA catabolic process
description: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of the unspliced pre-mRNA (pre-messenger RNA).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: anti-Mullerian hormone receptor signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by the binding of anti-Mullerian hormone to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription. Upon ligand binding, the receptor  forms a complex consisting of two type II and two type I transmembrane serine/threonine kinases. Type II receptors phosphorylate and activate type I receptors which autophosphorylate, then bind and activate SMAD transcriptional regulators.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: peptidyl-tyrosine dephosphorylation involved in inactivation of protein kinase activity
description: Any peptidyl-tyrosine dephosphorylation that is involved in inactivation of protein kinase activity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neutrophil migration
description: The movement of a neutrophil within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to transition metal nanoparticle
synonyms: response to colloidal metal|response to neutral metal atoms
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a transition metal nanoparticle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to gold nanoparticle
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a gold nanoparticle stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: RNA localization to chromatin
description: A process in which RNA is transported to and maintained in a part of a chromosome that is organized into chromatin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to insulin-like growth factor stimulus
synonyms: cellular response to insulin-like growth factor
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an insulin-like growth factor stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: gap junction-mediated intercellular transport
description: The movement of substances between cells via gap junctions. A gap junction is a fine cytoplasmic channel, found in animal cells, that connects the cytoplasm of one cell to that of an adjacent cell, allowing ions and other molecules to pass freely between the two cells.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: lipid transport across blood-brain barrier
synonyms: lipid transport across blood brain barrier
description: The directed movement of lipid molecules passing through the blood-brain barrier.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hyaloid vascular plexus regression
description: The developmental process in which the hyaloid vascular plexus is destroyed as a part of its normal progression.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitotic cleavage furrow ingression
description: Advancement of the mitotic cleavage furrow from the outside of the cell inward towards the center of the cell. The cleavage furrow acts as a 'purse string' which draws tight to separate daughter cells during mitotic cytokinesis and partition the cytoplasm between the two daughter cells. The furrow ingresses until a cytoplasmic bridge is formed.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic lung development
description: The process occurring during the embryonic phase whose specific outcome is the progression of the lung over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic liver development
description: The process occurring during the embryonic phase whose specific outcome is the progression of the liver over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: embryonic brain development
description: The process occurring during the embryonic phase whose specific outcome is the progression of the brain over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor signaling pathway
synonyms: CGRP receptor signaling pathway|calcitonin-gene-related peptide receptor signaling pathway|calcitonin-gene-related polypeptide receptor signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by an extracellular calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) combining with a calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor on the surface of the target cell. Calcitonin gene-related peptide receptors may form dimers, trimers or tetramers.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: adrenomedullin receptor signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals initiated by an extracellular adrenomedullin combining with a dimeric adrenomedullin receptor on the surface of the target cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: replication-born double-strand break repair via sister chromatid exchange
description: The repair of a replication-born double-strand DNA break in which the DNA molecule is repaired using the homologous sequence of the sister chromatid which serves as a template to repair the breaks.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to brain-derived neurotrophic factor stimulus
description: A process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a brain-derived neurotrophic factor stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to insulin-like growth factor stimulus
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an insulin-like growth factor stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitotic recombination-dependent replication fork processing
synonyms: homologous recombination dependent replication fork recovery|homologous recombination-dependent replication fork processing|mitotic recombination involved in collapsed replication fork processing|mitotic recombination involved in recovery from replication fork arrest|mitotic recombination involved in recovery from replication fork stalling|mitotic recombination involved in replication fork processing|mitotic recombination involved in replication fork restart|mitotic recombination involved in replication restart
description: Replication fork processing that includes recombination between DNA near the arrested fork and homologous sequences. Proteins involved in homologous recombination are required for replication restart.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: miRNA transport
description: The directed movement of microRNA (miRNA) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, or within a multicellular organism by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: priRNA 3'-end processing
synonyms: priRNA 3\' end processing|primal small RNA 3\'-end processing
description: The process of forming the mature 3' end of a priRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: siRNA 3'-end processing
synonyms: siRNA 3\' end processing|small interfering RNA 3\'-end processing
description: The process of forming the mature 3' end of a siRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to nitrosative stress
synonyms: nitrosative stress-induced apoptosis|nitrosative stress-induced intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway
description: The series of molecular signals in which an intracellular signal is conveyed to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway is induced in response to nitrosative stress; a state often resulting from exposure to high levels of nitric oxide (NO) or the highly reactive oxidant peroxynitrite, which is produced following interaction of NO with superoxide anions.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to ultrasound
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an ultrasonic stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mRNA pseudouridine synthesis
description: The intramolecular conversion of uridine to pseudouridine in an mRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dense core granule maturation
description: Steps required to transform a dense core granule generated at the trans-Golgi network into a fully formed and transmissible dense core granule. Dense core granule maturation proceeds through clathrin-mediated membrane remodeling events and is essential for efficient processing of cargo within dense core granules as well as for removing factors that might otherwise interfere with dense core granule trafficking and exocytosis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dense core granule exocytosis
description: The secretion of molecules (e.g. neuropeptides, insulin-related peptides or neuromodulators such as serotonin and dopamine) contained within a membrane-bounced dense core granule by fusion of the granule with the plasma membrane of a cell in response to increased cytosolic calcium levels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitotic DNA-templated DNA replication
description: A DNA replication process that uses parental DNA as a template for the DNA-dependent DNA polymerases that synthesize the new strands during the mitotic cell cycle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ribonucleotide excision repair
description: The pathway by which a ribonucleotide is removed from DNA and replaced by a deoxyribonucleotide. The ribonucleotide is incised by RNase H2, and further excised by an endonuclease. The resulting 1 nt gap is then repaired by DNA polymerase and DNA ligase.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: pyrimidine nucleotide import into mitochondrion
description: The process in which a pyrimidine nucleotide is transported across the mitochondrial inner membrane, into the mitochondrial matrix.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: bone regeneration
description: The regrowth of bone following its loss or destruction.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: neuron projection maintenance
synonyms: axon homeostasis|axon maintenance|neurite maintenance|neuron process maintenance|neuron protrusion maintenance|neuronal cell projection maintenance
description: The organization process that preserves a neuron projection in a stable functional or structural state. A neuron projection is a prolongation or process extending from a nerve cell, e.g. an axon or dendrite.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: fructose import across plasma membrane
description: The directed movement of fructose substance from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial manganese ion transmembrane transport
description: The process in which a manganese ion is transported across a mitochondrial membrane, into or out of the mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial transmembrane transport
description: The process in which a solute is transported from one side of a membrane to the other into, out of or within a mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial S-adenosyl-L-methionine transmembrane transport
description: The process in which S-adenosyl-L-methionine is transported across a mitochondrial membrane, into or out of the mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial ATP transmembrane transport
description: The process in which ATP is transported across a mitochondrial membrane, into or out of the mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial phosphate ion transmembrane transport
description: The process in which a phosphate ion is transported across a mitochondrial membrane, into or out of the mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial FAD transmembrane transport
description: The process in which FAD is transported across a mitochondrial membrane, into or out of the mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial NAD transmembrane transport
description: The process in which NAD is transported across a mitochondrial membrane, into or out of the mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial alpha-ketoglutarate transmembrane transport
description: The process in which alpha-ketoglutarate is transported across a mitochondrial membrane, into or out of the mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial coenzyme A transmembrane transport
description: The process in which coenzyme A is transported across a mitochondrial membrane, into or out of the mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: UDP-N-acetylglucosamine transmembrane transport
description: The process in which UDP-N-acetylglucosamine is transported across a membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: potassium ion import across plasma membrane
synonyms: potassium import|potassium ion import|potassium ion uptake
description: The directed movement of potassium ions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial L-ornithine transmembrane transport
synonyms: mitochondrial ornithine transmembrane transport|mitochondrial ornithine transport
description: The process in which L-ornithine is transported across a mitochondrial membrane, into or out of the mitochondrion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein K69-linked ufmylation
description: A protein ufmylation process in which a polymer of the ubiquitin-like protein UFM1 is formed by linkages between lysine residues at position 69 of the UFM1 monomers, is added to a protein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cytoplasmic translational initiation in response to stress
description: Modulation of the frequency, rate or extent of cytoplasmic translational initiation as a result of a stimulus indicating the organism is under stress. The stress is usually, but not necessarily, exogenous (e.g. temperature, humidity, ionizing radiation).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial outer membrane fusion
description: The membrane organization process that joins two mitochondrial outer membranes to form a single membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitochondrial inner membrane fusion
description: The membrane organization process that joins two mitochondrial inner membranes to form a single membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to prolactin
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a prolactin stimulus. The anterior pituitary hormone prolactin has a number of roles including being essential for lactation.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to iron ion starvation
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a starvation stimulus, deprivation of iron ion.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to prolactin
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a prolactin stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to melanocyte-stimulating hormone
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a melanocyte-stimulating hormone stimulus. The binding of any one of three melanocyte-stimulating hormones causes dispersal of melanosomes in melanophores of poikilothermic vertebrates.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: DNA double-strand break attachment to nuclear envelope
description: A process in which the DNA double-strand breaks are attached to the inner surface of the nuclear envelope proximal to the spindle pole body, or iMTOCs.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein depalmitoleylation
description: The removal of palmitoleyl group, a 16-carbon monounsaturated fatty acid (C16:1), from a lipoprotein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: nucleolar chromatin organization
synonyms: establishment or maintenance of nucleolar chromatin architecture|nucleolar chromatin organisation
description: Any process that results in the specification, formation or maintenance of the physical structure of nucleolar chromatin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: conditioned place preference
description: The associative learning process by which an animal learns and remembers an association between a neutral, unchanging environment and a putatively rewarding, internal state produced by a xenobiotic or drug.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: presynaptic active zone organization
description: A process that results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a presynaptic active zone.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to manganese-induced endoplasmic reticulum stress
synonyms: manganese-induced ER stress response|response to Mn-induced ER stress|response to manganese-induced ER stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of endoplasmic reticulum stress caused by a manganese stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein sialylation
description: A protein modification process that results in the addition of a sialic acid unit to the end of an oligosaccharide chain in a glycoprotein.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular detoxification
description: Any process carried out at the cellular level that reduces or removes the toxicity of a toxic substance. These may include transport of the toxic substance away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of the toxic substance.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitotic spindle microtubule depolymerization
description: The removal of tubulin heterodimers from one or both ends of a microtubule that is part of the mitotic spindle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: mitotic sister chromatid biorientation
description: The mitotic cell cycle process in which sister chromatids establish stable, end-on attachments to the plus ends of microtubules emanating from opposite spindle poles, oriented such that separation can proceed. This is the final step in metaphase plate congression.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: myofibroblast contraction
description: The actin filament-based process in which cytoplasmic actin filaments slide past one another resulting in contraction of a myofibroblast.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: small intestine smooth muscle contraction
description: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry in the intestine between the stomach and the large intestine.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: clathrin-dependent extracellular exosome endocytosis
description: The clathrin-mediated endocytosis of an extracellular exosome.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to angiotensin
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an angiotensin stimulus. Angiotensin is any of three physiologically active peptides (angiotensin II, III, or IV) processed from angiotensinogen.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: protein localization to cell periphery
description: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, the cell periphery.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to water-immersion restraint stress
synonyms: response to immobilization stress combined with water immersion
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of water immersion while being held immobile.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to dsDNA
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a double-stranded DNA stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: dorsal root ganglion development
description: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a dorsal root ganglion over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to glial cell derived neurotrophic factor
synonyms: cellular response to ATF|cellular response to GDNF|cellular response to astrocyte-derived trophic factor
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a glial cell derived neurotrophic factor stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: endoplasmic reticulum tubular network membrane organization
description: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) tubular network membrane.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: basic amino acid transmembrane transport
description: The directed movement of basic amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: hepatocyte dedifferentiation
description: The process in which a hepatocyte (specialized epithelial cell of the liver) loses the structural or functional features that characterize it in the mature organism, or some other relatively stable phase of the organism's life history. Under certain conditions, these cells can revert back to the features of the stem cells that were their ancestors.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to leukemia inhibitory factor
synonyms: cellular response to CDF|cellular response to cholinergic differentiation factor
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a leukemia inhibitory factor stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to odorant
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an odorant stimulus. An odorant is any substance capable of stimulating the sense of smell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to endothelin
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an endothelin stimulus. Endothelin is any of three secretory vasoconstrictive peptides (endothelin-1, -2, -3).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: adaptive thermogenesis
description: The regulated production of heat in response to short term environmental changes, such as stress, diet or reduced temperature.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to lectin
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a lectin stimulus. A lectin is a carbohydrate-binding protein, highly specific for binding sugar moieties.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to endothelin
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an endothelin stimulus. Endothelin is any of three secretory vasoconstrictive peptides (endothelin-1, -2, -3).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular response to chemokine
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a chemokine stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: vascular associated smooth muscle cell proliferation
synonyms: VSMC proliferation|vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation
description: The multiplication or reproduction of vascular smooth muscle cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population. A vascular smooth muscle cell is a non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cell found lining the blood vessels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: cellular detoxification of copper ion
description: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of copper ions in a cell. These include transport of copper cations away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to hypobaric hypoxia
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating lowered oxygen tension combined with low atmospheric pressure. Hypoxia is defined as a decline in O2 levels below normoxic levels of 20.8 - 20.95% and hypobaric is defined as atmospheric pressure below 0.74 atm (greater than 2,500 m above sea level).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to psychosocial stress
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of exposure to aversive or demanding psychological and social conditions that tax or exceed the behavioral resources of the organism.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: double-strand break repair involved in meiotic recombination
description: The repair of double-strand breaks in DNA via homologous and nonhomologous mechanisms to reform a continuous DNA helix that contributes to reciprocal meiotic recombination.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: short-term synaptic potentiation
description: The process by which synaptic transmission, induced by the arrival of a spike (action potential) at a synapse, acts to increase the amount of neurotransmitter released in response to the arrival of subsequent spikes. This effect is seen when a train of closely space spikes arrives at a synapse with a low initial release probability. It occurs in a timeframe of tens to hundreds of milliseconds.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: calcium ion regulated lysosome exocytosis
description: The process of secretion by a cell that results in the release of intracellular molecules contained within a lysosome by fusion of the vesicle with the plasma membrane of a cell, induced by a rise in cytosolic calcium-ion levels.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: response to amino acid starvation
description: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of deprivation of amino acids.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: metaphase/anaphase transition of meiosis I
synonyms: first meiotic metaphase/anaphase transition|meiosis I metaphase/anaphase transition
description: The cell cycle process in which a cell progresses from metaphase to anaphase as part of meiosis I.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: intramanchette transport
description: The movement of vesicles and protein complexes carried out by molecular motors, kinesins and dynein, along the microtubule tracks within the manchette and by myosin along actin filaments.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: eosinophil homeostasis
synonyms: eosinocyte homeostasis|eosinophilic granulocyte homeostasis|eosinophilic leucocyte homeostasis|eosinophilic leukocyte homeostasis
description: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of eosinophils such that the total number of eosinophils within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: basophil homeostasis
description: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of basophils such that the total number of basophils within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: xenobiotic detoxification by transmembrane export across the plasma membrane
description: A process that reduces or removes the toxicity of a xenobiotic by exporting it outside the cell.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: xenobiotic transport across blood-brain barrier
description: The directed movement of a xenobiotic through the blood-brain barrier.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: establishment of blood-retinal barrier
synonyms: establishment of BRB|establishment of blood-retina barrier
description: Establishment of the barrier between the blood and the retina. The blood-retinal barrier is located at two levels, forming an outer barrier in the retinal pigment epithelium and an inner barrier in the endothelial membrane of the retinal vessels. Both these membranes have tight junctions of the 'nonleaky' type.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: ATP generation from poly-ADP-D-ribose
description: The process of generating ATP in the nucleus from poly-ADP-D-ribose. Nuclear ATP generation is required for extensive chromatin remodeling events that are energy-consuming.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of translational initiation by tRNA modification
description: A process in which translation initiation is regulated by post-translation modifications of a tRNA molecule.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: DNA recombinase disassembly
description: The disaggregation of a DNA recombinase complex into its constituent strand exchange proteins (recombinases).

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of DNA damage checkpoint
synonyms: regulation of DNA damage response|signal transduction resulting in cell cycle arrest
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a DNA damage checkpoint.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of DNA damage checkpoint
synonyms: negative regulation of DNA damage response|signal transduction resulting in cell cycle arrest
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of a DNA damage checkpoint.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of DNA damage checkpoint
synonyms: positive regulation of DNA damage response|signal transduction resulting in cell cycle arrest
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of a DNA damage checkpoint.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of metanephric S-shaped body morphogenesis
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of metanephric S-shaped body morphogenesis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of metanephric comma-shaped body morphogenesis
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of metanephric comma-shaped body morphogenesis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of protein localization to cell surface
synonyms: regulation of protein localisation at cell surface|regulation of protein localization at cell surface
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of protein localization to the cell surface.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of protein localization to cell surface
synonyms: negative regulation of protein localisation at cell surface|negative regulation of protein localization at cell surface
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of protein localization to the cell surface.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of protein localization to cell surface
synonyms: positive regulation of protein localisation at cell surface|positive regulation of protein localization at cell surface
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of protein localization to the cell surface.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of determination of dorsal identity
synonyms: negative regulation of determination of adaxial identity
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of determination of dorsal identity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of determination of dorsal identity
synonyms: positive regulation of determination of adaxial identity
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of determination of dorsal identity.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of male gonad development
synonyms: negative regulation of testicular development|negative regulation of testis development
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of male gonad development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of male gonad development
synonyms: positive regulation of testicular development|positive regulation of testis development
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of male gonad development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of multicellular organismal development
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of multicellular organismal development.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of animal organ morphogenesis
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of animal organ morphogenesis.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of stem cell division
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of stem cell division.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of stem cell population maintenance
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of stem cell population maintenance.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of double-strand break repair via homologous recombination
synonyms: negative regulation of HDR|negative regulation of HRR|negative regulation of Rad51-dependent recombinational repair|negative regulation of Rhp51-dependent recombinational repair|negative regulation of homologous recombinational repair|negative regulation of homology-directed repair
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of double-strand break repair via homologous recombination.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of cardiac cell fate specification
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac cell fate specification.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle
description: Any signaling pathway that modulates the activity of a cell cycle cyclin-dependent protein kinase to modulate the switch from G1 phase to S phase of the mitotic cell cycle.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of cell-cell adhesion mediated by cadherin
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cell-cell adhesion mediated by cadherin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of cell-cell adhesion mediated by cadherin
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cell-cell adhesion mediated by cadherin.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: regulation of non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway
synonyms: regulation of beta-catenin-independent Wnt receptor signaling pathway|regulation of non-canonical Wnt receptor signaling pathway|regulation of non-canonical Wnt receptor signalling pathway|regulation of non-canonical Wnt-activated signaling pathway
description: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: negative regulation of non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway
synonyms: negative regulation of beta-catenin-independent Wnt receptor signaling pathway|negative regulation of non-canonical Wnt receptor signaling pathway|negative regulation of non-canonical Wnt receptor signalling pathway|negative regulation of non-canonical Wnt-activated signaling pathway
description: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway.

label: BiologicalProcess
name: positive regulation of non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway
synonyms: positive regulation of beta-catenin-independent Wnt receptor signaling pathway|positive regulation of non-canonical Wnt receptor signaling pathway|positive regulation of non-canonical Wnt receptor signalling pathway|positive regulation of non-canonical Wnt-activated signaling pathway
description: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of non-canonical Wnt-activated signaling pathway.

description: Hemorrhage affecting the gingiva.

name: Epistaxis
synonyms: Bloody nose|Frequent nosebleeds|Nasal haemorrhage|Nasal hemorrhage|Nose bleed|Nose bleeding|Nosebleed
description: Epistaxis, or nosebleed, refers to a hemorrhage localized in the nose.

label: Phenotype
name: Hematuria
synonyms: Blood in urine|High urine occult blood
description: The presence of blood in the urine. Hematuria may be gross hematuria (visible to the naked eye) or microscopic hematuria (detected by dipstick or microscopic examination of the urine).

label: Phenotype
name: Petechiae
description: Petechiae are pinpoint-sized reddish/purple spots, resembling a rash, that appear just under the skin or a mucous membrane when capillaries have ruptured and some superficial bleeding into the skin has happened. This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to developing petechiae.

label: Phenotype
name: Bruising susceptibility
description: An ecchymosis (bruise) refers to the skin discoloration caused by the escape of blood into the tissues from ruptured blood vessels. This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to bruising. The corresponding phenotypic abnormality is generally elicited on medical history as a report of frequent ecchymoses or bruising without adequate trauma.

label: Phenotype
name: Purpura
synonyms: Blood spots|Red or purple spots on the skin
description: Purpura (from Latin: purpura, meaning purple) is the appearance of red or purple discolorations on the skin that do not blanch on applying pressure. They are caused by bleeding underneath the skin. This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to developing purpura. Purpura are larger than petechiae.

name: Muscle weakness
description: Reduced strength of muscles.

label: Phenotype
name: Hepatosplenomegaly
description: Simultaneous enlargement of the liver and spleen.

label: Phenotype
name: Splenomegaly
description: Abnormal increased size of the spleen.

label: Phenotype
name: Weight loss
description: Reduction of total body weight.

description: Abnormal decrease of absolute number of neutrophils in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

label: Phenotype

label: Phenotype
name: Decreased total leukocyte count

description: An abnormal decreased number of leukocytes in the blood.

label: Phenotype

label: Phenotype
name: Thrombocytosis

description: A chronic lymphocytic/lymphatic/lymphoblastic leukemia (CLL) is a neoplastic disease characterized by proliferation and accumulation (blood, marrow and lymphoid organs) of morphologically mature but immunologically dysfunctional lymphocytes. description: A type of of pulmonary hemorrhage that originates from the pulmonary microcirculation, including the alveolar capillaries, arterioles, and venules. The diagnosis is confirmed by the observation of the accumulation of red blood cells, fibrin, or hemosiderin-laden macrophage in the alveolar space on pathologic biopsy. Hemosiderin, a product of hemoglobin degradation, appears at least 48-72 hours after bleeding and is helpful in distinguishing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage from surgical trauma. Mild interstitial thickening, organizing pneumonia, or diffuse alveolar damage can also be seen.

description: A reduction in the number of red blood cells, the amount of hemoglobin, and/or the volume of packed red blood cells. Clinically, anemia represents a reduction in the oxygen-transporting capacity of a designated volume of blood, resulting from an imbalance between blood loss (through hemorrhage or hemolysis) and blood production. Signs and symptoms of anemia may include pallor of the skin and mucous membranes, shortness of breath, palpitations of the heart, soft systolic murmurs, lethargy, and fatigability.

Some patients can also develop autoimmune complications such as autoimmune hemolytic anemia or immune thrombocytopenia. Morphologically, follicular lymphomas are classified as Grade 1, Grade 2, and Grade 3, depending on the percentage of the large lymphocytes present. The vast majority of cases (70-95%) express the BCL-2 rearrangement [t(14;18)]. Histological grade correlates with prognosis. Grades 1 and 2 follicular lymphomas are indolent and grade 3 is more aggressive (adapted from WHO, 2001).

Specific features of AML-M5 include hyperleukocytosis, propensity for extramedullary infiltrates, coagulation abnormalities including disseminated intravascular coagulation and neurological disorders. Morphologically, a blast population with a myelomonocytic stage of differentiation is observed.

description: Acute myeloid leukemia with inv(3)(q21;q26.2) or t(3;3)(q21;q26.2) is a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia with recurrent genetic abnormalities characterized by clonal proliferation of myeloid blasts in the bone marrow, blood and, rarely, other tissues. Patients typically present with leukocytosis, anemia, variable platelet counts and a variety of nonspecific symptoms related to ineffective hematopoesis (fatigue, bleeding, bruising, recurrent infections, bone pain) and/or extramedullary site involvement (gingivitis, splenomegaly). High resistance to conventional chemotherapy is reported.

description: Megakaryoblastic acute myeloid leukemia with t(1;22)(p13;q13) is a rare subtype of acute myeloid leukemia with recurrent cytogenetic abnormalities characterized by clonal proliferation of myeloid blasts with predominantly megakaryoblastic differentiation in the bone marrow and blood, often with extensive infiltration of the abdominal organs. It occurs typically in infants and usually presents with hepatosplenomegaly, anemia, thrombocytopenia and nonspecific symptoms related to ineffective hematopoesis (fatigue, bleeding and bruising, recurrent infections). Myelofibrosis and fibrosis of other infiltrated organs is also characteristic of this disease.

description: Acute myeloid leukemia with NPM1 somatic mutations is a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia with recurrent genetic abnormalities characterized by clonal proliferation of myeloid blasts harboring mutations of the NPM1 gene in the bone marrow, blood and other tissues. It is associated with multilineage dysplasia, involving the myeloid, monocytic, erythroid, and megakaryocytic cell lineages. Patients usually present with leukocytosis, thrombocytosis and nonspecific symptoms related to ineffective hematopoesis (fatigue, bleeding and bruising, recurrent infections, bone pain), with frequent extramedullary involvement typically presenting as gingival hyperplasia and lymphadenopathy.
